News.title: Miracle in New York City as pregnant woman pulled from rubble of collapsed Brooklyn building
News.content:
Miracle in New York City as pregnant woman pulled from rubble of collapsed Brooklyn building

A man desperately tried to push through emergency responders to get to his wife. "I'm very happy, I'm very happy," he said after the woman was rescued.

View 3 Images An emergency response worker consoles a man after his pregnant wife was rescued from the rubble at the scene of the partial building collapse (Image: Getty)

A pregnant woman has been rescued after a building collapsed in a New York City borough, after her horrified husband desperately pleaded with emergency crews to search for her. The horror incident has left at least one person dead and others injured.

‌



‌



Emergency responders swarmed the scene of the three-storey building to help the victims at around 4pm on Wednesday, November 11. Two and a half hours after the collapse, a woman, said to be six months pregnant, was pulled from the rubble.

‌



The footage showed her being pushed on a stretcher as the lights of ambulances flashed franticly, Emergency personnel tried to clear the way for rescuers transporting the woman, with one yelling, "Back up! Back up!"

‌



A man who believed the person was his six-month-pregnant wife told WABC: "I'm very happy, I'm very happy."

View 3 Images The man was consoled at the scene (Image: Getty)

Earlier on, the man had desperately tried to push through emergency responders to get to his wife. "She's inside the building. She's pregnant," he told reporters.

‌



A complex technical rescue operation is underway and news helicopter footage has captured dozens of firefighters scouring the debris. A group was focused on one area and appeared to use a saw to cut through the wreckage.

The aerial videos showed firefighters digging at least one person out of the rubble and removing them on a stretcher.

‌



View 3 Images First responders tend to a collapsed building in Brooklyn in New York (Image: Getty)

"This is a delicate and high-risk technical rescue operation," an FDNY spokesperson confirmed from the location.

‌



Early reports and footage from the scene suggest the affected building was under construction, leaving upper-level rooms and interior framework exposed down to the lower floors.

The building that collapsed had been perched at the edge of a lot where another one-story building had been torn down for a construction project. The site was being excavated, and the building that fell down filled the construction pit with bricks and wood.

Article continues below

Another building that shared a wall with the collapsed structure remained standing, but its wall was shorn off, exposing the rooms inside, including a bedroom and closets filled with clothing.

News.title: King Charles reflects on favourite music performances during radio show appearance with Sir Elton John
News.content:
King Charles reflects on favourite music performances during radio show appearance with Sir Elton John

The monarch is set to feature on the rockstar’s radio programme, as they share some of their favourite artists who have been bolstered by the King’s Trust

The King & Sir Elton John have recorded an hour-long special episode of Apple Radio show Rocket Hour

King Charles is set to appear on Sir Elton John’s radio programme, with the pair discussing some of their favourite musicians who have been supported by the King’s Trust. The monarch sat down with the rockstar in secret at the Apple Music Studios in Battersea Power Station in south London last month for the musical collaboration.

‌



‌



Elton hosts a regular radio programme on the streaming platform, with Charles’ special episode filmed to highlight the key role of music in the work of the monarch’s charity The King’s Trust, which is celebrating its 50th year.

‌



The King described it as “an opportunity too good to resist”, while Sir Elton admitted afterwards: “I learnt a lot from speaking to His Majesty.”

‌



View 3 Images Charles has appeared on Sir Elton's radio programme

Princess Kate beams as she plays with baby during hospital visit READ MORE :

Charles also thanked Sir Elton for adding “a little Rocket Power to the proceedings”, and praised the popstar for becoming "such a national treasure after all these years". Sir Elton quipped "I'll be on the Antiques Roadshow", with the King laughing and retorting "Join the club".

The pair shared memories of their favourite performances by some of music’s biggest stars in support of the trust over the last five decades – from Wembley Arena rock galas of the 1980s through to pop concerts in Hyde Park and sold-out charity shows at the Royal Albert Hall.

‌



The episode also highlighted some of those who received help from the trust in their early days, including Muse, who were given a grant from the-then Prince’s Trust to purchase PA equipment when they were starting out as a band under the name Rocket Baby Dolls.

View 3 Images The King and Elton spoke about their favourite music performances (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Sir Elton told the King: “I never knew that some of these musicians were involved in the trust. It’s great news to me… and it reinforces for me all the great work that you’ve done all these 50 years, because I had no idea. So bravo.”

The King said it was “wonderful” to see the difference the trust’s programmes can make, adding: “Well really, what I was trying to do was invest in the future, but particularly investing in talent.”

‌



Sir Elton said: “That’s the greatest thing you can do. Young people are our future, and you’re doing a wonderful job.” Charles and Sir Elton took part in the episode – the first to be recorded in the new Apple Radio studios – in October when they both visited Battersea Power Station for the launch of the Apple x King’s Trust Creative Labs which aim to help young people explore potential careers in creative industries.

View 3 Images Elton has long been a supporter of the King's Trust (Image: PA)

‌



In a trailer, the King and Sir Elton are shown chuckling together as they chat during the recording. Sir Elton said in a voiceover: “Hi I’m Elton John. Welcome to my Rocket Hour. This week, my special guest, and I really mean special guest. I’m so excited to hear what he’s got to say about music, about The King’s Trust and memories that we both share.”

In the episode, the King said: “Music has always been at the heart of The Prince’s, and now The King’s Trust. So when I was asked whether I would like to showcase a selection of music from among the many talented performers who have so generously supported us over the years, together with some of the newer artists the trust has helped to launch, it was an opportunity too good to resist.”

‌



Buckingham Palace described the episode as “a show that is something of shared musical journey” and said the King and Sir Elton’s playlist “spans a range of decades and genres, from some meaningful personal favourites and golden oldies, to this year’s new releases”.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



“From Tina Turner and Rod Stewart to Calvin Harris and this year’s Mercury Prize winner Raye, we hope there is something there for everyone, whatever their age or musical taste,” the spokesperson said.

Sir Elton has long been a supporter of The King’s Trust, and performed at some of its rock galas at Wembley in the 1980s and donated a pair of his rose-tinted spectacles to raise money as part of its 50th anniversary auction

Article continues below

The full episode of Elton John’s Rocket Hour will premiere at 9am on Saturday - the King’s 78th birthday - on Apple Music 1.

News.title: Meghan Markle's brother breaks silence on 'monster' dad Thomas Markle Snr's arrest
News.content:
Meghan Markle's brother breaks silence on 'monster' dad Thomas Markle Snr's arrest

The father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, left his son 'shocked' as he appeared scowling in his prison mugshot, after being charged with possessing child sexual abuse material

View 4 Images Thomas Markle Snr, who is back in custody for allegedly cutting off his electronic tag just days after his arrest for possessing child sex abuse material (Image: Pinellas County Sheriff's Office/Press Association)

Thomas Markle's son, and the half-brother of Meghan Markle, has broken his silence after his father's arrest on suspicion of possessing child sexual abuse material, including images allegedly showing him with naked young girls.

Markle's son was appalled by his father's first mugshot from a prison facility where he now languishes following him allegedly cutting off his electronic monitoring tag - just days after being released on bail.

The son declared "h e looks like Jack Nicholson in The Shining" as the mugshot of the Duchess of Sussex's father emerged, showing him scowling down the camera in a bright orange prison uniform.

Thomas Markle Jnr, 60, said he believed his “monster” of a father deliberately tore off the device so he could get free medical care behind bars, according to reports from The Sun.

Meghan’s estranged 82-year-old dad was taken back into custody in the US after allegedly breaching the conditions of his pre-trial release, accused of cutting off the electronic ankle gadget monitoring his movements while under house arrest.

He has now been charged with possessing child sexual abuse material.

View 4 Images Meghan Markle and her father, Thomas Markle Snr

His jail photo was released by the Pinellas County sheriff’s office following his re-arrest on Tuesday night, just days after he was charged.

Thomas Jnr recalled the 1980 horror film famous for its terrifying 'Here's Johnny' line, telling The Sun: “I couldn’t believe that mugshot — my dad looks just as angry and crazy as Jack Nicholson in The Shining.”

According to first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli, Markle Snr appeared in federal court in Tampa, Florida, after authorities learned he had cut off the tag at 1.45am (6.45am UK time), reports continue.

View 4 Images Jack Nicholson walking through the hotel maze in the film 'The Shining' (Image: Getty Images)

US magistrate judge Lindsay Saxe Griffin ordered Markle to stay in custody until the end of his trial, having “violated the conditions of his pretrial release”. She said he should be detained separately, as far as possible, from the general prison population.

The judge added his dementia care home stay had “become untenable” and that he had surrendered his US passport and Philippines visa.

The pair moved to the the Philippines in January last year but Markle Snr returned to the States for treatment after a blood clot forced medics to amputate his left leg.

View 4 Images Thomas Markle Jr (Image: Getty Images)

Thomas Jnr said yesterday: “I’m not surprised he’s being accused of removing the tag because he probably realised there’s no one to take care of him if he stayed at home.

‌



“My sister Samantha was his carer but is now in a wheelchair and he wouldn’t be able to cope on his own."

Markle Snr was arrested by FBI agents after they seized a haul of material from two Los Angeles storage units he rented for nearly two decades.

‌



He is charged with one count of possession of child pornography and is subject to home detention and electronic tagging following his release on bail after his court appearance on Friday.

He came under investigation after he was reported to police in the Philippines and the FBI last month by his son, Thomas Markle Jr, who allegedly found illegal images in his father’s belongings in Cebu City.

Meghan said she was “deeply distressed” at the allegations surrounding her father, from whom she has been estranged since the run-up to her 2018 wedding.

News.title: Dad, 25, charged with attempted murder after son buried alive in South Carolina
News.content:
Dad, 25, charged with attempted murder after son buried alive in South Carolina

WARNING: DISTRESSING CONTENT Koah Sharp is expected to make a "full recovery" after being burried alive in a dog crate - his dad Michael Comer now faces attempted murder and other charges

View 4 Images Michael Comer (right) was arrested while hiding in a building (Image: Amber Hammond via AP)

A 25-year-old man has been charged with attempted murder in South Carolina after his son survived being buried alive in a dog crate for about 24 hours.

The 11-month old, Koah Sharp, was reported missing in Lexington County, just west of Columbia on Monday. After a full day of searching Tuesday, authorities found freshly disturbed soil in the woods not far from the home of the boy's grandfather - and heard cries from below ground, the sheriff said.

Koah was soon freed and "clinging to life," the sheriff told reporters. "He was screaming at the top of his lungs, which is a good thing in the baby world, I would guess," Koon said. He was released from a hospital Tuesday night following the rescue and is expected to make a "full recovery," Sheriff Jay Koon said.

The boy's 25-year-old father, Michael Comer, was arrested while hiding in a building in Batesburg-Leesville. He faces attempted murder and other charges. A court hearing was planned for Thursday.

View 4 Images The boy's 25-year-old father, Michael Comer

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

The boy survived because of cool temperatures and an air pocket created by a towel that was wrapped around the crate below ground, said Koon.

"We're better now that we know that Koah is safe," his great-aunt, Amber Hammond, told The Associated Press.

She was watching as he was freed from the crate. Authorities said Koah had been in the care of Comer's mother. She had to run an errand and left the boy in Comer's care while another caregiver was on the way.

"By the time the caregiver got there, Michael was gone, and Koah was gone with him," the sheriff said. Surveillance video from several businesses in the area showed Comer without the baby on Monday afternoon, Koon said.

View 4 Images Amber Hammond, the great aunt of 11-month-old Koah Sharp (Image: AP Photo/Erik Verduzco)

Koah's parents "have had some situations" regarding domestic violence charges, the sheriff said. "Children," he said, "sometimes get caught in the middle."

Hammond said her nephew had talked about taking the baby to New York because "he didn't want to be in the same state as the mom." When Koah vanished, she and others assumed that Comer had given the boy to someone.

"We had no idea something like this would happen at all," Hammond said.

View 4 Images Koah Sharp with his dad

Comer was sentenced to probation in October after pleading guilty to domestic violence and aggravated breach-of-peace charges related to an arrest in July, Lexington County online court records show. Prosecutors dropped a gun charge as part of the plea deal. He also got credit for spending more than two months in jail.

At nearly a year old, Koah has been trying to stand on his own, said Hammond, who cared for him last weekend. And he already has some TV favorites.

"I'd go to feed him, and it had Mickey Mouse on," Hammond said. "You can't feed him and have Mickey Mouse on at the same time."

News.title: M25 traffic chaos after pile-up sparks severe delays near Junction 11
News.content:
There were severe delays on the M25 in Surrey after a multi-vehicle crash between junction 11 (Chertsey) and junction 12 (Thorpe)

There were severe delays on the M25 in Surrey after a crash involving three vans and a lorry.

The collision, which left one person injured, happened at around 6.55am on Wednesday on the clockwise carriageway between junction 11 (Chertsey) and junction 12 (Thorpe).

South East Coast Ambulance Service said the man was treated at the scene for a leg injury before being taken to St George's Hospital in London for further treatment.

Three of the carriageway's four lanes were closed after the crash, causing delays of more than 90 minutes. All lanes reopened about two and a half hours later, but delays continued until noon.

News.title: Apple worker accused of murdering girl, 2, in '100mph' fireball car crash
News.content:
Apple worker accused of murdering girl, 2, in '100mph' fireball car crash

Eric Chen Su, 37, has been charged with the murder of a two-year-old girl after he allegedly drove around three times over the speed limit before slamming into the youngster

View 3 Images Two-year-old Riley Kathryn Howard was killed in the crash (Image: Facebook)

A worker at Apple's headquarters in California is accused of murdering a two-year-old girl after allegedly ploughing into a car that was carrying the youngster while he was travelling at 100mph.

‌



‌



Eric Chen Su was initially arrested on suspicion of gross vehicular manslaughter but his charges were upgraded to murder on Tuesday.

‌



The high-speed collision unfolded at an intersection in Cupertino near Apple Park on Friday afternoon.

‌



Emergency services raced to the scene during the lunchtime rush hour and found a severely injured woman and child inside a Chevy, which burst into flames from the impact, according to the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office.

Tragically, the child, later named as Riley Kathryn Howard, died despite the best efforts of emergency responders.

View 3 Images The collision caused the Chevy to burst into flames (Image: ABC7 News Bay Area)

‌



Human torso found stuffed inside sofa as murder investigation launched in Sydney READ MORE :

Su was alone in a Toyota Camry and suffered minor injuries. The 38-year-old was treated at a hospital before being discharged and arrested.

"When the two cars collided, the Chevy Trax burst into flames," sheriff's office spokesperson Brooks Jarosz told reporters.

‌



The speedometer in Su's vehicle appeared to be frozen at 100mph, roughly three times the speed limit, Santa Clara County Deputy District Attorney Rob Baker told local ABC affiliate KGO.

Prosecutors allege Su made no attempt to slow down before slamming into the vehicle carrying Riley. "'Unquestionably, murder was the appropriate charge," Baker said.

‌



The toddler was travelling with her babysitter when the car caught fire. Witnesses told KGO that passers-by rushed to pull both occupants from the burning wreckage.

View 3 Images Riley, pictured bottom right with her family (Image: Support Now)

‌



Su appeared in court on Tuesday in a wheelchair, although he had no other injuries, Baker said. He remains in custody and has not yet entered a plea.

It is unclear what role Su held at Apple. The Mirror has contacted the company for comment.

‌



An investigation into the crash is ongoing. Sheriffs Captain Neil Valenzuela said: "This is a heartbreaking tragedy for everyone affected. Our thoughts are with the child's family and loved ones as they navigate an unimaginable loss."

A fundraiser has been launched by the San Jose community to raise funds for Riley's family following her death.

Article continues below

The Santa Clara County Firefighters said the youngster's mom, Alaina, was a part of their 'County Fire family.'

Linking to the fundraiser, the firefighters wrote: "No family should ever have to endure a loss like this. Our members have spent their careers showing up for this community in its hardest moments. Now we ask the community to show up for one of our own."

News.title: Donald Trump Jr defends Russell Brand and points to rapist ‘finding God’
News.content:
Donald Trump Jr defends Russell Brand and points to rapist ‘finding God’

Russell Brand was found guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others following a trial at Southwark Crown Court in London

Russell Brand Jailed for 10 Years, 6 Months

Donald Trump's son has defended Russell Brand, suggesting he was convicted of rape due to his recent conversion to Christianity.

Donald Trump Jr., known as Don Jr., is the latest celebrity to express his support for the disgraced comedian, who has been sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison after he was found guilty of one rape and three sexual assaults following a trial at Southwark Crown Court in London. The president's son suggested the prosecution was politically motivated .

In a video posted on Rumble on Tuesday, he said: "He finds God, I guess, changes his ways, sees some aspects of conservative life, and talks about them, and now he's going to spend 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape when no one had a problem with it in the prior 27 years."

View 2 Images Donald Trump Jr (Image: Donald Trump Jr/Rumble)

Russell Brand jokes about previous arrest to Jonathan Ross in unearthed clip READ MORE :

Despite the Crown Prosecution Service already reviewing two more rape allegations against Brand, Don Jr. questioned the timeline of the allegations presented during the trial.

The offences Brand was convicted for took place between 2004 and 2009. However, Brand was acquitted of other allegations of rape and sexual assault, which dated back to 1999.

Don Jr., 48, added: "He was convicted, by the way, with no forensic evidence, no DNA, no police report from the time now decades old, on allegations dating back to 1999. So, when he was like married to Katy Perry, he's one of the most famous actors in the world, no one seemed to have a problem. No one seemed to think he was a rapist then."

View 2 Images Brand arriving at Southwark Crown Court in October (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The businessman went on to criticise the length of Brand's prison term, questioning the British justice system. He said: "This raises what I think are some pretty obvious questions about why his sentence was more severe than, I don't know, sentences handed to Muslim grooming gangs across the UK.

"Every week we did a story about some kid getting raped in a tank by — oh, they just let him off with a slap on the wrist. We told him not to do it again. Russell gets to spend 10 and a half years in prison."

Sentencing Brand, Mr Justice Bennathan slammed the comedian’s “staggering arrogance” and said he had “become a sexual predator” during his rise to fame.

The judge said Brand harboured a “casual arrogant disregard to any woman’s right to say no to you”, while his fame meant he believed “you could act when you liked and how you liked”. Brand is expected to serve two-thirds of his prison sentence before being released on licence.

High-profile figures who expressed their support for Brand include Elon Musk, who called the comedian's punishment "unjust". Megyn Kelly also described the conviction as a "political witch hunt" and said the jail term is "insane".

Trump has not yet commented on Brand's conviction. However, a 2014 tweet made by the president has resurfaced, with Trump writing at the time: "@katyperry Katy, what the hell were you thinking when you married loser Russell Brand. There is a guy who has got nothing going, a waste!"

News.title: UK weather maps turn purple as 608-mile wall of snow and rain to engulf nation
News.content:
UK weather maps turn purple as 608-mile wall of snow and rain to engulf nation

Forecasters with Metdesk, which produces WXCharts, show a band of snow and rain to move across the UK amid a cold snap, during which temperatures could dip to -7C

View 3 Images Weather maps show areas are to experiencing snow or heavy rainfall (Image: WXCharts)

These striking weather maps show the UK looks set to be blanketed by a massive wall of snow and rain.

‌



‌



The country is poised to endure turbulent weather following a huge plunge in temperatures. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) issues its first cold-health alert of the winter.

‌



This is because temperatures could plunge to as low as -7C in some places overnight, a contrast from the 14C recorded on Tuesday in Camborne, Cornwall. Now, weather maps, produced by experts at WXCharts indicate that locations from Fort William in Scotland down to Cornwall in England are anticipated to face icy conditions.

‌



Communities are to brace for the shivering vortex from Tuesday November 17. Snow is expected across parts of northern and western Scotland, including Fort William, Glasgow and Inverness, and torrential rainfall is likely to batter the rest of the UK.

Martin Lewis explains how to use your curtains to keep heat in your home this winter READ MORE :

View 3 Images Parts of the UK will be battered by heavy snow next week, the maps show. (Image: WXCharts)

Forecasters say temperatures are projected to plummet to -7C in the vicinity of Fort William. Across other parts of Scotland, including Glasgow, Inverness and Edinburgh, temperatures are anticipated to sit between -3C and -5C, the maps indicate.

‌



This comes after the UKHSA's yellow cold health alert for the Northwest of England and West Midlands from 9am on Thursday to midday on Saturday, reports the Express. The agency cautioned that low temperatures can place increased pressure on health and care services and urged people to check on loved ones and neighbours.

Temperatures are projected to drop significantly below the seasonal average by Thursday and Friday, bringing widespread frost to many regions of the country.

‌



View 3 Images Snowy scenes like this - earlier this year in Greater Manchester - are possible (Image: PA)

In some sheltered rural spots particularly vulnerable to cold weather, the mercury could tumble to -6C or -7C. Overnight frost is anticipated across numerous areas, especially throughout rural parts of Britain, though these colder spells are predicted to become mostly confined to southern regions as the weekend unfolds.

‌



The Met Office's long-range forecast between November 16 and 25 reads: "Following the tail end of the colder, more settled conditions seen over the weekend, a marked transition to more changeable conditions is expected at the start of the period.

"This will allow areas of low pressure to move in from the Atlantic and bring bands of rain and periods of windy weather. There will be some brighter, showery spells in-between however, particularly in the north.

Article continues below

"Overall, this period is likely to be wetter than average for the majority of the country. And whilst colder conditions will be possible at times, it will often be mild, with temperatures near or a little above average for the time of year."

News.title: Some under-25s should get less benefits, Milburn review to say
News.content:
Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review.

Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits, the Times reported, external.

Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet".

He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.

His report is expected to recommend that under-25s are no longer able to claim the health element of universal credit or personal independence payment (Pip).

Instead, they would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit.

Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions.

But many claimants would receive less under the plans, which the government is set to take forward into legislation in the new year.

Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers.

Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate.

Speaking to the Times about his report, Milburn said: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system.

News.title: Author says there were 'real concerns' about David Walliams within publishing industry
News.content:
Earlier on Wednesday, media minister Ian Murray said there is a "cultural problem" in the industry that needs to be "stamped out".

Giving evidence to the Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee, Murray said he was "deeply saddened and also angry" to see the prevalence of abuse by men in the media industry.

Meanwhile, Minister for Women and Equalities Bridget Phillipson paid tribute to the "bravery" of victims who have shared their experiences in recent days.

Speaking in the Commons, she said: "Women and girls should never have to shrink our lives or ambitions because of outdated, misogynistic attitudes, and the appalling testimonies we have heard in recent days underline how much further we have to go."

Phillipson later said the government would "go further" on restricting the use of non-disclosure agreements, telling Sky News: "We cannot have a system where rich and powerful individuals, rich and powerful men, are able to silence women, buy their silence and stop things coming to light."

She said that she believed injunctions were being misused, and that her colleagues at the Ministry of Justice were looking at how the government can intervene to ensure this did not happen.

Comedian and podcaster Deborah Frances-White told BBC Radio 4's The World at One that young women are "definitely" still being exploited in the comedy industry.

She told the programme that perpetrators understand consent but they just enjoy the power that comes with ignoring it, adding: "The thrill is in the contravention of consent."

Asked whether she recognised the picture Russell Brand's conviction and allegations against Walliams had painted of the comedy industry, she said: "Yes, entirely."

She described an industry where she was asked to meet male producers in darkly lit rooms "walking a tightrope", having to make them feel attractive and avoid being assaulted as they influenced future employment opportunities.

She said these events are "definitely still going on" and that she is in a WhatsApp group with female comedians who share their experiences with each other.

News.title: Hegseth and advisers reprimanded by guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
News.content:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and a group he was with were reprimanded by a sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery on Wednesday. The incident followed a wreath-laying ceremony marking Veterans Day.

Hegseth had joined the group for a photo and someone laughed, prompting the US Army sentinel guarding the tomb to shout. "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times", the sentinel said.

According to the BBC's US partner, CBS News, the people in the photo before the reprimand also included Hegseth's advisers Patrick Weaver and Tami Radabaugh, Hegseth's chief of staff Ricky Buria and Hegseth's wife Jennifer Hegseth.

News.title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?
News.content:
Cold and flu drugs fall into three broad camps: household names such as Lemsip and Sudafed; supermarket own-label alternatives; and single-ingredient medicines containing paracetamol or ibuprofen.

The difference in price can be striking.

A packet of 16 Lemsip All-In-One Max Strength tablets retails at Â£7.30, more than 20 times the Â£0.35 cost of paracetamol pills in some supermarkets.

Both contain 500mg of paracetamol, which doesn't treat the underlying infection but does relieve pain and can bring down a fever.

The Lemsip version, along with many of its competitors, also contains the decongestant phenylephrine.

It's meant to constrict leaky or swollen blood vessels in the nose which can cause congestion.

But Prof Lawrence says there is little evidence it works when taken as a tablet, rather than as a nasal spray, because much of the drug is broken down before it can reach the bloodstream.

In 2024, the US drug regulator said it wanted phenylephrine removed from all cold and flu pills, saying it was simply not effective, although that proposal has yet to be finalised.

Some cold and flu remedies contain a third active ingredient - guaifenesin - which is meant to loosen mucus in the airways.

That sits in more of a grey area: some studies report improvements in chest congestion, while others find little or no benefit.

A spokeswoman for Reckitt, which owns Lemsip and Nurofen, said the ingredients in its products are approved by regulators and formulated for multiple symptoms including fever, congestion and coughs.

News.title: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
News.content:
Poundland looks set to avoid immediate collapse after its US owners told MPs on Wednesday they were in favour of extending a deadline to find a rescue deal.

The discount chain, which has 11,000 employees, has been edging towards administration after being blocked by Gordon Borthers from accessing cash in its bank accounts.

A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation told the BBC they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release funding in recent days.

A committee of MPs questioned Gordon Brothers following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal.

Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just Â£1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period.

The investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied the claims.

But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

About Â£50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops.

The BBC understands that Gordon Brothers agreed to release a further Â£9m from Poundland's accounts, on top of Â£10m announced earlier. This will grant the company an additional 10 days to find a new buyer.

There are three bids currently on the table for Poundland, all of which have so far been rejected by the Gordon Brothers, who stand to profit from selling the company and its stock piecemeal.

News.title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers
News.content:
Levels of the two most toxic "forever" chemicals in England's rivers have dropped by nearly a third over the last decade, according to new figures from the Environment Agency (EA).

The decline in the chemicals, PFOS and PFOA, has been put down to stricter restrictions on their use in products after increasing evidence emerged of their damaging impact on human health and the environment.

One expert studying the impact of the chemicals said it was "brilliant" to see how far the UK has come on this issue.

Thousands of other forever chemicals, known officially as PFAS, remain in use but the regulator said its report showed the need for them all to be better monitored and regulated.

PFAS were first developed in the 1930s in the US and became popular with companies making products like frying pans and firefighting foam because of their useful, oil-resistant, water-resistant and electrical properties.

They are called forever chemicals because their natural resistance means they take a very long time to break down naturally.

The earliest types of these chemicals were called PFOS and PFOA. But two decades ago researchers started to find that they were linked to tissue damage in animals and increased rates of certain serious health conditions such as testicular cancer., external

As a result, PFOS was all but banned in the UK in 2010 and PFOA in 2020.

The latest data from the regulator, published on Thursday, shows that the concentrations in English rivers of PFOS and PFOA over the last ten years have now fallen by 30% and 29% respectively.

Levels in fresh-water fish have fallen 49%.

"It's brilliant to see how far we have come in the last 10 years," said Dr David Megson, reader in environmental forensics at Manchester Metropolitan University.

News.title: Scottish DJ, 32, confirmed as victim of Krakow shooting
News.content:
Det Ch Insp David McAlinden, senior investigating officer from Police Scotland's Counter Terrorism Policing unit, said the force was "aware of the tragic death of a Scottish man in Krakow".

He added: "Working in conjunction with COPFS (the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service), Police Scotland is supporting the UK counter-terrorism policing network and the Polish authorities.

"The immediate shared priority is to ensure that identification is properly established for the family, so that repatriation can take place as quickly as possible.

"The family has asked for their privacy to be respected. Our thoughts are with them and everyone impacted by this incident."

Mark Jewell, a close friend of Campbell's who regularly DJ'd with him, described him as "a quiet, kind and soft-hearted person, who wouldn't have harmed a fly".

He added: "It's just so tragic that he had to be in the wrong place at the wrong time.

"I had been speaking with him when he was headed over to Poland and I messaged him as soon as I heard about the terrible attack, to ask if he was safe - not for one minute expecting that he would have been caught up in it all.

"I was fully expecting a funny message back from him, saying not to worry. I can't quite get my head round it all."

News.title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog
News.content:
A watchdog has launched a crackdown on misleading sunbed adverts, warning tanning firms they must not claim their beds are safe or can treat medical conditions.

The Committee for Advertising Practice (CAP) said it was issuing a UK-wide enforcement notice to "send a clear message to the industry that advertisers must not downplay the risks associated with sunbed use".

Earlier this year, the BBC identified hundreds of social media videos claiming the beds could boost energy and treat skin conditions or mental health problems.

The Sunbed Association, which represents around half of the UK's tanning salons, said it fully supported action against misleading adverts, but said businesses must still be allowed to demonstrate they operate responsibly.

The CAP, which draws up the UK's advertising rules, said some of the claims being made by companies were potentially harmful and could discourage customers from seeking appropriate medical treatment or advice.

"Sunbeds carry serious health risks, including an increased risk of skin cancer," said the CAP's compliance executive James Burnett.

"Ads shouldn't downplay those risks or present sunbed use as a way to improve health."

Cancer charities and doctors are clear about the risks of using sunbeds - and say the machines are linked to higher rates of melanoma and other skin cancers.

Using a bed before the age of 35 increases the risk of melanoma by 59% later in life, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

Young people are by far the biggest sunbed users in the UK - about one in seven 18-to-24-year-olds say they used one in the past year, double the average for all age groups, according to a 2025 YouGov survey.

Rosie Vare, health information manager at Teenage Cancer Trust, said skin cancer was one of the most common forms of the disease in young adults and she welcomed stricter enforcement of the advertising rules.

"We want young people to be properly informed about the risk of sunbed use and we recommend using trusted, regulated sources to find out information such as the NHS, external or cancer charities, external," she added.

News.title: No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister
News.content:
The education secretary told MSPs that she had held a meeting with police and local authorities.

"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," Mairi McAllan said.

"I would take this opportunity to repeat Police Scotland's advice that there is nothing to suggest any threats to the public from the content of the emails."

The cabinet secretary added there was a "considerable amount of work" ongoing by Police Scotland and partners across the UK to "understand the motivations and the individuals behind this".

Most local authorities contacted by BBC Scotland said schools were operating as normal but some confirmed pupils had been evacuated.

More than 300 calls were made to police when a similar message was sent to schools around the country on 19 October.

In many areas, pupils were off due to half-term holidays.

On Wednesday the majority of schools in Dumfries and Galloway received the email and some were evacuated as a precaution.

A spokesperson for the local authority said: "Each school community/setting is unique and as such has its own way of supporting and reassuring learners and staff.

"We also know that local police have attended some school settings in a community capacity to assist and reassure."

In Edinburgh Queensferry High School was evacuated and pupils were sent home.

Highland Council confirmed a number of its schools "made the decision to activate their emergency protocols".

Local authorities in Glasgow, Edinburgh, East Lothian, Aberdeenshire and Orkney also confirmed their schools received the message.

In Northern Ireland, the Education Authority (EA) said the "message has similarities with a bogus threat sent last month" which was treated as a hoax by the (PSNI).

The Police Service of Northern Ireland said the email originated from outside the UK.

Italian reports said 280 school head teachers had received threats in recent days. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has called a meeting of top ministers and intelligence chiefs over the issue.

News.title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
News.content:
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives that it alleges were involved in a string of plots in the US and Europe.

The DOJ said Iranian agents most recently "orchestrated a terrorist plot at an air force base in the United Kingdom", saying they were involved in the major incident in September near RAF Fairford in the UK, where US armed forces were stationed.

The three men have been accused by the DOJ of being involved in 18 attacks and attempted attacks, including in London, Amsterdam and Paris. Some of the incidents were said to be directed by the men over FaceTime.

The DOJ said they acted in the name of the group Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI).

Iranian Mohsen Mohajeri, Iraqi national Mohammad Ali al-Hassani and dual Iranian-Iraqi citizen Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi were charged in an indictment unsealed on Tuesday, the DOJ said.

The DOJ said that most recently, al-Hassani "orchestrated a terrorist plot" at RAF Fairford - where on 27 September a major incident was declared after suspicious vans were reported near the base.

Seven men have been arrested in the UK over the incident at RAF Fairford.

Iran has strongly denied any involvement.

Al-Hassani and Mohajeri were allegedly both in Iran at the time of the incident, the indictment claims.

Meanwhile, al-Saadi was coordinating with the pair through third parties from a prison in New York, where he is awaiting trial on previous charges after being arrested in August, it adds.

US court records show that al-Saadi is due in court on 19 November, though it is not clear whether this status conference - which is usually a routine scheduled appearance - relates to the new charges or the previous ones. The BBC has asked the Southern District of New York for comment.

News.title: Jailed undertaker lodges bid to appeal against sentence
News.content:
Victims of the Legacy funeral scandal say it is an "insult" Hull undertaker Robert Bush has lodged an application to appeal against his 20-year prison sentence.

Bush, 48, admitted keeping 30 bodies after their funerals, presenting families with the ashes of strangers and selling fake funeral plans.

He pleaded guilty to 67 separate offences and was sentenced in July 2026.

Humberside Police said it had been notified by the Criminal Appeal Office at the Royal Courts of Justice and added "any decision regarding the appeal will be a matter for the courts".

In August, Bush wrote to families impacted by his crimes to express regret and said he was "deeply sorry".

Prosecutors said he ran a "shambolic and chaotic" funeral business at premises on Hessle Road in Hull and his "appalling" offending had caused "extreme emotional pain, anguish and upset".

His crimes over a 12-year period involved more than 300 victims.

News.title: Reform boycotts Senedd after member banned for saying white people are being replaced
News.content:
Jenner confirmed her party's boycott on the steps of the Senedd on Wednesday afternoon.

"It is now clear that the freedom of speech of one of our Senedd members is being curtailed, meaning his constituents are being silenced," she said.

"We stand behind Joe, and we will not attend today's plenary session in protest at his treatment.

"Every Reform MS [Member of the Senedd] will be in their Senedd office working hard for our constituents."

Martin said he would not apologise.

"My voters sent me to the Senedd to speak on their behalf," he said.

"I am being blocked from doing so, and now it's clear that I have fewer rights than the people who elected me.

"That cannot be the situation in a national parliament."

Asked by BBC Wales if he genuinely believed white people were being "replaced" in the UK, Martin said: "That's obviously a fact."

Aliya Mohammed, chief executive of the charity Race Equality First, said "the idea that white people are being 'replaced' is linked to a conspiracy theory that creates division and wrongly portrays people from minority ethnic backgrounds as a threat".

"Immigration can and should be debated, but language that fuels fear and hostility has no place in public discourse," she said.

"Being Welsh or British is not defined by race or skin colour.

"Wales belongs to all of us, and our diversity is one of our greatest strengths."

News.title: Police believed Huntingdon train attacker had schizophrenia, jury told
News.content:
Police dealing with a man accused of trying to kill 10 people on a train noted he had schizophrenia following his arrest, a court has been told.

Anthony Williams denies attempting to murder passengers and staff on a London-bound train, which made an emergency stop in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, on 1 November last year.

Cambridge Crown Court heard PC Caitlin Brown, who was involved in transporting Williams to hospital then to the police station, said he "appeared to be talking to himself" and spoke about the devil.

Williams, 33, of Langford Road in Peterborough, also denies four other counts of attempted murder related to earlier attacks in Peterborough and London.

Jurors were shown footage of Williams' arrest in the car park of Huntingdon railway station, and the court heard a Taser and a baton gun - which fires less lethal objects - were used against the defendant.

In a statement read to court, the arresting officer said Williams had said something along the lines of "kill me, kill me".

PC Matt Panks, another officer involved in transporting Williams, said in his statement he saw the suspect "acting strangely, appeared completely unphased by what had occurred... he was rocking and laughing".

News.title: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms
News.content:
Some Labour MPs have called on the government to reject the Rosebank oil field, saying it is "incompatible" with the UK's climate commitments.

There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field off the north-west coast of Shetland will be given the go-ahead.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that a decision would be "taken in due course" while Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh stressed that affordability of energy bills was her "overriding objective".

But in a sign of the division within the party, more than a dozen Labour MPs expressed concerns in Parliament about approving it. Others expressed support, pointing to economic benefits.

Supportive Labour MPs said some other parts of the world emitted far more greenhouse gases than the UK and warned of relying on imports. Reports have suggested that Chancellor John Healey is in favour of approval.

Separately, it is understood some Labour backbenchers have organised a letter opposing Rosebank - intended for Burnham, but not yet sent - which more than 60 out of about 400 Labour MPs have indicated they support.

One signatory told the BBC that approving Rosebank "would not create new jobs, would bring minimal money into the Treasury and be bad for the climate".

"The government's central aim is to tackle the cost of living crisis, and drilling for more oil at Rosebank isn't the answer," the MP said.

Wednesday's Westminster Hall - a type of parliamentary debate where backbench MPs raise topical issues but do not vote - was organised by Green MP Carla Denyer.

Labour MP for Sheffield Central Abtisam Mohamed told the debate: "Rosebank fails on every test.

"It will not benefit taxpayers who will shoulder the vast majority of the development costs, it will not strengthen our energy security because most of the oil will be sold on international markets, and it will not reduce energy bills for our constituents, who will remain exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices."

Richard Burgon, a former frontbencher on the left of the party, said: "Rosebank is not compatible with our climate targets - it's dangerous to pretend otherwise."

The UK is committed to reaching net zero by 2050 and wants to limit global warming to no more than 1.5C above the pre-industrial period.

The UK government has always insisted that Rosebank is a quasi-judicial decision, formally resting with Fahnbulleh. She green-lit production in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea last month, but Rosebank hangs in the balance.

News.title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse
News.content:
Former safeguarding minister Jess Phillips has joined calls from campaigners for the government to back new technology that blocks the live-streaming of child sexual abuse.

The UK National Crime Agency has flagged the UK as the third biggest market in the world, external for live-streamed abuse, where children are sexually abused live on camera to order.

Device-level blockers can prevent this material being filmed and viewed on smartphones, laptops and tablets in the first place, Phillips said, at the launch of a policy report in Parliament.

Anti-abuse campaigners claim keeping the technology at device level maintains privacy and encryption. Civil liberties campaigners Big Brother Watch dispute this.

The government has already legislated to demand tech firms like Apple and Google, which develop the operating systems of most smartphones used in the UK, block under-18s from taking or sharing nude images on smartphones and other devices.

However, three-quarters of child sexual abuse material (CSA) was not self-generated but likely captured on adult devices, according to 2025 research from the Internet Watch Foundation (IWF), which works to eliminate child sexual abuse imagery online.

Some 1.8 million men in the UK admitted to some form of online sexual offending against children, according to research from child safety institute Childlight.

Phillips, who complained of repeated delays to work to tackle CSA when she resigned as safeguarding minister in May, is demanding action to tackle the source of the crime and reduce the number of British offenders.

"This should be a source of national shame, and we must stop it," the Labour MP said.

"The technology, the evidence and the public support are all there - I want to work with ministers to extend on-device blocking to child sexual abuse material on every device sold in Britain, making children here and over the world safer."

The software uses AI to classify known child abuse images in the phone's operating system, and blocks the material at the moment it is viewed or created, whatever app is in use.

Nothing is logged, stored or sent anywhere, and the tech would work alongside encryption.

The AI classifier has been trained against a database of known child abuse images so it can differentiate between harmless material such as children at the beach, and sexual abuse.

Phillips said online child sexual abuse is "an issue that we did not keep control of" as legislators and now must be prioritised, at the event in Parliament.

She was joined by survivors of online child sexual abuse, who said they should not have to beg for the removal of images of themselves being abused from the internet.

Phil Eccles, from the National Crime Agency (NCA), said the scale of the problem was "at crisis point".

"This would cut off at source somebody on the UK their ability to direct a live stream for a child to be abused," he said.

"To me, safeguarding children will always supersede the ability to prosecute. If we can stop that abuse we must.

"But it's so important that tech companies come onboard - we cannot arrest our way out of this problem."

News.title: London borough is Britain's happiest, survey finds
News.content:
Richmond upon Thames has been named as the happiest place to live in Britain in an annual survey.

Residents of the south-west London borough have easy access to central London and strolls along the Thames on their doorstep, as well as boutiques, cafes and opportunities to spot roaming deer in their local parks.

Richmond ranked particularly highly across several aspects of local life in Rightmove's "happy at home index", including access to nature and green spaces, essential local services, shops and restaurants, employment opportunities as well as residents' pride in their area.

But, living there comes at a cost, with the average asking price for a home in the borough standing at more than Â£1m.

Harrogate in North Yorkshire and Cirencester in Gloucestershire came in second and third places respectively in Rightmove's 15th annual "happy at home index".

In Wales, Monmouth was the highest ranked, while Kirkcaldy took the top spot for Scotland.

News.title: Ousted Press Secretary Katie Zacharia melts down in BBC interview
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Katie Zacharia, who briefly served as White House press secretary last month, repeatedly redirected questions about the 2026 midterm election results during an interview on the BBC’s “Newsnight,” focusing instead on an ongoing Senate race in Alaska.

During the interview, presenter Victoria Derbyshire asked Zacharia about statements made by President Donald Trump following election losses that handed control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate to Democrats.

Derbyshire noted that Trump had initially expressed a desire to work with congressional Democrats before raising concerns about election integrity days later.

In response, Zacharia raised questions about the Senate contest in Alaska, where the Republican incumbent, Senator Dan Sullivan, faces a challenge from Mary Peltola, a Democrat, as well as an independent candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan.

"Do you think that Dan Sullivan in Alaska is fair?" Zacharia asked.

open image in gallery During an appearance on the BBC program ‘Newsnight,’ former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia avoided questions regarding the 2026 midterm election results, focusing instead on a disputed Senate race in Alaska ( Getty )

Derbyshire questioned why Vice President JD Vance did not cite the Alaska contest in a recent social media post attributing the Republican Party’s midterms performance to the war in Iran.

"Why didn’t JD Vance mention the Sullivans and Alaska?" Derbyshire asked. "Does questioning if the election was honest mean that the president is now at odds with his vice president, who clearly said, in a long social media post, it was because of the Iran war, why Republicans lost?"

Zacharia said that Derbyshire was avoiding the subject of the Alaska ballot structure.

"You don’t want to answer the question because you know it’s not fair," Zacharia said. "You know that, that was a set-up! It is so clearly a set-up, and that is why it is being investigated right now.

“And that should be across the pond being questioned just as much as anywhere else in the world. This is not some random obscurity. This is two Dan Sullivans that were on the ballot in Alaska."

open image in gallery The former press secretary repeatedly pointed to Alaska’s contentious Senate race, where incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan shares the ballot with an independent candidate of the same name ( Getty )

Republicans have asserted that the presence of the independent candidate was intended to confuse voters. Allegations of Democratic involvement in the independent candidate’s campaign have been denied.

As ballot counting continued Wednesday morning with 84 percent of votes tabulated, Peltola’s lead exceeded the combined vote totals of both other candidates on the ballot.

When Derbyshire attempted to return to Vance’s comments regarding the Iran conflict, Zacharia asked: "Who put Dan S. Sullivan on that ballot? Who did that?"

She added: "The New York Times had an answer. Did you read that? Did you read what The New York Times came out with? Yes or no?"

Zacharia also addressed potential policy differences within the administration.

“The president has been very clear; there is not any kind of ‘at odds’ right now,” she said. “He made those statements very clear, both in his interview and across the board. Any kind of insinuation that there’s this massive division happening is not actually understanding the relationship between the president and the vice president.”

open image in gallery Asked why President Donald Trump transitioned from pledging cooperation with Democrats to raising election integrity concerns, Zacharia described him as the ‘fighter in chief’ regardless of the outcome ( Reuters )

The exchange also covered Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who was the subject of an impeachment resolution introduced by Representative Thomas Massie, Republican of Kentucky, over the administration’s authorization of military action in Iran. House Republicans voted 211 to 204 on Tuesday to refer the eight articles of impeachment to committee, effectively blocking the measure from reaching the House floor.

In the interview, recorded prior to the vote, Derbyshire asked whether Hegseth should resign to relieve political pressure on the White House.

"Pete Hegseth should absolutely not resign," Zacharia said. "He’s been a wonderful secretary of war, and he absolutely did what any other secretary of war or secretary of defense would do in these circumstances."

She added: "And history will prove that not only President Trump, but also Secretary Hegseth will be thanked for ensuring the U.K. and the rest of the world won’t have to deal with nuclearized Iran."

open image in gallery Zacharia served five days as press secretary in October before being replaced following a 14-minute briefing ( AFP/Getty )

Derbyshire also asked whether the midterm results indicated that Trump had lost political momentum. Zacharia rejected the characterization, citing historical trends where the sitting president's party typically loses congressional seats during midterm cycles.

"Regardless of the outcome, he is the fighter in chief," Zacharia said, describing the midterms as "not even a setback" for the president.

"Absolutely not a loser,” she said.

Zacharia served five days as press secretary in October before being replaced following a 14-minute briefing in which she took questions from three news organizations. The position has remained vacant since Karoline Leavitt stepped down in August.

News.title: White House makes astonishing claim about ‘giggling’ on Trump’s C-Span call
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The White House has claimed that a woman's laughter heard at the start of President Donald Trump’s phone call to C-SPAN was "leftover audio from a previous caller who had not disconnected yet."

The statement was provided to Inside Edition following online speculation about the brief audio glitch during Trump's eight-minute interview on Monday night.

The exchange began around 9 p.m. when host Mimi Geerges introduced the segment, saying, “It looks like we’ve got a call from the White House.”

As the line connected, an unidentified woman could be heard laughing before a click sounded and Trump began speaking.

“Thank you, Mimi, and good luck with the show,” Trump said, making no reference to the laughter. “I’ve watched you numerous times, and you do a great job. But good luck with the show.”

open image in gallery According to the White House, the female laughter picked up at the beginning of President Donald Trump’s phone call to C-SPAN was ‘leftover audio from a previous caller who had not disconnected yet’ ( Getty )

Geerges also did not address the sound during the call, during which she struggled to keep the president on topic.

Social media users quickly began guessing who the voice belonged to, with several observers pointing toward the president's personal aide.

“Stephen Miller first day as chief of staff,” foreign policy journalist Laura Rozen posted online. “Natalie Harp audibly giggling as Trump calls into C-SPAN.”

Late-night comedians also mocked the mystery audio.

“Based on the happy laugh, experts are 100 percent sure it wasn’t Melania,” Jimmy Fallon joked on his show. “Trump was, like, ‘Don’t worry, that’s my assistant Natalie, and definitely not my new Chinese spy girlfriend.’”

open image in gallery Online commentators pointed to personal aide Natalie Harp as the mystery laugher ( AFP/Getty )

Rather than addressing the mystery voice, Trump turned his focus to media coverage surrounding the logistics of the appearance. After The New York Times reported that his call to the network was unannounced, the president pushed back in a post on Truth Social around 1 a.m.

“The New York Times incorrectly reported that ‘Mr. Trump called into the premier of a C-Span show, APPARENTLY WITHOUT NOTICE.’ This is WRONG,” Trump wrote. “It was a fully scheduled call, as a favor to C-Span, set up through White House Communications. It was done at C-Span’s request, not mine. The Times knew this, but lied, in order to demean - But this is the least of their lies!”

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

News.title: Pat Cummins to address media on sandpaper scandal
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Australia captain Pat Cummins has called a press conference to have his say on Usman Khawaja’s ball-tampering allegations that have reopened the 2018 sandpaper scandal.

Cummins has been rested from the white-ball series against England which begins on Friday in Perth, but has publicly invited a media grilling in Sydney on Friday morning to respond to the accusations which have followed the publication of Khawaja’s new autobiography.

Khawaja’s memoir Sabr has reopened old scars in Australian cricket, specifically with his claims that knowledge of the sandpaper plot was widespread within the team and coaching staff even though Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft alone were punished.

In an interview with the Sydney Morning Herald he said blame was shared by “all of us”, said his calls for collective responsibility were shot down by specific un-named team-mates and suggested tampering had been going on prior to the Cape Town Test where Bancroft’s cheating was exposed.

His revelations have invited renewed speculation over the role of the bowling group which benefitted from the ball manipulation – with Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon having previously distanced themselves from the episode.

In 2021, the quartet issued a carefully worded statement responding to “rumour mongering and innuendo” in which they denied knowing that a foreign substance had been taken on to the field to alter the ball.

That line may no longer hold water, given Khawaja’s suggestions that the matter was openly discussed and had taken place in the previous match.

open image in gallery Cummins (right) is set to respond to accusations made by Khawaja (left) (Adam Davy/PA) ( PA Archive )

Now Cummins, who could find his position as captain of the national team called into question, is set to confront the issue head on.

“I’m training at Cricket Central (in Sydney) tomorrow morning before the Blues play in the Shield match,” he wrote on X.

“Happy to speak with any and all media about the events of this week at 9.30 am. I’ve taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy’s allegations so I can respond properly. Afterwards please stay and support the Blues! I’ll ask CA (Cricket Australia) to send out details.”

Starc appeared at a sponsor’s event earlier this week, offering a stiff response that reiterated his previous position.

“As far as our statement said, we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field, that’s where I’ll leave it,” he said.

“I’ll stick to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time, eight years ago. Clearly, there’s different versions from different people, and I’ll leave it where I left it back then.”

News.title: Young people to no longer get main sickness benefit and PIP under Milburn’s welfare overhaul plan
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Young people would no longer be entitled to the main sickness and disability benefits under a radical overhaul of the welfare system that would see a reduction in financial support for some.

Former health secretary Alan Milburn has proposed a “big rewriting” of the system as part of his review to be published on Tuesday - and admitted the road will not be “pain-free” in an interview with The Times.

The chair of the Social Mobility Foundation spent the last year reviewing the one million people aged 18-24 who are not in education, employment or training. He said that reforming the system would be the best way to offer young people a chance of finding work.

His plan, reported The Times, would see young people no longer able to claim the two main sickness and disability benefits: the health element of universal credit and the personal independence payment (PIP).

Instead, they would move on to a new “youth allowance”, which would be paid at the same level as the standard rate of universal credit.

open image in gallery Former health secretary Alan Milburn has proposed a ‘big rewriting’ of the welfare system ( PA Wire )

For those who received PIP which is intended for people with a disability, they will be moved on to a new “additional cost allowance” which would cover day-to-day costs relating to their conditions.

Those who are not capable of working at all due to their disability would be given a new benefit, paid at a higher rate.

In the interview with The Times, he said: “I’m not saying that any of this will be easy or that it will be pain-free because it won’t.

“Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. But actually, for young people, there’s a different debate that we’ve got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances.”

He added that he was more focussed on what would give young people a better chance of creating a good life, rather than just be better off for a year or two.

The government plans to bring forward major welfare reforms in 2027 amid efforts to reduce the 45 per cent of young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) – around a million people.

Prime minister Andy Burnham has said an overhaul to the benefits system will require the government to “invest up front in young people”.

Under Mr Milburn’s plans, employment support would also be expanded.

“The menu of opportunities has got to increase,” he told The Times. “They’ll have a personal adviser, they’ll be coached all the way through. The adviser will stick with them until they have found a job or an apprenticeship or college place.”

Disability charity Sense said it supported efforts to give more young disabled people the opportunity to work while protecting those who cannot.

But director of influencing Harriet Edwards said: “We’re deeply concerned that, if these proposals are taken forward without proper funding for specialist employment support alongside welfare changes, some young disabled people could lose out.

“We need to understand who will qualify for the new support, who risks missing out, and what practical, accessible help young disabled people will actually receive to find work.

“We know many of the families we support are deeply anxious about what these changes could mean for them, and we urge the government to provide clarity as soon as possible.”

News.title: Black University of Mississippi students wrestle with forgiveness in wake of racist gestures
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Three Black University of Mississippi students who shared a now-viral Ring camera video of two white students making monkeylike sounds and gestures outside their front door say they received an apology from one woman.

But the other only amplified her behavior, they said, divulging details of the rest of the encounter that weren't captured on camera.

“She continued to make the gestures after the girl was apologizing. It was like a slap in the face,” Victoria Johnson told “CBS Mornings” in an interview that aired Wednesday.

Johnson was joined by her roommates, Jakiyra Metcalf and Kaiyden Caldwell, to talk about the incident that has ignited a firestorm on the Ole Miss campus and across social media. The animalistic gestures and sounds are seen as racist because they were reminiscent of ugly, old stereotypes comparing Black people to simians.

For it to happen at a college community in the Deep South with a long history of racism has added to the raw emotions.

Metcalf saw the video Friday and she and Johnson went outside to talk to the two women, who had another friend with them. She was only seen glancing at the door in the video.

They said one woman, Alaina Kunes, apologized but said they had been making animallike noises and gestures in front of other doors in the apartment complex. But the second woman, who lives in the complex, purportedly kept the antics going off camera.

Metcalf's TikTok post has been viewed over 13 million times in four days. On Monday, the university posted a statement condemning the actions in the video as “offensive, hurtful, and unacceptable behaviors that conflict with our university values.” School officials also said the incident is being investigated and they are dedicated to “maintaining a safe and welcoming environment.”

Kunes, 18, issued a public apology Tuesday through a law firm.

“Before the incident on Nov. 6, I never met the women involved and was unaware of their race, however I recognize my actions were insensitive, inappropriate and deeply harmful,” Kunes said. “I would have never intentionally made those noises or gestures toward a person of color. I have apologized to the women and I pray they will forgive me.”

She has since withdrawn from school. She also said she would fully cooperate with any investigation.

The statement was originally posted on the firm's website, but it had to be taken down because of ongoing harassment, said Kate Gardiner, a spokesperson for the firm.

Kunes will not be speaking beyond the statement, Gardiner added.

Outrage at taunting prompts opposition to social media shaming

The outrage against Kunes and the second woman, who has not publicly identified herself, has also stirred up opposition against using social media to malign them.

Tom Hennessey, an influencer tied to online fundraisers for people criticized for making xenophobic remarks, is credited with starting a fundraiser for the other woman on Christian fundraising platform GiveSendGo. It has raised over $30,000 as of Wednesday afternoon. The fundraising page states the “online mob (is) treating a juvenile stunt as a hate crime because the residents were Black.”

The fundraiser also says it could possibly be canceled if the woman “disavows our support and bends the knee” and apologizes.

When contacted via X, or Twitter, DM, Hennessey said there is a double-standard and less attention is given to Black-on-white crime. He declined to say whether he had been in touch with the student about the fundraiser.

This is not the first time the university has been the backdrop for a Black student dealing with taunting animallike mimicking. In a May 2024 campus demonstration over the Israel-Hamas war, a counterprotester made monkey sounds and gestures at a Black, female student. The interaction was filmed by a student journalist. The video got the attention of outgoing Georgia Republican U.S. Rep. Mike Collins, who appeared to praise the behavior in a tweet.

University has ties to nation's desegregation movement

Ole Miss also has a long history with racism, civil rights and segregation. In 1962, activist James Meredith was the first Black person to be admitted to the school after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in his favor.

Then-Gov. Ross Barnett tried to block his admission but could not disobey federal law, according to the National Museum of African American History & Culture. Still, white objectors instigated a riot on campus. Two bystanders died and over 200 arrests were made.

Metcalf, Caldwell and Johnson hedged when asked if they forgive Kunes.

“I still have very mixed feelings about it,” Metcalf said.

Caldwell said she appreciated the apology but said it doesn't change what happened.

“It's still hurtful, and it's still devastating that someone would go to our camera and do that," Caldwell said.

News.title: Tim Robbins says he’s trying to solve ‘mystery’ of why his cult 90s movie isn’t on streaming
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Tim Robbins says it’s a “mystery” who owns the rights to his 1992 cult political satire Bob Roberts.

The film is not currently available on streaming services, and the 68-year-old Shawshank Redemption star says he hopes to change that.

Robbins wrote, directed and starred in Bob Roberts, a mockumentary that followed the titular conservative politician and folk singer.

The film heavily referenced the Bob Dylan documentary Dont Look Back, and featured a starry cast including Susan Sarandon, John Cusack, Alan Rickman and, in his film debut, Jack Black.

On X, Robbins wrote: “Very excited to find out who controls the rights to Bob Roberts as it has been a mystery for quite a few years.”

open image in gallery Susan Sarandon and Tim Robbins were a couple during the making of ‘Bob Roberts’, before splitting decades later in 2009 ( AP )

He continued: “Yesterday we posted a clip from the end of the film, and a restriction was placed on it from the owner. We pulled the clip and the film from the website with apologies and with the hope that the owner will engage with us on how to get the film distributed on a platform.”

Robbins said he posted a clip showing the character of Terry Manchester (Brian Murray), who is supposedly the director making the mockumentary.

He explained: “For those who did not see it, the clip follows the film’s documentarian into the Jefferson Memorial as we hear a news report about how opinion polls of Americans who opposed the first Iraq war have shifted from opposition to support. The final frames of the film pan across Jefferson’s words etched in the stone of the memorial. ‘I have sworn upon the altar of God eternal hostility against every form of tyranny over the mind of man.’”

In 2024, Robbins spoke out against conspiracy theories drawing parallels between Bob Roberts and the attempted assassination of Donald Trump.

In the film, Roberts stages a failed attempt on his life to increase his public support in order to win the election.

When Trump was injured in a shooting incident at a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, some conspiracy theorists on social media claimed it was similarly staged.

Writing on X at the time, Robbins spoke out against the speculation, saying: “To anyone drawing a parallel between my film Bob Roberts and the attempted assassination of Trump, let’s be clear. What happened yesterday was a real attempt on a presidential candidate’s life.”

He continued: “Those that are denying the assassination attempt was real are truly in a deranged mindset. A human being was shot yesterday. Another killed. They may not be human beings that you agree with politically but for shame folks.”

“Get over your blind hatred of these people,” he added. “They are fellow Americans. This collective hatred is killing our souls and consuming whatever is left of our humanity.”

News.title: Mississippi elects its first Black senator in 150 years giving Democrats a 55-seat majority
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Blanche Bruce was born into slavery in 1841. He later served one term as a U.S. senator from Mississippi. He was the second — and the last — Black senator from a state at the violent heart of the nation’s civil rights struggle.

Nearly 150 years later, Mississippi voters elected Scott Colom, who is poised to be the first Black candidate elected to the U.S. Senate from the Deep South state since the aftermath of the Civil War.
