The former EFL boss had previously received a vote of confidence, but talkSPORT understands he has now decided to walk away from the role.

During discussions over a number of weeks, Beale's decision follows a misalignment with leadership over the long-term vision of the club.



It is understood he had concerns around the club’s decision-making, particularly due to a lack of consultation and involvement in recruitment.

Beale walks despite public backing

In his brief spell in Belgium, Beale took charge of 12 games, winning just four times, drawing twice and losing on six occasions.



Pressure had begun to mount on the 46-year-old in late October after his Zulte Waregem side suffered a fourth straight defeat to strugglers La Louviere - who have since sacked Ed Still as manager.

Despite the poor run of form, sporting director Niels Leroy publicly backed Beale, and insisted his job was not under threat.

He said: “Michael Beale is not under pressure right now.

4 Beale's time in Belgium never quite got going, as he lost more games than he won Credit: AFP

4 The Englishman leaves with Zulte Waregem sitting 14th out of 17 in the Belgian Pro League Credit: AFP



“We are confident that we can turn things around and pick up points in the upcoming games.

“But even if we were to lose three more games in a row, that wouldn’t automatically mean we’re going to fire Michael.

“At this club, we always consider the bigger picture. And we have a philosophy here that we don’t part ways with a coach lightly.

“As long as our analysis of a situation gives us sufficient reasons for hope, there is no reason to dismiss a coach.”



Despite this, Beale has made the decision to walk away after finding himself on a different page to club officials.

His appointment at Zulte Waregem marked the first time the 46-year-old had managed outside of the UK.

4 Beale has struggled at both Sunderland and Zulte Waregem after a promising start to management with QPR and Rangers Credit: Getty

He started out at Championship side QPR in June 2022 and oversaw an impressive run of eight wins in 11 games that had the west London side at the top of the table.



However, QPR's form nosedived with four losses in five games after Wolves unsuccessfully attempted to poach Beale from Loftus Road.

But there was nothing QPR could do to stop Beale from moving north to Scottish giants Rangers in November 2022.

Under Beale, Rangers finished the 2022/23 Scottish Premiership in second with 93 points, the largest runners-up total in league history.

Despite a bright start in Glasgow, a run of three losses in seven games in his second season at Ibrox brought the end of his tenure.



Beale was only out of work briefly though as Sunderland chose to roll the dice on him just over two months later, only for his reign to last only 12 games before he was sacked.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola eyed for new manager’s job in dramatic swoop
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola eyed for new manager’s job in dramatic swoop

US Soccer want Pep Guardiola to replace Mauricio Pochettino as the men's national team head coach, talkSPORT understands.

Pochettino looks set to leave for Premier League giants Manchester United having agreed a deal in principle to replace Michael Carrick.



2 Guardiola could be on his way back into management as the United States eye a replacement for Pochettino Credit: AFP

Those overseeing the managerial change in the United States set-up want to hire Guardiola in what would be a sensational appointment.

The Spaniard has been out of management since the summer when he left Manchester City after a decade at the club.

Guardiola won six Premier League titles and the Champions League, and is regarded as one of the best managers in history.



He also lifted three consecutive league trophies with Barcelona and Bayern Munich.

Joining the USMNT would present a fresh challenge as Guardiola has never managed at international level.



However, it won't be as straightforward for the powers that be as he hinted before his City exit that he would take a break from football.

Could Guardiola join USMNT?

"After my contract with City, I'm going to stop. I'm sure," he said in May 2025.



"I don't know if I'm going to retire, but I'm going to take a break. How I want to be remembered, I don't know."

In a separate interview, he reiterated: "So I'm not retiring, but I will take a break, for sure."

"When I finish here, I will take a break. I need to make a stop, that's all," Guardiola added.

2 Guardiola is one of the most successful managers in history and would be a remarkable appointment for the United States Credit: Getty



Despite leaving the club, Guardiola has maintained support for City in recent months.

He sent an emotional message to fans after City were found guilty on all charges of Premier League financial breaches in September.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all," the 55-year-old said.

Guardiola then attended their Champions League league phase clash at home to holders Paris Saint-Germain last month.



However, he watched his former side lose 4-2 in what was their worst home defeat in the competition ever.

Should Guardiola take the USMNT job, he could be on the touchline in time for the Gold Cup next summer.

Sports.title: Harry Kane confirms 2030 World Cup plans and doesn’t rule out future Premier League return
Sports.content:
Harry Kane hasn't got retirement on his mind as he revealed his intention to play at the next World Cup in just under four years time.

The England captain and Ballon d'Or winner joined talkSPORT Drive for an exclusive interview, and he was asked a variety of questions by Andy Goldstein and Darren Bent in a brilliant, wide-ranging chat.

5 Kane was in good spirits ahead of appearing for the 126th time for England against Croatia Credit: talkSPORT

He recently put pen to paper on a new contract with Bayern Munich that lasts until the summer of 2029.

Kane said he doesn't believe this will be the final contract of his football career, although he doesn't have any intention of cutting short his agreement with his current club.

The England legend is very happy in Germany, but once that deal expires, he's not sure what will happen.

One thing he is determined to make happen is the 2030 World Cup.

We saw in the 2026 World Cup that Lionel Messi, Luka Modric and Cristiano Ronaldo all took part despite being in their late 30s or early 40s.

And Kane is targeting involvement in the tournament that is set to be hosted in Spain, Morocco and Portugal, saying: "I hope to still be around by then. I'd be 35 nearly 36, but I think that is pretty young, to be honest.

"There are examples of players playing well into their 30s at the highest level, and as long as I am performing and I deserve my place in the team, then I'll be here.

"If I am scoring 50, 60, 70 goals a season for my club, there is no reason why I won't be here to help the national team.

"My biggest dream is to win a major trophy with England. There are some great things I have achieved throughout my career, but there are many more that I want to win.

"I think it is fairly realistic that I'll still be here for the World Cup in four years, but as we know, we have the home Euros, and that is where the focus lies."

5 Kane was named the best player in the world in October after a stellar 2025/26 season for Bayern Munich Credit: Getty

5 Kane is England's record goalscorer and now a Bayern fans' favourite Credit: Getty

Premier League return for Kane?

After spending his entire career in England, Kane took the bold plunge to abandon Tottenham and join Bayern Munich in a £100m deal.

That happened in 2023, and though the Champions League has evaded him thus far, the move has been a huge success.

He has won the Ballon d'Or and two Bundesliga titles and has scored over 150 goals already.

Kane is loved at the club and by their fans, while his family are settled in Bavaria.

When asked about a potential Premier League return, he said: "I'll be honest, I am really not sure.

"When I think back coming back, it isn't just about the record (top goalscorer in the Premier League), there are things I haven't achieved yet.

5 A few of the questions threw Kane off, but he handled them well Credit: talksport

"But since I've been away, it has really opened my eyes that there is a big old world out there, and I think people are appreciating my game more.

"So, I think it would have to be a perfect situation for me to ever come back, and I can't see where that would be."

Goldstein pressed if that meant it was still possible, he said: "One day, anything is possible."

Right at the end of the interview, Goldstein tried one more question about Kane returning to the Premier League, asking him if he'd re-join Tottenham or another top-flight club.

It left Kane shaking his head before he said: "All the tough questions at the end before I go.

"Who knows, I can't tell you. Time will tell."

5 Kane is a club legend at Tottenham and fans would be desperate to have him back Credit: Getty

Record breaker again

Kane will start England's Nations League game on Thursday night against Croatia, live on talkSPORT.

And ahead of that match, Kane has been speaking about breaking Peter Shilton's record.

This game will be Kane's 126th cap, and in a pre-match press conference, he said: "It's definitely up there as the biggest (achievement).

"I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career."

Sports.title: Harry Kane tells Manchester United fans exactly what to expect from ‘incredible’ Mauricio Pochettino
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has heaped praise on Mauricio Pochettino ahead of his potential appointment at Manchester United.

talkSPORT understands United players expect Pochettino to replace head coach Michael Carrick, who is likely to be told on Thursday that he has been relieved of his duties.

3 Pochettino looks set to replace Carrick in the Man United dugout and already reached an agreement in principle with United Credit: Getty

The Argentine is currently head coach of the United States national team, but has reached an agreement in principle with the hierarchy at Old Trafford.

Pochettino has a $10million (£7.5m) release clause in his contract, and an appointment is set to increase in value with his background staff.

Formerly of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, he has won 150 of his 294 matches in the Premier League, and also won Ligue 1 with Paris Saint-Germain.

The 54-year-old is mostly known for his stint at Spurs from 2014 to 2019, during which they had two league title challenges and reached their first ever Champions League final.

Kane flourished with him as his head coach having netted 169 goals in 242 outings under him, and since became the all-time top scorer for England as well as a Ballon d'Or winner.

With Pochettino looking likely to join United, Kane was asked about what their fans can expect from during an exclusive interview on talkSPORT Drive.

Kane on 'incredible' Pochettino

"I can't speak highly enough of him," Kane said. "At a stage in my career, he was massive to my development.

"He took a team that was extremely young and not seen as one of the top teams, to us having back-to-back title races, getting to a Champions League final. He took the club to the highest place it has almost ever been.

"For me, personally, he helped me develop as a player not just on the pitch, but also off the pitch. We built up a really good open relationship.

"It was my first time playing regularly at the highest level, all the demands and pressure that comes with that, he was a big help in dealing with that.

3 Kane credited Pochettino with helping him develop at Spurs and spoke on how he makes an impact off the pitch Credit: Getty

"He's an incredible manager, I think he has proven that over his career, but he's just a great person as well.

"I'm sure if it does happen, Man United will have a great coach that will do everything to get them back to the levels that they expect to be at."

Ex-England striker Darren Bent then spoke on how Pochettino comes across as both a manager and head coach, with the former role usually covering all bases rather than just tactics like the latter.

"He took a lot of the training, he took a lot of the tactical stuff and how he wanted us to play in pretty much every session," Kane revealed.

"But then he was a really good man manager as well. I think because we were such a young team at the time, I think he understood that there's a lot of players who would need guidance or an arm around the shoulder, or someone who's pushing.

"Even for me, to push me from a physical level, to do more at the gym. You always respected him and could have a talk with him, and be open with personal issues.

3 Kane has backed Pochettino to be a success at United and take them back towards the top of English football Credit: Getty

"For sure, he does both. I think that is the way that maybe more modern coaches are as well, you see that more and more."

Kane spoke ahead of England's Nations League clash against Croatia on Thursday night, which will be live on talkSPORT.

He is set to parade his Ballon d'Or trophy before kick-off, and then become his country's all-time leading appearance maker by winning his 126th cap.

Sports.title: Liam Delap outlines England ambition after frustrating Chelsea experience
Sports.content:
Liam Delap remains committed to earning a first ever England call-up amid his strong start to life at Nottingham Forest.

The striker, who signed in a £50million move from Chelsea during the summer, shone for his new club in their 3-1 win over Manchester City over the weekend.

3 Delap couldn't find his feet at Chelsea and, with only two goals scored for the club, he left after just one season for Forest Credit: Getty

Delap scored two thumping goals against his former side to help Forest rise out of the Premier League relegation zone.

The double took his league tally to three for the season thus far, and he has already beaten his total from the 2025/26 campaign at Chelsea.

Having impressed at Ipswich Town, Delap joined the Blues for £30m in June 2025 but had an underwhelming spell at Stamford Bridge.

With two goals in 41 outings across all competitions, one of which was in the Premier League, the 23-year-old flattered to deceive.

Speaking to talkSPORT on White and Jordan on Wednesday, Delap honestly reflected on his tough time at Chelsea as he said: "When things don't go so well, you learn a lot.

"You're sitting there sometimes, frustrated and angry. But you've just go to get through those moments because football's not a linear path.

"I think it grows you as a man more than anything, to be honest, just staying focused and concentrating on yourself."

Delap reveals England hopes

Club football has paused for the international break for one final time in 2026, although Delap is still at Forest as he did not receive a call-up with England for upcoming matches against Croatia and Spain.

He has 14 goals in 38 appearances at youth level for his country and is yet to be involved with the senior side, but the honour is in his sights.

"Yeah, 100 per cent, it's the ambition as a little kid," he replied when asked of his aspirations to play for England.

3 Delap showcased his quality and potential with two excellent strikes against City on Saturday evening Credit: AFP

3 With his club form now on the up, the striker is looking to take the next step and earn a senior call-up with England Credit: Getty

"I've just got to focus on what I can control, focus on game by game at Forest, and then see what happens."

When could Delap play for England?

Nine-time England international Danny Murphy joined the show, and believes that Delap is capable of featuring for England at Euro 2028.

Qualification officially gets underway in March, with the tournament then being played from June 9 to July 9, 2028.

That gives Delap plenty of time to stake his claim for a striker spot in the England squad should they qualify, with captain Harry Kane set to remain as the no.1 choice.

And Murphy is confident that, should he maintain his current form at Forest, he will be in and around head coach Thomas Tuchel's plans.

"I think Liam's got a great chance of carrying on the way he is," Murphy said.

"If he's playing regularly and his confidence builds, I think he's got a great chance of being in the Euros squad."

Sports.title: Danny Kelly: Tottenham, Adrian Durham, Simon Jordan and Laura Woods pay glowing tributes to talkSPORT legend
Sports.content:
Tributes for Danny Kelly have flooded in from far and wide following the tragic news of his death.

On Wednesday morning, it was announced that beloved broadcaster and talkSPORT presenter Danny had sadly passed away, aged 69.



6 Thousands have joined talkSPORT in paying tribute to Danny Kelly, who has sadly died aged 69

He was one of the most recognisable, respected and engaging voices across our network, having joined the team in 2007.

Danny stepped away from the mic in March following a throat cancer diagnosis and, during his last appearance, he urged men to go out and get themselves checked in what was an emotional message.

Like music, football was a massive passion of his, with Danny being a huge fan of Premier League giants Spurs.



His love of the game was clear for all to see in October 2008 as Aaron Lennon scored a last-gasp equaliser against their north London rivals Arsenal in the iconic 4-4 draw.

"I love football, Stan. I love it," he cried, and Spurs have offered their respect to Danny with a heartfelt post on social media.



Tottenham tribute to Danny Kelly

"The entire Tottenham family mourns the loss of one of our own, broadcasting legend Danny Kelly," they said.

"Our thoughts and love are with his family and friends at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Danny."



talkSPORT's announcement on X drew in more than one thousand replies from listeners and fans of Danny to pay respect, a testament to his legacy.

Simon Jordan offered his own tribute on White and Jordan, and in doing so, he revealed his admiration for Danny.

"I knew Danny very well. He was a brilliant broadcaster, a brilliant editor, a brilliant writer. He was a brilliant friend.

6 Danny was a cherished member of the talkSPORT family, and brought great joy to listeners on the airwaves Credit: talkSPORT



"The reasons why I'm able to broadcast and occupy the space I'm in now are because I worked with Danny. When I came here and started working with you guys, it was with Danny.

"Danny nurtured me and developed me, and corralled me, and persuaded me, and educated me, and censored me in equal measure."

Danny Murphy worked alongside the broadcasting icon on Kick Off for talkSPORT, and he said: "Warm, charismatic, funny... so funny. He could make a really serious moment lighthearted.

"And educational, he had a story about everyone and everything, he met everybody there is to know. Every time someone famous got brought up, he'd tell a little anecdote about when he met them and talked to them, and he was just always engaging to listen to.



"It was a pleasure to work with him over the years, I didn't realise how knowledgeable he was not just on music, but football as well. He loved his football, and that came through in abundance."

Former Breakfast host Laura Woods also joined the show, and recalled how much Danny helped her during a difficult moment in her career.

6 Danny will forever be remembered as one of radio's biggest and best presenters, and leave a lasting legacy for all of us Credit: talkSPORT

"You don't meet a lot of broadcasters that will really be informed and interested in your own career, he was interested in mine and he was so caring."



Woods added: "When I got the Breakfast show, it was in COVID and it was a really tough time for everyone. I felt it a lot, I really felt like I needed an ear, I was struggling to get to grips with the job and, for a little while, I didn't think I was right for it.

"Danny messaged me, and he was like, 'How's it going? How are you? Are you okay? Are you getting enough sleep?' And I said, 'No!' He went, 'Right, call me after the show tomorrow and we'll have a chat'.

"I remember that call, and it was exactly what I needed. It was just an ear at a time where I needed guidance from this great man. I felt like I always had that at talkSPORT, and he was like that for all of us.

"It didn't matter who you were, you were part of his little family if you worked anywhere near him. If you were in touching distance of Danny Kelly, he was your guidance."



talkSPORT legend Adrian Durham joined the boys on Drive to pay tribute to Danny, who was a very close personal friend.

An emotional Adrian said: "I would consider him one of my closest personal friends, not just a brilliant broadcaster and a wonderful colleague.

"He had this natural warmth with his voice that was infectious, it made you want to get involved as well.

"I remember being on a train full of Palace fans back from Wolves one day, and they asked me who my favourite presenter was, and I said Danny Kelly.



"They said they loved Trans Euro Express, and it is by far the best show on the station partly because of the European expert opinion but also because of Danny's warmth and the fact he was so interested, and that is why he was such a great broadcaster. It felt like was sitting next to you in the car or in the living room.

"Three years ago, I was going through a really terrible time in my life, and I was with my son.

"I went over to Ireland to see Danny just because I needed to talk to somebody who I thought could help me, and Danny was there for me.

"He was a trusted colleague and we hadn't even broadcast together at that point, thankfully, we did afterwards , but he was so good to me and warm and welcoming to me and my son and incredibly helpful on a personal level.



"We were talking about The Smiths and Stevie Wonder, and all the people we love, and my son asks him if he had any gangster rap.

"He pulls out the Wu Tang Clan and puts that on, and they were in their element - it was sensational, and he just had time for everybody.

"We worked together at the Sports Book Award, which is particularly emotional for me because I was on the judging panel, and Danny and I are meant to be doing that show together later this month, and obviously, he won't be doing it.

"So, I sent the winning book to him, so he had it in his possession and then this terrible, truly shocking news broke today - it is just tough for everybody."



6 Adrian's emotion reflects how the talkSPORT family feel about Danny

6 Danny was famously part of the Trans Europe Express show on Sunday evenings, with his knowledge marking a perfect end to the week Credit: talkSPORT

Many of Danny's other talkSPORT colleagues also paid their respects on social media, with chief football correspondent Alex Crook saying: "This is so sad. Danny was a great broadcaster and a brilliant colleague and friend.

"Had a wonderful day with him watching Spurs' last game at White Hart Lane. talkSPORT will never be quite the same again."



"Absolutely heartbroken to hear Danny Kelly has passed away," added reporter Ian Abrahams. "One of the best broadcasters I’ve worked with. One of the most amazing, kindest, funny, passionate people I knew.

"Danny, we'll always have "I love Football". I will miss you my friend, sleep well."

Stan Collymore also gave a lengthy tribute to Danny, as he said: "This morning I was told of the passing of my good friend and colleague, Danny Kelly.

"The tributes to him in the coming days from those who knew him and worked with him will give you an idea of how much he was loved. I loved him too. Very much so.



"A man who I called "Dad" on air because I wished he was. I hope you give me a few minutes to read my thoughts, and I hope they do you justice, Dan.

"By 2008 I was a mess. I would sleep 18 hours a day, the other 6 mostly wanting to die. Once or twice a week I would open my laptop, organise football tabs, gossip and news as prep for jobs in broadcasting that I knew would never come, "just in case".

"When hope dies, we die, after all. Then Danny Kelly came into my life. I was driving out of London having been to see a psychiatrist about the state I was in and had BBC London on the radio.

"Danny was presenting with a guest, reviewing books. My name came up in the conversation, so I called in. We hit it off straight away, talked about football for what seemed like forever but was probably a standard 10-12 minute section.



"But for me it sparked a temporary respite from sleep and chronic mental health issues and even for that I was grateful. A couple of years later Danny joined talkSPORT to do the 7-10pm slot through the week.

6 Rest in peace Danny, and thank you for everything

"He told me he was offered a few co-presenters but he remembered that conversation we had and he wanted me to do it. A lifeline of work, passionately talking about our sport, having fun and feeling a value as a human again.

"Something lost for 7 long years. Danny gifted me that. Without that I know I wouldn't be writing this today. "Always fresh, never frozen" was the tagline in a Domino's read we had to do in the show, something we'd instinctively greet each other with until our last meeting, in a pub, broadcasting for talkSPORT around 3 years ago.



"I didn't know that time would be the last, but perhaps fittingly we hugged as I left, I'm glad I did. The shows were loved. They were funny, honest, insightful and I hope, along with Saggers after that, proof that Danny's belief in me was worthy.

"But to say my love for him was only thanks for a job doesn't even scratch the surface.

"His kindness, his phone calls late at night (Dan was a notorious night owl) of support, his man hugs, his indomitable spirit, his big brain on anything from football to music to geopolitics, his love, as I know many others will testify, came from the biggest of hearts and the biggest of souls housed in a giant of a man in every sense.

"Dan, thank you, thank you for the kindness, the fun, the hope, the support and for being someone to look up to and aspire to be. I love you very much, I know I'll hug you again some day. Thank you for everything. 'I love football Stan, I love it'."

Sports.title: Man United set to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach: Club make formal approach to US Soccer after agreeing personal terms - with Michael Carrick's exit to be confirmed TOMORROW
Sports.content:
Manchester United are set to name Mauricio Pochettino as head coach to replace Michael Carrick following a day of talks over both men. United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer. Meanwhile, the club’s chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew back from Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was expected to ratify their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer. Carrick’s departure could be confirmed on Thursday, but official confirmation of Pochettino’s appointment may take a little longer with more talks planned overnight on Wednesday. Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday. It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games, with United said to be relaxed over the Argentine taking the team. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester. Manchester United are set to name Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager - but he took training as usual on Wednesday Pochettino, who has managed Southampton,Tottenham, and Chelsea, will succeed Michael Carrick Carrick checked in at Carrington at 7.45am on Wednesday with his fate in the balance He was pictured leaving Manchester United's training base at around 1.15pm Pochettino is pictured working on United States national team duty on Tuesday (Source: X/USMNT) The second leg is Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and Pochettino may even would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later. It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave. It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill. The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m. The 54-year-old only signed a new deal after the World Cup meaning that United could have got him for nothing in the summer. Amid the secret talks between United and Pochettino’s camp on Wednesday, there was more intrigue when the federation cancelled media access to the players at late notice but allowed cameras to film an open training session. Sources said the decision was made out of respect for Veterans Day in America, but it also meant the players didn’t have to field any awkward questions over their coach’s future. Bournemouth midfielder Tyler Adams was quoted by the US media as saying: ‘Why would his name not be on it (United’s list)? Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are meeting in Monaco for talks today The United execs meet in Monaco today (Pictured is the Casino Monte-Carlo in Monaco)

Your browser does not support iframes.

‘I mean, the credibility, the resume speaks for itself. It goes to show for us how lucky we are to be able to work under a manager of his quality and the person he is.’ Meanwhile, Berrada and Wilcox flew back to Manchester from Nice on Wednesday with United expected to announce Carrick’s departure imminently after 10 months in charge. The 45-year-old took training at Carrington for the second day running, arriving at 7.45am and leaving shortly after 1.30pm. However, it has been clear for some days that Carrick would lose his job after United dropped into the relegation zone following the club’s worst start in 40 years.

Sports.title: Astonishing moment UFC star is brutally 'attacked' by a rival while filming an interview at a hotel, leaving him battered and bruised just days before his next fight
Sports.content:
UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was left bloodied after claiming rival Usman Nurmagomedov attacked him in a hotel while he was filming an interview.

Dvalishvili is set to fight on Saturday in Abu Dhabi, and had described preparations as 'a normal fight week'.

That, though, has now been thrown out the window, with Dvalishvili claiming footage showing him getting jumped portrayed Nurmagomedov and his brother, Umar, alongside their friends, attacking him.

The group appeared to approach Dvalishvili, 35, from behind, before one man said a couple of words to him and punched him in the face.

Dvalishvili was rocked, then kicked, and was held back by a man he appeared to be with.

He tried to fight back, but a number of men overwhelmed him as his companion was attacked too.

WARNING: Graphic content

🚨DEVELOPING: Multiple angles have been released of Merab Dvalishvili getting JUMPED by Usman Nurmagomedov, Tagir Ulanbekov and their crew in Abu Dhabi. 😳



Merab was in the middle of filming an interview when Usman and his crew just walked up and openly started assaulting him. pic.twitter.com/eFVWq9S5gW — Parry Punch (@ParryPunchNews) November 11, 2026

UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was attacked in a hotel - blaming rival Usman Nurmagomedov (Instagram/merab.dvalishvili)

The 35-year-old was blind sided while carrying out an interview ahead of his fight this weekend (Instagram/merab.dvalishvili)

Eventually, the groups were separated, and Dvalishvili took to social media to respond to the incident.

He said in a video, bloody and bruised as he received treatment: 'What a sneaky way guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? If you want to fight, let's do it the real way.

'You guys came when there was two of us, you were prepared. What the f***.'

His companion then added: 'From behind? You call yourselves men? You're a little b***h.'

Dvalishvili continued: 'You are sneaky guys. You are not real men. It shows your guys' character, what the f*** guys? If you want to fight, let's fight. We are fighters. I talk straight, but you guys came from behind. I don't know how many guys, all your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way, wow.

'I knew guys, I knew what kind of guys you were. Usman, Umar and his friends came sneaky from behind, so many guys. Wow. I am fine guys. All my friends and family, I am f***ing fine. I am a fighter. This is nothing for me, but it shows what kind of people you guys are. P***ys do this bro. We are warriors.'

Dvalishvili and the Nurmagomedovs have been rivals for over a year now, with the Georgian-American facing Umar Nurmagomedov at UFC311 in January 2025.

After a heated build-up, Dvalishvili won via unanimous decision, but they have butted heads again in recent months.

Dvalishvili branded the attackers 'sneaky guys' after the ambush (Instagram/merab.dvalishvili)

The Georgian-American fought Umar Nurmagomedov at UFC311 in January 2025, coming out victorious

Dvalishvili said in a separate post on social media: 'So funny, my young friend, he is only 21 years old, a wrestler from Georgia. He was with me and he fought both brothers, Usman and Umar, and he only has this face, nothing else. He said I'm moving to MMA, if they can do only this to me, two guys...

'Oh my God bro, security was holding me, and they were kicking and punching us, and what the heck. Life is good, guys, everything is good.'

Sports.title: Man United legend Peter Schmeichel fumes over club's 'very disrespectful' treatment of Michael Carrick as Mauricio Pochettino closes in on Old Trafford job
Sports.content:
Peter Schmeichel has hit out at the 'very disrespectful' way that he believes beleaguered Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is being treated as he awaits his sacking at Old Trafford. The former club captain has endured a torrid start to the season, and while the Man United hierarchy publicly backed him as recently as three weeks ago, Carrick is now set to be handed his marching orders following a crisis summit in Monaco. Man United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to the Principality to meet with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to ratify the decision to move on from Carrick, with current USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed in his wake. But with Carrick still taking team training at Carrington while plans for his ejection from the club made global headlines, Schmeichel admitted he felt deep sympathy for the former midfielder's awkward position. 'I think the way this is playing out is very disrespectful to him,' Schmeichel said on The Overlap Daily. 'If I’m honest, I don’t think he’s doing anything wrong. Michael Carrick remains in limbo at Manchester United after a shocking start to the season Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have been in Monaco discussing his dismissal this week

Your browser does not support iframes.

'I know the team that he’s in charge of is where they are in the table, but I don’t put all of that on him. There are so many things that have been going on at Manchester United literally since Alex (Ferguson) and (former chief executive) David Gill left the club. And it’s never been corrected. 'It’s not been the correct people, not the right people in charge, and slowly it’s just gone worse.' Man United sit within the relegation zone as this international break plays out, with Carrick's men winless in the Premier League since late August. Last-minute comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in domestic action however may have briefly boosted morale at Old Trafford. But to Schmeichel, the issue lies at the feet of those who recruit at the club, rather than Carrick himself. 'If you think about this transfer window now, it’s abundantly clear to everyone - everyone who knows just a little bit about football - that Manchester United needed defenders,' he continued. 'They got through a whole transfer window without signing a single defender. 'There was a little bit of talk about Lewis Hall joining the club or going for Lewis Hall. That didn’t happen. And so, they bought three midfield players. And we know, because we’ve been in the game for so many years, that you can’t win games - if you concede 30 goals in 10 games, then there is a problem, and that was not addressed. 'Now, was Michael Carrick in on those decisions? Well, it took them forever, forever, to give him the job. So, I suspect he wasn’t in any of those discussions about who to sign up until the point he got named as manager. Former Man United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel believes the club's treatment of Carrick has been demeaning The under-fire manager turned up to take training for a second day in a row as speculation swirled over his future

Your browser does not support iframes.

'So yes, I do feel a lot of sympathy for Michael. I think what is happening is wrong. I think we should stick with Michael. I think we should just try and steady the ship a little bit and then get into January and then sign the players that he feels he needs to bring the team forward and then be realistic about what this season is all about. Obviously, it’s about climbing as high as Manchester United can in the table.' By contrast, Schmeichel's co-pundit Tim Sherwood said he did not feel sorry for Carrick, because he will have understood the brutal situation he was stepping into at Man United. The former Middlesbrough head coach served as interim manager for the second-half of the previous season following the sacking of Ruben Amorim, and was named on a permanent basis over the summer. But while Schmeichel admitted that the life cycle of a Premier League coach was undeniably short, his issue is with the manner of treatment Carrick has received in the process of the changing of the guard in the dugout. 'If they’re looking for somebody else, then relieve the man of his duties,' the former goalkeeper argued. 'Don’t let him come into training yesterday. He took training yesterday. How disrespectful is that? 'How do you think this fella – I mean, he’s a human being. He’s a very, very good human being. He’s one of the nicest people you’ll ever meet in your life, and obviously you two know him well. So, treat the guy with respect. Tell him, "Sorry, mate. We don’t think that you are the future here. Here’s a cheque. Move on." But they’re not doing that. They’re dragging it out.' Schmeichel was incensed too by Carrick's status within the club, wondering aloud whether, since they had taken 'weeks and weeks' to come to their messy, public decision, the club's hierarchy might not really understand what it is to truly represent the club. 'Do you think these people know? Do you think they care?' Schmeichel continued. 'These people are not Manchester United people. 'They don’t understand what it’s like to be one of the Manchester United people. They don’t know that. This is obviously part of the broader issue here, part of the reason the club is where they are now. I’m not saying I feel sorry for Michael, but I’m a little bit angry at how this great football club is treating one of its greatest players. Simple as that.' Talks have been planned with Pochettino overnight on Wednesday, with the club's hierarchy thought to be preparing to dismiss Carrick face-to-face on Thursday. Mauricio Pochettino remains locked in talks to take over at Old Trafford as the club's preferred candidate for the role

Your browser does not support iframes.

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday. It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester. The second leg in Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and it seems inconceivable that Pochettino would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later. It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave. It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill. The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m. Meanwhile in Manchester, Carrick took training for the second day in a row at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday, arriving at 7.45am and departing shortly after 1.30pm. Carrick has overseen the club's worst start to the season in 40 years, but the man himself remained adamant that he would not be falling on his sword after battling back to claim a draw against Villa. In an awkward interview with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick remained steadfast in the face of questions as to whether he would quit his role amid the turbulence. 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games,' he said. 'But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola 'set to be made top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino as United States boss' as ex-Spurs manager closes in on Man United job
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola 'set to be made top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino as United States boss' as ex-Spurs manager closes in on Man United job

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola will be the United States' top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino if and when their manager joins Manchester United, according to a report.

It is looking more and more likely that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will take over from Michael Carrick at Old Trafford in the coming days.

Pochettino is currently with his United States Men's National Team players ahead of their fixtures against Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League this fortnight, but is expected to join up with United after those games.

That will leave the United States needing a new boss and, according to The Athletic, they will set their sights on Guardiola.

The Spaniard is renowned as one of the best managers around, having won the Champions League and six Premier League titles while with City.

He also has historic success with Bayern Munich and Barcelona, and has previously shown interest in potentially moving into international football.

The United States are reportedly set to make Pep Guardiola (pictured) their top target to replace Mauricio Pochettino as manager

Pochettino (right) is set to leave his role at the USMNT to take over at Manchester United

As recently as the summer, Guardiola came so close to being appointed Italy manager that he was 'writing down line-ups' before ultimately deciding not to take the role on.

He was touted to take over an under-performing Italian national team, but the move fell through, and Italian Football Federation technical director and defensive legend Paolo Maldini resigned after a move to appoint Andrea Pirlo also collapsed due to his commercial links with a Russian betting company.

Maldini opened up on how close Guardiola came to taking over the team, revealing that the Spaniard was seemingly on board for a pretty long time.

'(Guardiola) is the coach who best embodies technical, attacking football,' Maldini told Corriere della Sera. 'He had expressed the idea of wanting to coach a national team to some friends.

'We went to meet him in Barcelona, we had lunch together, we talked for an entire day.

'He was very tempted. He came very close to accepting. He even started writing line-ups down on sheets of paper.'

It is reported that Guardiola has spoken to officials at the US national side in the past and is intrigued by working in America. He lived in New York briefly after leaving Barcelona in 2012.

He is said to have been approached in 2024 before Pochettino was appointed, and wished the Argentine well upon his appointment.

Pochettino is currently away with the States but is likely to join United in the coming days

He said: 'I wish him and the USA - I have friends there - the best of luck. I know he's a top-class manager.'

He has also been previously quoted as saying: 'The USA is fascinating to try and build a project for many years and being able to get the national team to the next step. The potential with the USA is there for the amount of people and sports and so on.'

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were in Monaco where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was expected to ratify their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick's departure could be confirmed on Thursday, but official confirmation of Pochettino's appointment may take a little longer with more talks planned overnight on Wednesday.

Sports.title: Why Brittany Mahomes' baby news means the Chiefs will make the Super Bowl: Eagle-eyed fans spot eerie trend that could propel Patrick all the way
Sports.content:
Correlation does not imply causation, but that won't stop Kansas City Chiefs fans from pinning their Super Bowl hopes on Patrick Mahomes' growing family.

The three-time Super Bowl MVP's wife Brittany is now pregnant with their fourth child, and as several Chiefs supporters were quick to point out on X, her previous three pregnancies all included a trip to the Super Bowl.

Brittany was pregnant with daughter Sterling Skye, son Bronze and daughter Golden Raye during Super Bowls in 2021, 2023 and 2025, respectively. Of course, Kansas City has reached five Super Bowls since the start of the 2019 season, so the odds of Brittany being pregnant at the biggest spectacle in sports were favorable to say the least.

'I’m going to need them to have around 10 more kids,' one fan joked on X.

It wasn't just fans who noticed the trend. Even Patrick admitted to banking on another Super Bowl berth with an expecting wife watching from the stands.

'I'm hoping,' Mahomes said. 'I don't know if Brittany is, but I'm hoping we can keep that going and get another Super Bowl win with a baby on the way.'

Brittany Mahomes was expecting in 2023 when she watched the Chiefs' Super Bowl LVII win

Patrick Mahomes and his wife Brittany have announced they are expecting their fourth child

Mahomes hopes to see his expecting wife at Super Bowl LXI, but admits she may not want to

The news isn't all good for the Chiefs. As several fans noted, Kansas City is only 1-3 in the Super Bowl when Brittany is with child.

Currently the Chiefs are 6-2 on the season, despite a barrage of injuries at receiver. Andy Reid's team travels to Atlanta on Sunday to face the 3-6 Falcons.

The couple made the announcement on Tuesday evening, posting a series of photographs on Instagram alongside the caption: 'Another blessing from God... and then there were six.'

Chiefs superstar Patrick Mahomes is already a father to two daughters, Sterling Skye, five, and Golden Raye, one, and a son, three-year-old Patrick 'Bronze' Lavon Mahomes III.

In the family photoshoot, Patrick and his three children are seen putting their hands on Brittany's bump on the beach. The surprise announcement, which sparked an avalanche of well-wishes on social media, comes barely 18 months after Brittany suggested they might not have any more children.

'We're done, we're done for a while,' she said in June 2025. 'I don't know... I feel like you can never say you're done. I think three is all I need.'

The couple made the announcement on Tuesday, posting a series of pictures on Instagram

The couple, who have become close friends with Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift, tied the knot in 2022 after a decade together.

'Being a mom changed so many things in my life and changed how I looked at so many things,' Brittany told Yahoo in June. 'It really reshaped and redefined a lot of things in my life.'

She added: 'It's made me more intentional, more purposeful and, honestly, more motivated to keep going and keep showing my kids that there are no boundaries in front of you.

'You can achieve anything. You can be a part of anything that you want to. You need to dream big and understand that you have to work hard and do the hard things to do the fun things.'

Just minutes before revealing the news on Tuesday, both Patrick and Brittany Mahomes had posted about the Kansas City Chiefs trading for wide receiver Josh Downs ahead of the NFL's deadline.

The Chiefs superstar recently returned to the field after suffering damage to his ACL and LCL in a game against the Los Angeles Chargers last December.

The Chiefs star is already a father to two daughters - Sterling and Golden - and one son Bronze

The news comes 18 months after Brittany suggested they might not have any more children

The three-time Super Bowl champion went under the knife and then challenged himself to be back on his feet before his daughter, Golden, had learned to walk.

Brittany, a former soccer player who co-owns the Kansas City Current, has been by her husband's side throughout his career.

Following the Chiefs' recent loss to the Denver Broncos, she accused NFL referees of deliberately making calls against Kansas City in a blistering social media meltdown.

Mahomes and his teammates suffered a heartbreaking loss on the road after lineman Jaylon Moore was penalized for a false start that ruled out a game-winning touchdown pass to Rashee Rice.

The penalty forced the Chiefs back to the six-yard line and Mahomes was sacked on fourth-and-goal, handing the Broncos a wild 28-24 win, and Kansas City's second loss of the season.

'You can't tell me you call that on a game winning [touchdown],' Brittany posted to her 2.1 million social media followers. 'Oh wait yeah I can cause it's us. That was the weakest call I have ever seen, you can't tell me otherwise.'

Sports.title: Harry Kane is annoyed at his '50-50' England team-mates who pull out of international duty, reveals Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has revealed that Harry Kane is annoyed by team-mates who pull out of England squads – and says his captain would never do so.

Several of the head coach’s camps have been blighted by withdrawals, including Cole Palmer’s ‘load management’ excuse in September. The Chelsea playmaker was then left out of the squad for this week’s Nations League fixtures.

And Tuchel says Kane, who will become England’s record cap-holder with his 126th appearance against Croatia on Thursday evening, is not a fan of those who pass up the opportunity to play for their country.

‘He is always here and doesn’t like it if 50-50 decisions are taken by the players not to come to camp,’ said Tuchel.

‘We had this conversation very early when I took the job and it was one of his points, to make sure that players come and are proud to arrive because it’s the biggest honour.

‘We need to make sure that if it happens (withdrawals) we are so strong that we actually set the tone that everybody is desperate to be in camp, because everybody can lose their shirt if they miss out on a camp.

Thomas Tuchel (centre) has revealed Harry Kane's frustrations at his team-mates pulling out the England squad

Cole Palmer (right), pictured with Kane in 2024, has been criticised by Tuchel for missing too many England opportunities

‘So it was one of the first discussions and straight away he set the standard and made it very clear where the standards are for him. He would never pull out. Never.’

Kane, meanwhile, says his desire burns brighter than ever as he targets 100 England goals and records that will stand for generations.

He insists he is far from finished and has warned team-mates Declan Rice and Jude Bellingham that his caps record could yet reach 150.

‘This is no time to rest,’ said Kane. ‘I've got better year on year. While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

‘Jude and Dec, they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are. So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! Before we know it, it’ll be the home Euros. I might be on 140 caps by then, and then we'll be talking about 150. My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I have an ego to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential: Why Will Wright is the breakout star of Reds academy - LEWIS STEELE reveals club's plans for 6ft 3in hat-trick hero, his rise from Euxton Villa to Anfield and why coaches believe he's Andoni Iraola's next big thing
Sports.content:
Liverpool Confidential: Why Will Wright is the breakout star of Reds academy - LEWIS STEELE reveals club's plans for 6ft 3in hat-trick hero, his rise from Euxton Villa to Anfield and why coaches believe he's Andoni Iraola's next big thing

On Will Wright’s last two trips abroad, he has needed to check in some extra baggage on the return flight.

Two UEFA Youth League away games, two hat-tricks and a pair of match balls to go with them. It’s now 13 goals for the season for 18-year-old Wright after his treble in a 5-3 win at Fenerbahce last week, and he has earned a first England youth call-up to boot.

Another hat-trick in one of those three games for the Young Lions? You wouldn’t bet against it – but Wright is used to these rapid rises.

Eighteen months ago, the 6ft 3in striker signed for Liverpool on a Friday, passed his driving test at 8am the next morning and then played for the first team the day after in a friendly at Anfield.

Now, the former Salford City striker is the name on everyone’s lips around Kirkby – with many thinking he could be the next cab off the rank from Liverpool’s famed academy.

So who is he – and how high can he go?

Will Wright has lit up the academy goal charts this season for Liverpool, scoring a pair of hat-tricks in the UEFA Youth League

The Under 19s captain struck a brilliant treble against Fenerbahce last week to take his season tally to 13

Wright was first spotted by Salford scouts when playing for local side Euxton Villa, a ninth-tier club who have two England internationals among their alumni in David Unsworth and Sam Johnstone. Wright’s father, Mark, coached at Euxton and is an ex-professional for Preston North End.

It was an unusual path as most future stars are normally signed up by their mid-teens but Wright had injury issues amid a growth spurt that took him to the lanky frame that now bullies defenders. He had heel issues and has worked with a specialist on fascia problems.

Wright made his Salford debut in an 8-0 FA Cup defeat by Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City in January 2025 but scouts had already been alerted by his 50-goal haul at youth level. Arsenal, led by then-academy chief Per Mertesacker, launched an aggressive approach to sign him.

At one point, Liverpool signalled to Wright and Salford that they were pulling out of the deal, given Arsenal’s interest was so advanced. But the Reds soon returned to prevent the Gunners signing their next ‘Wrighty’.

The deal was worth peanuts in the grand scheme of things, around £300,000. It is good money for League Two Salford, though, and they will be set for additional payments for first-team appearances, honours and future national team caps.

Wright, who has a younger brother and is a Nike athlete, is a throwback No9. It is easy to reach for comparisons to current players but the way he combines pace, power and prolific finishing is not too dissimilar to Erling Haaland.

He is a strong dribbler and scored a fantastic solo goal for Liverpool's Under 21s against Rochdale in the EFL Trophy in September, receiving possession on the touchline around halfway, tricking his way past two defenders and curling a sumptuous effort into the top corner.

He is the captain of the Under 19s team and I have watched him play live several times, including one game last season where he was clearly targeted by Atletico Madrid defenders. The striker was clattered, suffered a medial ligament injury and was sidelined for several months.

He is a strong dribbler and scored a fantastic solo goal for Liverpool's Under 21s against Rochdale in the EFL Trophy in September

Coaches have pinpointed hold-up play and heading as two things to work on, as well as instructing Wright not to ‘rise to the bait’ of bigger defenders who might try to ruffle him up

He has returned with a vengeance, with a hat-trick against LASK last month and then last week's effort against Fenerbahce. What impressed more in the latter was not his goals – one a penalty, the other two both true poachers’ finishes – but his assist.

Wright was on a hat-trick at the time but, instead of shooting, he played a ball to Finn Inglethorpe – son of academy director Alex – to score. Earlier, Wright and Josh Sonni-Lambie had argued over who was to take a penalty. Wright won the row and scored.

Under 21s boss Rob Page told the pair later that he would rather them show hunger to score and passion rather than shy away. Page is a huge fan of Wright and said: ‘There was a real maturity about his performance. One of the parts of the development for all the forwards is being unselfish in their actions.

‘As much as he wants to see the headlines and be successful himself, it is all about sharing that. Will has done that really well today with a hat-trick, a complete performance.’

Pressed on how far away Wright is from the first team, Page replied: ‘He doesn’t have to worry about that. Just bring the best version of yourself every day in training, give absolutely everything in games as he does. The rest will take care of itself.

‘He’s got a great support around him. His family are very supportive. Alex (Inglethorpe) is there to lean on, he’s got myself and Jay (Spearing, academy coach). He never gets carried away.’

Coaches have pinpointed hold-up play and heading as two things to work on, as well as instructing Wright not to ‘rise to the bait’ of bigger defenders who might try to ruffle him up. They have also worked on his off-the-ball runs to the back post.

So, what next? It is understood a January loan is being considered. Liverpool think toughening up Wright in a senior league could be a step worth taking, having used him in each of the last two pre-seasons. His agent was at the AXA Training Centre on Tuesday and there will be no shortage of clubs willing to take him on.

Liverpool think toughening up Wright in a senior league could be a step worth taking, having used him in each of the last two pre-seasons

Wright got six minutes off the bench against Como in a friendly at Anfield in August, coming on for Alexander Isak up front

Andoni Iraola will be consulted, too. He has called up the likes of Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and Luke Chambers this season and is eager to use young stars.

Iraola is in frequent dialogue with youth staff such as Page, Inglethorpe, plus Luiz Fernando Iubel who is often cited as the ‘link’ between the academy and first team.

The Brazilian has been spotted at several academy games this term, including for Wright’s hat-trick in Turkey where Iubel sat alongside sporting director Julian Ward and loans manager Gary Probert.

Whether a first-team breakthrough comes now or in the future, the future for Wright looks bright.

Van Dijk out, Szoboszlai to follow?

Dominik Szoboszlai’s participation with Hungary this week remains in the balance with the national team doing all they can to get their captain fit for crunch games.

The Hungarians take on Georgia and Northern Ireland in must-win Nations League matches – and may have to go without their star man. Szoboszlai hurt his knee in the win at Crystal Palace and, after an injury-hit six weeks, could do with a rest.

But he will try his best to be fit for national team duty and a decision will not be made until the 11th hour.

It comes after Virgil van Dijk pulled out of Dutch duty with a minor muscle issue. It is believed he has been managing the problem for at least a month and was surprised to be substituted on to the field against LASK — which might explain the team conceding three after he came on!

Virgil van Dijk (left) has pulled out of international duty and Dominik Szoboszlai (right) could be set to follow him

Loan watch: Harvey’s back!

Confidential readers will recall our musings on Harvey Elliott a fortnight ago, with Valencia sources telling us that the La Liga outfit might consider cancelling his loan in January.

The English midfielder had struggled in Spain for fitness and form. He was then sent off against Villarreal but, as we reported, Valencia would give him another chance to prove his worth.

He has started well, scoring a free-kick in what was his first start for any club in 285 days. It was part of a notable 6-0 win in the Copa del Rey.

Elliott ran over to fans and put his arms aloft appearing to apologise, which adds to his comments a week ago about the red card where he said: ‘I made a mistake and I’m truly sorry. It won’t happen again.’

Sports.title: HARRY KANE INTERVIEW: England captain opens up on having an 'ego', the secret behind Ballon d'Or glory, the 'tough' moments with his country - and why he isn't finished yet
Sports.content:
Harry Kane is contemplating his ego. England’s humble superstar, believes the outside world at least, does not have one. He laughs when reminded of his endearing habit of fiddling with his suit buttons during his Ballon d’Or acceptance speech.

But there must, surely, be one example beneath the modest exterior when he descends into a diva?

‘That's a great question. I’m sure my wife will be able to say a thing or two!’ he returns. ‘But ego is funny, because ego is many different things. I guess I have an ego to be the best, because I want to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

Kane does have an ego, only it is measured in goals and self-improvement, not vanity and self-indulgence. He has the records because he wants the records, and he wants them more than all of his rivals. He played more games and scored more goals than Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal last season. After his 126th cap against Croatia tonight, he would have played more games and scored more goals than any player in England’s history. He wants those records to stand, too. Ego, you see.

‘Jude (Bellingham) and Declan (Rice), they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are,’ says Kane, as we chat at England’s base at the Tottenham Hotspur training ground. ‘So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! The goal record (currently 91) is going to be the one that's difficult to beat. I think that’s good!’

It’s better than good, Harry. It is hard to believe now, but Kane was billed as a one-season wonder after his 31-goal breakthrough campaign at Tottenham 11 years ago. He remembers that, just like he does rejection by Arsenal aged eight years old, his missed penalty against France at World Cup 2022, the loan spell at Norwich when he was demoted to the reserves and the loan at Leicester when he sat alone in his flat and wondered if he was good enough for the Premier League.

England captain Harry Kane has admitted he has 'an ego to be the best' after winning the Ballon d'Or

‘I’ve had to prove people wrong my whole career,’ he says. 'If someone tells me I can’t do something, it motivates me to do it more. You look at all the great athletes, Tom Brady and that unwavering mentality to be the best. Maybe with me, because I’m a calm person and you don’t see the ego of some of these great players, it doesn’t mean I don’t want it as much as everyone else. It doesn’t mean I don’t put in the work and drive myself and everyone around me to be the best.

‘Getting released that early (by Arsenal) and proving them wrong. Proving my early coaches at Tottenham wrong, who I wasn’t playing as much under. Loan moves that didn’t go well. The World Cup in Qatar, missing that penalty was a really tough moment for me. After that, I scored the next 30 penalties! It’s the same thing, “I’m going to show them”, using all the negative stuff as motivation to push me to another level.’

Then there was Euro 2024, when Kane was substituted in the final defeat by Spain after an hour. The popular opinion went that his best days were behind him and England needed a new striker. He has since scored 25 goals from 27 international games. So much for the decline.

‘It was tough, getting taken off in a final,’ he says. ‘There was so much talk (before the final) around, “Maybe Harry shouldn't start”. I was like, “Well hang on a minute, I'm doing my best for the team here”.

‘I scored three goals and was joint for the Golden Boot. It wasn't like there were many other players doing crazy stuff that I wasn't doing. But from my own standards, I know I probably didn't quite reach the level that I could have. I don't think the team reached the level that we could have. After that, my position was under pressure. That motivated me to make sure that it wasn't. I was going to have to do even more to keep my place. From that moment, you've seen an improvement in me.’

Spend time with Kane, even just half an hour, and you realise he isn’t done yet.

’In football, you’ve never completed it,’ says the Bayern Munich star. ‘No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has. This is no time to rest. If anything, I've got better year on year, and the numbers have got better. While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I'm just on the back of scoring 73 goals in one year, which is incredible, and I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

‘My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I want to make sure that I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that, whenever that day comes, I can say, “I’ve done everything possible. I have this record, I don’t have this record, but it doesn’t matter, I can sleep well at night”.’

You could never accuse Kane of not giving his all. His ego, the best kind of ego, would never allow anything else. England's greatest player is the diva who makes only demands of himself.

Sports.title: Merab Dvalishvili shares gruesome injuries after Usman Nurmagomedov attack in interview
Sports.content:
Merab Dvalishvili shares gruesome injuries after Usman Nurmagomedov attack in interview

GRAPHIC CONTENT - Merab Dvalishvili was left with a bloody face after he was attacked by Usman Nurmagomedov during an interview ahead of RAF Abu Dhabi

View 5 Images Merab Dvalishvili was slapped by Usman Nurmagomedov (Image: @ChampRDS/X)

Merab Dvalishvili was left with a bloodied face following a brawl with Usman Nurmagomedov and his crew in a hotel lobby on Wednesday.

‌



‌



The Georgian UFC talent was conducting an interview ahead of Saturday's RAF Abu Dhabi, where he is set to take on Marlon Moraes in a catchweight freestyle wrestling match-up, when Usman and a group of friends approached him from behind.

‌



A short exchange of words occurred before Nurmagomedov slapped Dvalishvili in the face, sparking an all-out brawl between the two sets of camps. Video footage captured and uploaded to social media show punches and kicks flying as security work to diffuse the situation.

‌



At one point, Dvalishvili is also picked up and slammed to the ground by a member of Nurmagomedov's team, before quickly springing back to his feet and continuing to defend himself. A small fracas also ensued between Dvalishvili and Nurmagomedov, with the Georgian taking a knee to the face as bystanders call for security.

Crowd erupts into violence at Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson boxing clash READ MORE :

Now, Dvalishvili has uploaded a statement to social media giving his side of the story. He wrote: "Was doing an interview for RAF in hotel lobby and Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend. Security was holding me - They kept kicking us when we were down like losers."

The accompanying footage shows Dvalishvili bloody faced and receiving medical treatment, as he rants: "What a sneaky way guys? Just two of us, me and my friend came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman Nurmagomedov and his friends came like snakes from behind.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"What kind of fighters you guys are? What kind of man does this, bro? If you want to talk fight, let's do it the real way, bro. You guys came from...There's just two of us and you guys were prepared, bro. What the f***?"

‌



Dvalishvili's friend, Saba Lazishvili, who helped him fight off Nurmagomedov's crew, was also spotted in the video with a cut below his right eye and contusions on his forehead from the incident. He said: "From behind. Who does that? You call yourselves men? You are little b****."

View 5 Images Merab Dvalishvili and his friend fought off a group of Usman Nurmagomedov's pals (Image: @ChampRDS/X)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Dvalishvili then added: "We bleed, we fight, we war, but you guys are just sneaky guys, bro. You guys are not real men. That shows your guys' character, shows you guys aren't real men.

‌



"What the f*** guys? If you want to fight, fight. Let's f***ing fight. We are fighters, bro. I talk. I'm a real guy, I talk straight. But you guys came from behind bro. I don't know how many guys you was. All of your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way.

WARNING: GRAPHIC CONTENT

‌



5 View 5 Images The brawl broke out in a hotel lobby (Image: @ChampRDS/X) 5 View 5 Images Merab Dvalishvili was left with a bloody face (Image: Instagram)

‌



"Wow. I knew what kind of guys you are. I just came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman, Umar (Nurmagomedov's brother) and his friends came from behind and tried to beat us. So many guys. I'm fine guys. All my friends and family, I'm f***ing fine."

It is unknown as to whether Dvalishvili's planned match with Moraes will go ahead as planned as a result of the altercation, as well as the injuries sustained as a result. Umar Nurmagomedov, who Dvalishvili also claims was involved in the brawl, is also set to take on UFC legend, Urijah Faber at lightweight on the same card.

‌



It comes just a matter of months after Dvalishvili slapped Umar's friend, Akhmed Gadzhimagomedov, backstage after RAF Georgia. Dvalishvili, who had beaten Henry Cejudo in a freestyle wrestling match that evening, had shut down talks of a bout between himself and Umar.

Gadzhimagomedov then approached him to confront him about his comments, with Dvalishvili responding by slapping the Dagestani - leading to a similar scrap between camps. Speaking with Ariel Helwani, Dvalishvili explained his reasoning for the slap.

‌



View 5 Images Merab Dvalishvili is supposed to wrestle on Saturday evening (Image: @ChampRDS/X)

He said: "I was super relaxed, super chilled and then somebody came and grabbed my neck and pulled me over and started yelling at me in Russian language, which I hardly understand. And he mentioned Umar.

Article continues below

"It took me a couple of seconds to realise, 'Who is this guy to tell me what to talk about him? It's between me and Umar.' I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters.

"The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan [Magomedov]. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads."

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola thrust into Man Utd manager saga after being made 'top target'
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola thrust into Man Utd manager saga after being made 'top target'

The USA are set to see Mauricio Pochettino leave for Manchester United but have set their sights on Pep Guardiola as his replacement

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola has the chance to make a swift return to management (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

The USA will make Pep Guardiola their top target if, as is expected, Mauricio Pochettino leaves his role and heads to Manchester United.

‌



‌



The Argentine is set to take over from Michael Carrick with the Premier League side already striking an agreement to buy him out of his contract with US Soccer.

‌



As a result those in the States have been drawing up a list of candidates to replace Pochettino and Guardiola, who left Manchester City in the summer, is their ideal candidate, reports the Athletic, and has already been discussed internally.

‌



The Catalan has already turned down the opportunity of a swift return to management with Italy showing an interest in him, only to be rejected by the former City boss. Italian chief Giovanni Malago told La Repubblica: “Pep was honest. He took a sabbatical, partly for family reasons, but if he’d done anything, he would have done it with us.”

‌



Guardiola has had dialogue with US Soccer in the past and has history in America. He lived in New York City during a year-long sabbatical after he left Barcelona in 2012, living in a luxury apartment close to Central Park with his family.

Guardiola has also previously said: “The USA is fascinating to try to build a project for many years and being able to get the national team to the next step. The potential with the USA is there for the amount of people and sports and so on.”

‌



US Soccer contacted Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp at the beginning of the federation’s last managerial search, which ended with the hiring of Pochettino in 2024.

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino is set to leave his role as head coach of the United States (Image: Charlotte Wilson/Getty Images)

‌



The Argentine is now poised for a return to the Premier League, where he's previously coached Tottenham and then Chelsea. In north London he saw his stock rise and that's when he was first linked with a move to Manchester, but he was overlooked for the role in 2018 as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer got the gig.

Since then he won the first honours of his managerial career, doing so at PSG. He led the USA in their home World Cup in the summer, but they were knocked out by Belgium in the Round of 16.

Article continues below

Pochettino is set to oversee the USA's two upcoming games, both against Haiti, and that would delay his move to Old Trafford, where he is due to replace Michael Carrick.

Sports.title: What Mauricio Pochettino told USA team as Man Utd braced for frustration with new boss
Sports.content:
What Mauricio Pochettino told USA team as Man Utd braced for frustration with new boss

Mauricio Pochettino has carried on with his job with the USA as he prepares for their upcoming games - which could now delay his arrival at Manchester United.

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino is set to leave the US for Manchester (Image: Getty Images)

Mauricio Pochettino is still poised to take charge of the USA during the international break despite an agreement being struck with Manchester United.

‌



‌



That means that the Argentine may not report for duty at Old Trafford until the international break comes to an end, putting the Red Devils on the back foot from minute one. United have now taken the first step to arrange paying the compensation fee that would land Pochettino, with an announcement expected imminently.

‌



The international break is often an opportune time for clubs who are struggling to change manager because it can afford the new man in charge almost a fortnight of preparation time. But the Athletic reports that Pochettino is set to see out this set of games with the USA, with United bosses relaxed about that arrangement.

‌



They will play Haiti twice, with both games on American soil after the Haitians had their home game moved for security reasons. But ahead of the outings Pochettino did little to change the focus of his players despite the United links being so well publicised.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



When he spoke to players and staff to begin training he discussed the day’s session, the three Under-20 players who’d joined the group for the day, and other matters, none of which related to the Premier League side.

Defender Chris Richards said: “It’s kinda been business as usual here. He acknowledged that he and team-mates had seen “all the reports and stuff,” but “we’ve just kept our head down. We’re training and playing like we don’t hear anything.

‌



“We’re training like he’s going to be the coach tomorrow, because we don’t know what’s gonna happen or what’s not gonna happen. If you focus too much on what could happen, you won’t be able to really focus on what is happening.”

US Soccer does not have an easy way to replace Pochettino ahead of games on Saturday and Tuesday. The US will play a “home-and-home” with Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League, starting with Saturday's game in Miami. They will then play the same opponents on Tuesday in Cincinnati in the second leg of the series.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick is set to receive his marching orders (Image: Getty Images)

If United were to insist Pochettino and his staff, which includes long-time assistant Jesus Perez, depart as soon as buyout terms are agreed, it would put US Soccer bosses in a very difficult position.

‌



It leaves United in a difficult situation, largely of their own making. Carrick is yet to be formally dismissed, yet his imminent sacking his common knowledge. A £7million agreement with US Soccer to have Pochettino is agreed, but the club face the prospect of having no head coach to lead the players when they return after their scheduled time off.

That would be another damning reflection on the United hierarchy, who have known for weeks that Carrick is in troubled waters. They've been determined to stick by him, but results and performances have not improved. If it is Pochettino who takes over, then his first game will be at Liverpool off the back of just days in the role.
