World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: What could Chinese intelligence have learned from Nvidia CEO’s affair?
World.content:
Nvidia says no secrets were compromised, but experts question what sensitive information may have been exposed.

Share What could Chinese intelligence have learned from Nvidia CEO’s affair? on social media

United States lawmakers are pushing for answers from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid growing concerns over whether an affair he had compromised national security.

Huang, 63, has admitted to having extramarital relations during his time leading Nvidia, a major US tech firm. Media reports indicate the woman involved was Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based tech company Megaspeed who is accused of working for Chinese intelligence.

As the scandal continues to grip Washington, Republican leaders of three committees in the House of Representatives have asked Huang to appear at a closed-door briefing to testify about the relationship.

House Foreign Affairs Committee Chair Brian Mast said he was prepared to subpoena Huang if he did not respond by the end of Wednesday.

According to The New York Times, US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the Nvidia CEO and influence him to push for looser restrictions on chip sales to China.

In a statement on Sunday, Jensen Huang apologised to his family and Nvidia employees about the affair.

His company also launched an independent investigation, saying it had no reason to believe that “either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised”. Still, by Wednesday, media reports emerged that Nvidia was preparing to part ways with Huang over the controversy.

US President Donald Trump confirmed on Monday that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was looking into the matter, but he has stood by Huang, calling him an “honourable guy”.



But the pressure on Huang intensified on Tuesday when Republican Senator Kevin Cramer called for him to resign.

“The potential for extortion is so tremendous that something as sensitive as Nvidia chips, I just think he’s got to go,” Cramer said in an interview with Politico.

But Huang, who co-founded Nvidia more than 30 years ago, has shown no signs of heeding that call.

Despite the company’s assurances, experts say the affair raises concerns about what information Alice Huang may have been privy to and what role the relationship may have played in the Nvidia CEO’s decisions.

What are the national security concerns surrounding Nvidia?

Nvidia’s advanced chips, which power much of today’s artificial intelligence, have put the company at the centre of the race for tech dominance between China and the US.

Since 2022, Washington has restricted sales of some of the most advanced chips to China over concerns that they could be used by the country’s military or intelligence agencies.

According to US intelligence officials cited by The New York Times, Alice Huang was tasked with getting Jensen Huang to lobby for looser restrictions on chip exports.

The Nvidia CEO had already been pushing for an easing of the rules, arguing that China’s domestic chip industry would get stronger without better access to US products.

But some experts say it is worth looking at how Alice Huang may have influenced decisions Nvidia made specifically about her former employer Megaspeed, which bought more than $4.8bn worth of Nvidia chips over the span of about two years.

Megaspeed has also been investigated over allegations that it helped Chinese companies get access to restricted chips. Megaspeed denies the allegation.

Ryan Fedasiuk, a fellow at the Foundation for American Innovation who studies Chinese technology and intelligence activities, pointed to reports from Bloomberg and The New York Times that Nvidia contacted the US Commerce Department about its investigation into Megaspeed.

He also noted that, in disclosures to the government, Nvidia appeared to vastly undercount the value of the chips it sold to the company.

“The question at hand is whether Nvidia took specific actions with respect to Megaspeed that it might not otherwise have done,” Fedasiuk told Al Jazeera, “possibly as a result of the personal relationship between the two executives.”

What sensitive information could have been a risk?

There are also questions about what sensitive information Alice Huang may have had access to through her relationship with Jensen Huang.



In an analysis published by the Council on Foreign Relations, a think tank, senior fellow Jessica Brandt pointed to information about how Nvidia designs its China-specific chips.

“Information about its conversations with policymakers could be helpful for anticipating where those controls and other policies are headed,” she said. “Understanding where it disagrees with government could expose fault lines to exploit. And that’s before we get into anything touching R&D [research and development].”

Fedasiuk raised similar concerns about what Alice Huang could have learned about Nvidia’s internal operations and plans for future products, as well as its customer base, which includes American and foreign tech companies.

He also pointed to Jensen Huang’s close ties to Trump and other senior White House officials.

“I have to wonder what kind of information about those people and about those relationships may have inadvertently made its way to Ms Huang or to Chinese intelligence,” he said.

So far, however, there is no publicly available evidence that Alice Huang got access to sensitive information from Nvidia or influenced Jensen Huang’s decisions. US intelligence also has not made public any evidence that Alice Huang was working for Chinese intelligence.

China has flatly denied the allegations of espionage.

“The claim of so-called ‘Chinese spies’ is completely groundless and is nothing but a smear campaign against China,” said Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Monday.

World.title: Former Italian Red Brigades member escapes house arrest in Argentina
World.content:
Bertulazzi used a rope and harness to climb down from a fifth-floor apartment and evade authorities in Argentina.

A 74-year-old former member of Italy’s far-left Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina by climbing down from a fifth-floor apartment using a harness and rope, prompting a nationwide search.

Leonardo Bertulazzi, who faces extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence, escaped on Tuesday and was still on the run on Wednesday, Argentine police officials told The Associated Press news agency.

Bertulazzi was convicted in absentia by a court in his home country for his role in the kidnapping and death of a former Italian prime minister by the left-wing armed group, and his refugee status in Argentina was revoked under right-wing President Javier Milei.

Police said he descended onto the second-floor terrace of a neighbouring house, climbed down to a first-floor terrace, crossed a vacant lot and got onto the street by climbing over a gate.

Authorities did not immediately notice Bertulazzi was gone as he had tampered with his electronic ankle monitor, the officials said. They said he placed it inside a device containing a thermal blanket to maintain its temperature, along with grease or animal fat, apparently to keep moisture in.

Explosives specialists examined the device, which had been made to resemble an explosive.

Argentina’s Security Ministry has offered a reward of 20 million pesos (about $13,000) for information leading to his capture.

‘Years of Lead’

The Red Brigades were a far-left armed group responsible for a wave of kidnappings and killings in Italy in the 1970s and 1980s, a period known as the “Years of Lead”.



The group kidnapped and killed former Prime Minister Aldo Moro in 1978. Argentine authorities have said Bertulazzi, who belonged to the group’s Genoa branch, was involved in the logistics of Moro’s kidnapping.

Italian courts convicted him in the 1980s of “terrorism-related” crimes, resulting in a combined 27-year sentence, according to Argentine court records.

He was first arrested in Buenos Aires in November 2002, but an Argentine judge rejected Italy’s extradition request in 2003 because Italian law did not guarantee him a new trial after a conviction in absentia. He was granted refugee status in 2004.

Argentina revoked it in 2024, under Milei, and re-arrested him that August. Its Supreme Court approved his extradition last year.

Wanda Ferro, an undersecretary in Italy’s Interior Ministry, said Argentine police were responsible for ensuring he was handed over. “I am certain that every effort will be made,” she told local television, adding that she hoped the extradition could take place “very quickly” if Bertulazzi is recaptured.

World.title: Nvidia shares plunge amid reports board to discuss CEO Huang’s future
World.content:
Chip giant Nvidia’s stock price has tumbled amid reports that its board of directors is meeting to consider the future of CEO Jensen Huang.

Nvidia shares fell 8.6 percent in after-hours trading on Wednesday as questions swirled over Huang’s position at the top of the $4.2 trillion company.

The plunge comes after The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the Financial Times reported that Nvidia’s board of directors would discuss Huang’s position amid revelations he engaged in an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia employee, in addition to an affair with a woman accused of working with Chinese intelligence services.

Nvidia, which launched an investigation into Huang’s conduct on Sunday, did not immediately respond to Al Jazeera’s requests for comment.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, is one of the most visible faces of the AI boom, spearheading the development of high-end graphics processing units (GPUs) used to used to train and run frontier models.

The tech executive’s position has also placed him at the centre of the geopolitical rivalry between United States and China, which are locked in a battle for supremacy in AI.

As a confidante of US President Donald Trump, Huang has lobbied for the easing of restrictions on exports of high-end chips to China, putting him at odds with national security hawks in Washington who argue that Beijing must be blocked from access to cutting-edge US tech.

If Nvidia’s board were to oust Huang, it would mark a seismic moment for the chip giant.



Widely viewed as integral to Nvidia’s meteoric rise to the ranks of the world’s most valuable companies, Huang is known for a centralised leadership style that places him at the centre of the company’s day-to-day operations and strategic decisions.

“Jensen is Nvidia, without him the company loses it central, animating spirit,” Jay Goldberg, a senior analyst at Seaport Research Partners in San Francisco, told Al Jazeera.

“The organization is built around him and replacing him will be very painful organizationally, and impossible to do personality wise.”

This is a developing story.

World.title: Hegseth entourage reprimanded by guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
World.content:
Guard at memorial site can be heard yelling at group to ‘maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times’.

Share Hegseth entourage reprimanded by guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on social media

Hegseth scolded by security at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier

A video has spread online showing a military guard scolding a group accompanying United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth during a visit to the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

On Wednesday, Hegseth and members of his staff visited the memorial site at Arlington National Cemetery.

But as they paused to take group photos, they could be heard laughing. The video shows an Army sentinel turning to loudly reprimand them.

“All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times,” the guard yelled.

The tomb, seen as a sombre memorial to those who have died in war, marks the resting place of unidentified US soldiers from World War I and later conflicts.

A member of the 3rd Infantry Regiment – known as the “Old Guard” – watches over the site 24 hours a day.

The incident, which took place on Veterans Day, comes amid speculation over whether Hegseth will be able to maintain his cabinet-level position in the administration of US President Donald Trump.

Hegseth narrowly avoided a vote on articles of impeachment brought against him in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday, with Republican lawmakers banding together to derail the effort.

Critics have accused Hegseth of overseeing several unlawful actions while in his post, including spearheading the US-Israel war on Iran without seeking congressional authorisation first.

The war became a central topic in the November 3 midterm elections, in which Trump’s Republican Party suffered a bruising setback, losing both chambers of Congress.



Hegseth has also championed a campaign of deadly strikes targeting alleged drug-trafficking boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific Ocean. Legal scholars have called that campaign a series of extrajudicial killings.

During his time as defence secretary, Hegseth has been criticised for weakening rules meant to diminish civilian casualties in US strikes.

In addition, his tenure has been marked by right-wing culture war issues: he has sought to ban transgender service members from the armed forces and instituted testosterone testing for male soldiers.

In response to Wednesday’s interaction at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a statement that the sentinel had responded “correctly”.

He also underscored Hegseth’s commitment to respecting US soldiers.

“The Secretary and the entire Department have always honored – and will always honor – the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe,” Parnell said.

World.title: Why the US, Mexico and Guatemala may lose their measles-free status
World.content:
A independent commission is meeting to review whether countries in the Americas still meet its measles elimination criteria.

Share Why the US, Mexico and Guatemala may lose their measles-free status on social media

International health experts are meeting in Washington, DC, this week to determine which countries in the Americas have endemic measles transmission.

The outcome could decide whether the United States, Mexico and Guatemala retain their “measles elimination status”: a designation that the virus has not spread uncontrolled domestically for at least 12 months.

The Pan American Health Organization’s (PAHO) Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission (RVC) began its annual conference on Tuesday to assess the countries’ status. The conference will adjourn on Friday.

The review comes as a sharp resurgence of the virus has spread across the Americas, with the US experiencing its largest and deadliest measles outbreak in nearly 30 years. The US has held its elimination status since 2000, but it risks losing it this year.

The commission will review reports submitted by all 35 PAHO member states, with particular attention to countries experiencing prolonged outbreaks.

How does the process work? Al Jazeera breaks down what happens in this explainer.

Who decides whether a country has eliminated measles?

The RVC is an independent panel of international experts in epidemiology, public health and virology. The group advises PAHO, which is part of the World Health Organization, on which countries have maintained the elimination of measles and rubella.

The Americas became the first region in the world to eliminate endemic measles transmission in 2016, following decades of vaccination campaigns. For this year’s review, the commission is examining epidemiological data from 2025 and the first half of 2026.



Which countries could lose their elimination status this year?

The US, Mexico, Guatemala, Peru and Bolivia are at risk. Canada lost its status last November.

The US, which eliminated endemic measles transmission in 2000, has experienced sustained outbreaks since January 2025. Mexico has also reported prolonged transmission.

PAHO reported 57,666 confirmed measles cases across 17 countries and territories in the Americas between January and October 2026.

How does a country lose its status?

Experts at the conference evaluate whether infections result from separate introductions of the virus or whether the same strain has circulated locally.

Reported measles cases or deaths alone do not determine whether a country loses its elimination status. Some cases, for instance, come from exposure to measles during travel. A limited outbreak due to such exposure would not result in the loss of a country’s measles elimination status.

Under PAHO’s criteria, a country loses its elimination status if the same measles virus strain continues to spread uninterrupted for at least 12 months in a country or defined geographical area.

Investigators use genetic sequencing to determine whether infections are linked to the same virus strain. They also examine epidemiological data to establish how the virus has spread and whether transmission has been interrupted.

In addition, the commission considers vaccination coverage, how healthcare systems monitor measles cases, and the speed of outbreak responses in its decisions.

When will the decision be announced?

The commission’s deliberations in Washington run until Friday. It will assess the evidence and make recommendations on the status of individual countries to PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa, who will make the final determination.

The official announcement is expected early next week following the conclusion of the conference.

What happens if the US loses its status?

Experts agree that the US will likely lose its measles elimination status, marking a reversal of a major public-health achievement.

“It would be a disappointment, not a shock,” Matt Ferrari, the director of Pennsylvania State University’s Center for Infectious Disease Dynamics, told Al Jazeera. “This is moving backwards from a great public health achievement, and to see that backslide is just heart-wrenching.”

Although the loss of status would not trigger any immediate consequences, those working in the field say it would be an embarrassment.

“It’s a stain on your health programme,” Edwin Asturias, a professor of infectious disease and epidemiology at the University of Colorado, told Al Jazeera.



The long-term effects include greater pressure on public-health systems, which must devote resources to identifying infections, tracing contacts, conducting laboratory tests, isolating patients and organising vaccination campaigns.

When asked about how a country generally responds to losing its measles elimination status, Asturias pointed to Brazil, which found itself in that predicament in 2019. The country regained its measles-free designation in 2024 after launching a strategic vaccination campaign. But Asturias does not believe that the US will mount a similarly robust response.

On Tuesday, Erica Schwartz, the director of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, said losing elimination status would not change the agency’s approach to measles.

“Let’s say we did lose our measles elimination status. We’re going to be doing the same exact thing that we’ve been doing today, which is working with the states,” Schwartz told the news agency Reuters.

Ferrari said the announcement could nonetheless galvanise action at state and local levels by giving public-health officials and advocates shared language.

“Think globally, act locally,” Ferrari said. “We all will have the same language to talk about what’s going on. And that’s surprisingly important.”

World.title: Cameroon: Who is really calling the shots?
World.content:
Biya’s absences raise questions about who holds power and what comes next in Cameroon.

Share Cameroon: Who is really calling the shots? on social media

Yaounde, Cameroon – A dispute over roadworks in Yaounde in March, ahead of Pope Leo XIV’s visit to Cameroon the following month, highlighted tensions between central government and municipal authorities.

The disagreement involved Housing and Urban Development Minister Celestine Ketcha Courtes and Yaounde City Mayor Luc Messi Atangana over the rehabilitation of a road along the papal visit route, according to local media reports.

The episode raised a broader question about competing centres of authority in Cameroon: Who exercises power when President Paul Biya is absent?

Biya, 93, has governed Cameroon since 1982. His prolonged absences from public view have intensified scrutiny on how decisions are made, who has access to him and how much authority is exercised by those around him.

Biya returned to Yaounde on August 20 after more than 10 weeks abroad, following a stay in Europe that began on June 7 . His return did little to dispel questions about the management of power.

The issue is not simply whether the state continues to function. It is whether the institutions and informal networks built around one president can manage power coherently when he is not visibly directing government.

Cameroon’s constitution gives the president extensive executive authority. He defines national policy, appoints the prime minister and, based on the latter’s proposal, other members of government.

He is also commander-in-chief of the armed forces. The prime minister heads the government and directs its activities within the framework of the president’s policy.



Who holds executive authority?

Under Section 10 of the constitution, the president may delegate some of his powers to the prime minister, other members of government and senior administrative officials, within the scope of their respective responsibilities.

Where the president is temporarily unable to perform his duties, he must expressly delegate some of his functions to the prime minister or, if the prime minister is also unavailable, another member of government.

An absence abroad does not, in itself, establish that the president is temporarily unable to perform his duties or automatically transfer his constitutional powers to the prime minister.

The government has not provided a detailed public account of whether a clear delegation of presidential functions is in effect during Biya’s prolonged absences.

Research by the Organised Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP) found that Biya spent at least four and a half years abroad on private visits over a period of more than three decades.

The investigation, which examined records of his travels from 1982 onwards, renewed questions about how much government business depends on his direct involvement.

One figure central to that debate is Ferdinand Ngoh Ngoh, the secretary-general at the presidency.

According to the official biography published by the Prime Minister’s Office, his responsibilities include receiving the president’s instructions, monitoring the implementation of presidential decisions and coordinating administrations attached to the presidency.

On February 5, 2019, Biya signed Decree No. 2019/043, granting Ngoh Ngoh a permanent delegation of signature. The measure gave him authority to sign certain official documents on the president’s behalf.

A delegation of signature, however, is not a transfer of presidential powers. Ngoh Ngoh is not constitutionally the president’s successor, and his formal responsibilities should not be confused with the informal political influence attributed to him.

The influence of the inner circle

Other figures regularly mentioned in discussions about the presidency include First Lady Chantal Biya and the president’s son, Franck Biya. Neither holds a constitutional executive office. Claims about their influence and about rival networks around the president are difficult to establish independently.

Ryan Cummings, an Africa-focused security analyst, has argued that individuals close to the president may be playing increasingly tangible roles as questions grow about the management of power.



His assessment points to the importance of the presidential circle but does not establish who makes particular decisions or on whose authority.

Access to the president does not, in itself, establish that those around him exercise executive powers.

An uncertain succession

The succession question has become more pressing following a constitutional amendment approved on April 14 this year. The amendment reintroduced the office of vice president, with the president given the authority to appoint and dismiss its holder.

Under the revised Article 6, the vice president would assume the presidency if the office became vacant through the president’s death, resignation or permanent incapacity established by the Constitutional Council.

The vice president would complete the remainder of the presidential term.

The law also provides for circumstances in which there is no vice president or the vice president is unable to perform the duties of the office. In either case, a presidential election must be held between 20 and 120 days after the post officially becomes vacant.

The Senate president would serve as interim president until a new president is elected. If the Senate president is unable to perform the role, the responsibility passes to the Senate vice president, according to the order of precedence in the Senate.

The amendment establishes a formal succession mechanism but leaves the appointment of the vice president in Biya’s hands. As of November 10 , no appointment had been publicly announced.

The absence of a designated vice president means the new succession arrangement has yet to be tested. If the presidency became vacant before an appointment, the constitution provides for an interim presidency under the Senate president and a new presidential election. Accounts of competing factions and efforts to position potential successors should therefore be treated as assessments, not evidence of an agreed succession plan.

Military reshuffles and wider risks

Military appointments during Biya’s absence have added another dimension to the debate.

On August 4 , the Reuters news agency reported that three presidential decrees had reshuffled the senior military leadership. The changes included replacing commanders in four of Cameroon’s five joint military regions, promoting the head of the Presidential Guard from colonel to brigadier general and appointing a new commander of the Rapid Intervention Brigade.

Robert Besseling, CEO of intelligence advisory firm Pangea-Risk, interprets the changes partly through the lens of loyalty and the management of potential threats to the presidency. The decrees do not explain the reasons for the appointments, making their political significance difficult to establish independently.

The stakes extend beyond the presidential palace. Cameroon faces a separatist conflict in its English-speaking regions and attacks by armed groups linked to Boko Haram in the Far North.

Uncertainty over political authority at the centre could complicate the government’s response to these challenges, even as state institutions continue to operate.



Opposition criticism has focused on the concentration of executive authority. Social Democratic Front leader Joshua Osih criticised the constitutional amendment during the parliamentary debate in April. In remarks reported by Focus Media Afrique on April 3 , he argued that the reform weakened democratic legitimacy and reinforced the centralisation of power.

The government, meanwhile, has defended the president’s authority to make appointments. Communication Minister and government spokesman Rene Emmanuel Sadi told French broadcaster RFI in August that Biya was entitled to decide when to form a new government. The presidency did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

Not all observers see an immediate breakdown in state administration. Paul Anchang, a Yaounde-based political analyst, argues that institutions continue to perform their functions. Besseling, however, offers a more critical assessment of the political situation.

The distinction between a functioning state and an accountable centre of political authority remains at the heart of Cameroon’s predicament.

Government business may continue, but the concentration of power around one individual leaves unresolved questions about who exercises authority in his absence and how it will eventually be transferred.

As Robert Besseling puts it: “The political scene suffers from distinct institutional paralysis.”

World.title: Hegseth scolded by security at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
World.content:
Hegseth scolded by security at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier

NewsFeed Hegseth scolded by security at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier

An army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in the Arlington National Cemetery has reprimanded US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his guests, asking them to maintain ‘silence and respect’.

World.title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
World.content:
Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.

Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas.

Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption.

Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November.

The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Ãlvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant."

There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields.

Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de GrÃ cia, close to the iconic PlaÃ§a de Catalunya in the centre of the city.

Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store.

The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful". She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there."

She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said.

Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads.

The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices.

World.title: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race
World.content:
Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades.

Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be elected to the US Senate in more than 140 years.

Only a few thousand votes separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith.

The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called.

Colom won with 49.2% of the vote, while Hyde-Smith received 48.7% and an independent candidate got 2.1%, according to figures from CBS.

Hyde-Smith congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well.

"While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said.

World.title: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
World.content:
Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day.

Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion.

However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon.

Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest."

"I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible.

Comments by Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky were less conciliatory. "Right now... a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the US, and on whether Europe comes to its senses," he said.

After the talks it was announced that on Thursday US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - President Donald Trump's son-in-law - would travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to speak to Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.

The meetings in Abu Dhabi had been framed as centred around the "security architecture" of Europe.

For Kyiv, this may include reassurances that allies will come to its aid if Ukraine comes under attack again, despite the country not being a Nato member.

For Moscow, a reworked "security framework" is likely to include a limit to the influence of Nato in eastern Europe - a central concern for the Kremlin since the alliance's eastward expansion.

Earlier this week Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while the Kremlin's Medinsky said the world needed a "new" and "fair" security system.

That framework would serve as "a new Yalta and Potsdam", Medinsky said, referring to the 1940s summits in which the victorious Allied powers carved up post-war Europe into spheres of influence.

Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin.

Representatives of Britain, Nato and various EU countries were also in Abu Dhabi and met with US and Ukrainian negotiators, but the Kremlin - with whom the EU does not officially communicate - said its delegation had not had any contact with them.

Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent.

Many - particularly in eastern Europe - feel their security is linked to that of Ukraine. Agreements cannot be implemented "if no consensus can be reached among Nato members," a German government spokesperson said on Wednesday.

Kushner said the US was keen to bring the Europeans on board and said that getting them "added to the format" would be on the agenda for his talks with Putin.

There is also disagreement on whether discussions on a future security framework should be preceded by a ceasefire, as the Europeans and Kyiv would want, or whether the fighting only stops after an agreement has been reached, as the Kremlin has insisted.

Any agreement on a peacetime security framework, however, is contingent on the war ending, Kushner noted. But that cannot occur "until there's an agreement on territory and on all other bilateral issues," he added.

Since talks began last year, a core obstacle to any settlement has been Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are essential to its security.

Moscow, meanwhile, has never backed down from its demand that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds. "Every inch" of land would be "returned to Russia one way or another", Medinsky said.

Kushner acknowledged that the territorial question remained the hardest, while Zelensky's chief of staff and negotiator Kyrylo Budanov refused to be drawn on whether Russia was still demanding a Ukrainian withdrawal from the region.

Later, Budanov admitted the talks had been "tough" and that Ukraine's priority was to ensure Russia could not attack it again.

"These deals are very hard and complex, and this one is very emotional, very complex," Kushner said. "The reality is there is no trust right now between the sides and that is to be expected after a conflict like this."

World.title: New York building collapse kills one person and injures 12
World.content:
Two people have died and several others were injured when a three-storey building collapsed in New York City.

Rescuers are searching for survivors trapped under the rubble in the Flatbush neighbourhood of Brooklyn.

Footage from the ground also shows exposed bedrooms and stairwells in an adjacent building following the collapse.

World.title: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
World.content:
Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation, an aide has told the BBC, in a move which could further strain the political alliance that helped propel President Prabowo Subianto to power.

It comes after Indonesia's Supreme Court ruled that a high-school document used during Gibran's 2024 election campaign was invalid.

The ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran.

The aide, Budi Arie, said Gibran's resignation letter was submitted directly to Prabowo on Wednesday. It remains unclear if it has been accepted.

Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office.

Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials.

Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated.

"No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said.

It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion.

Gibran previously argued that undertaking university education was sufficient proof that he had completed senior high school.

On Tuesday, he asked for the chance to challenge the ruling and be given the opportunity to prove the legitimacy of his education credentials, State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi said.

Gibran's ascension to Prabowo's ticket in the 2024 election was part of an alliance formed between his father, outgoing president Joko Widodo - known as Jokowi - and Prabowo, his erstwhile bitter rival.

Gibran was 36 at the time, and only became eligible for candidacy after a controversial ruling by the Constitutional Court, which exempted him from the minimum age requirement of 40.

His resignation comes as tensions between Jokowi and Prabowo appear to have flared.

Since taking the presidency, Prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with Jokowi's legacy project: the construction of Nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country.

In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many Jokowi loyalists into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati.

Last week, authorities arrested presidential chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - no relation - on suspicions of wiretapping the president.

Prabowo sacked Listyo a day later, in what many pointed to as a sign of a crumbling alliance: Listyo, who formerly served as the national police chief, is widely considered a long-time ally of Jokowi.

Within the government, allegiances seem to be shifting. On Monday, three members of Prabowo's cabinet collectively resigned from the party led by Kaesang Pangarep, Jokowi's youngest son, citing their desire to focus on their duties in Prabowo's administration.

All this is unfolding at a particularly turbulent period in Prabowo's presidency. The free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation.

On Tuesday, students across the country staged demonstrations to protest against the government's handling of a range of issues, including the environmental crisis and corruption.

World.title: Kidnapper, 74, escapes from house arrest in Argentina by abseiling from balcony
World.content:
A 74-year-old Italian man who was found guilty of a kidnapping carried out by a far-left militant group in the 1970s has escaped while under house arrest in Argentina and is on the run.

Leonardo Bertulazzi used a harness to abseil down from a fifth-floor balcony in the capital, Buenos Aires.

His escape was not immediately registered because he had tampered with his electronic ankle monitor so that it continued to transmit body temperature measurements even after he had prised it open and absconded.

Bertulazzi already spent decades as a fugitive after he was sentenced in absentia in Italy for the 1977 kidnapping of Italian naval engineer Pietro Costa.

He was awaiting extradition to Italy and was being monitored by the Argentine ministry of security through an ankle tag which registers the wearer's body temperature and movements.

Officials said that they had become suspicious when they noticed that the tag had remained stationary.

When they entered the fifth-floor apartment in the centre of Buenos Aires, Bertulazzi was gone, but the ankle monitor remained.

Wary of Bertulazzi's past with the Marxist guerilla group the Red Brigades and his bomb-making skills, police called in explosives experts in case it had been rigged to detonate, according to Argentine newspaper ClarÃ­n.

However, the experts found that while Bertulazzi had tampered with the device, he had done so to prevent the alarm from sounding once he removed it.

A nationwide manhunt is now under way.

Italian media say that his extradition to Italy had been imminent after his last appeal was rejected.

Bertulazzi was first arrested after using a false passport to cross into Argentina from neighbouring Chile in 2002.

However, he was granted refugee status in 2004 and lived freely in the South American country until his re-arrest in 2024, when the current right-wing president, Javier Milei, took office.

Milei's government said at the time that "Bertulazzi is responsible for crimes that undermined democratic values and the lives of many victims".

He was a member of the Red Brigades, which kidnapped and killed a number of state officials in the 1970s and '80s.

Bertulazzi was part of the Red Brigades' Genoa section that kidnapped Pietro Costa on the street and then held him for 81 days before receiving a big ransom.

The money it made from the kidnapping was then used to buy a flat in Rome, which was used in 1978 for the Red Brigades' most notorious crime, the kidnap and murder of Italian former Prime Minister, Aldo Moro.

Moro was abducted when his car was ambushed on the way to the opening of parliament. He was held in the flat for 54 days before he was shot and his body abandoned in the boot of a Renault car in the centre of Rome.

World.title: Famed ship SS United States to be sunk off coast of Florida
World.content:
A ship that was once the fastest in the world and is longer than the Titanic will be sunk off the coast of Florida and turned into the world's largest artificial ocean reef.

The SS United States spent nearly 30 years docked in Philadelphia before it was moved to Florida, where it will soon become a home for sealife and an underwater attraction for marine enthusiasts.

Activists unsuccessfully fought for the historic liner - which crossed the Atlantic Ocean hundreds of times - to be preserved as a museum.

Instead, after being purchased by a Florida county, it will be added to the dozens of artificial reefs off the coast, as a land-based museum detailing the ship's history is also planned.

World.title: Schools in Italy, Scotland and Northern Ireland hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax
World.content:
Some 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, according to local authorities.

In Italy a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger".

"These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook.

Scotland's education secretary Mairi McAllan said there was no risk to the public and specialist cyber-crime officers were working to identify the source of the messages. In Northern Ireland education officials told schools to remain open unless otherwise advised by police.

It is unclear whether the incidents are connected.

"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," McAllan said.

Scottish police had earlier said that the warnings were "immediately assessed" as hoaxes. However some local authorities confirmed that some schools had been evacuated.

"Our advice is that there is no requirement to evacuate schools or keep children away from education based solely on the content of the emails," Police Scotland said.

Italian officials said a single email appeared to have been sent on Wednesday to the inboxes of 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 state schools, and private schools were unaffected.

The message, said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan", caused alarm in many schools.

The BBC has seen the email sent to Scottish schools which appeared to have similar wording, and also referenced the name Mikhail Andropov, although as leader of a "Red Owl" project.

Italy's Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the incidents involving Italian schools were probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk", adding that there appeared to be a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in across Europe targeting flights, supermarkets and even hospitals.

Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption.

Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.

World.title: Abiodun allocates 49 new duplexes to Ogun judges, swears in five new ones
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has announced the allocation of 49 newly constructed duplexes to judges of the State High Court, in a major intervention aimed at strengthening judicial welfare and improving the conditions of service in the state.

The governor made the announcement on Wednesday during the swearing-in ceremony of five new High Court judges at the Executive Chambers, Governor’s Office, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta.

The newly appointed judges are Luqman Oke, Adebimpe Obienu, Fatima Daudu, Rafiat Kadiri and Oludotun Osho, bringing the total number of judges in Ogun State to 49.

Abiodun said the 49 duplexes, located at the President Muhammadu Buhari Estate along Kobape Road, Abeokuta, were provided in fulfilment of his administration’s commitment to judicial welfare and the creation of an enabling environment for the effective administration of justice.

“As our administration approaches the conclusion of its tenure, we will continue to motivate and support the judiciary and provide for the welfare and well-being of our judges, who have signed up for this service to humanity, within our constitutional responsibilities,” he said.

The governor described the judiciary as the last hope of the common man, charging the newly sworn-in judges to uphold the highest standards of integrity, impartiality and professionalism in the discharge of their responsibilities.

He urged them to dispense justice without fear or favour, carefully evaluate evidence, apply the law faithfully and ensure that their courts remained accessible institutions where the rights of every citizen were protected.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also cautioned the judges against political interference, personal relationships and material inducement, stressing that neither public opinion nor the prominence of any individual or political party should influence judicial decisions.

In furtherance of his administration’s commitment to judicial infrastructure, Abiodun disclosed that construction had commenced on the Abeokuta Division of the Court of Appeal complex on a 2.6-hectare site adjoining the State Judiciary Complex at Kobape.

He listed other interventions to include the completion of six duplexes at Ibara Housing GRA, Abeokuta, for judicial officers, as well as 20 bungalows at Prince Court Estate, Kobape, for supporting personnel.

The governor noted that the appointment of the five judges reflected his administration’s determination to strengthen the state’s judicial capacity, adding that more judges had been appointed under his watch than during previous administrations in the state.

He particularly commended the Chief Judge for the appointments, expressing optimism that the emergence of a younger generation of judicial officers would provide continuity, renewed energy and long-term institutional development for the judiciary.

Abiodun also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to institutional cooperation and respect for the constitutional principle of separation of powers.

He highlighted the state judiciary’s adoption of an electronic affidavit platform as another significant step towards improving access to justice and service delivery.

According to him, the digital platform has facilitated the processing of more than 31,000 affidavits, with approximately 4,500 users and 25 agents operating across the state.

World.title: Mbah declares emergency on Nsukka-Adani road, tours Uzo Uwani
World.content:
Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State has declared an emergency on the Nsukka-Adani Road, describing it as a critical economic corridor and promising to commence work on it before the end of the month.

Mbah also said that with the rains receding, his administration would commence the construction of the Edem-Nrobo-Abbi-Nimbo Road in earnest.

This was even as he took a swipe at his opponents in the 2027 governorship race, accusing them of wasting precious time in Abuja shopping for shortcuts and ways to compromise the polls rather than face the people of Enugu to canvass programmes that would benefit the state.

He spoke at Adani and Ugbene Ajima during a campaign tour of Ogboli and Igbo-Ano Development Centres in Uzo Uwani Local Government Area of the state on Tuesday.

On the Nsukka-Adani Road, Mbah said, “We have committed to doing the Nsukka-Adani Road. But I think that that road is now a matter of utmost urgency. We cannot wait for another season. We are sending contractors immediately to that road. We are going to fix that road. So, before the end of this month, we are going to move contractors there,” he pledged.

The Governor, while thanking the people for voting for him in the 2023 governorship election, expressed happiness that the issue of insecurity in the area had been well addressed.

He said the Smart Schools initiative would introduce the children of Enugu State to contemporary skills and prepare them for the present and future global economy.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We also recognised that there was a crisis in our education sector. So, we set about to build Smart Green Schools because we felt that the world is moving very fast. And we didn’t want our children to be left behind. And we knew that the skills that the kids need today are different from the skills we were exposed to 30, 40 years ago.

“Today, our children need technology to be able to work and to create wealth. So, in this Development Centre, we have four Smart Green Schools and four Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres already built and standing in each ward,” he stated.

Meanwhile, Mbah recalled that his opponents were yet to present any manifesto because they had nothing to offer, adding that they only specialised in multiple certificate forgery.

“In fact, they cannot even come here. You know where they are? They are somewhere in Abuja, busy looking for an alternative instead of coming to know you or even talk to you.

“They think that there is a shortcut. So, rather than come and face the people, talk to them about their records and maybe even tell them about their plans, they go about shopping for alternatives to the Lion Building.

“They are unable to face you because, one, they don’t have any record. Two, they don’t have any plans.

“So, their only option is to see whether there are ways they can manipulate your votes or your mandate. But are you going to accept that? Do you have your broom? You must sweep them away and tell them you do not have room for them.

“As I said, we are dealing with people without records because they cannot point to anything they have done in life. Not one. They cannot.

“If they want to be honest, they can tell you about certificate forgery. And if you need experts in that area, you probably need to consult them. But we do not want to expose our kids to such people. We want people with genuine records; people who have worked and created wealth before offering themselves for service. Not people without records and without plans.

“They cannot come out and tell you this is the plan they have for you in your education sector, in your healthcare sector, in your agriculture sector or in the economic sector. Nothing. So, use your brooms, your votes to sweep them away,” he stated.

The Governor also made a stopover at Our Lady Health of the Sick Maternity Hospital (Arụ Ike Ndi Ọya), Adani, where he cleared all the medical bills of patients, running into millions, and also promised to equip the facility to the standard of the state’s Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centre, in addition to providing ultrasound equipment.

In their speeches, Deputy Governor of Enugu State, Barr. Ifeanyi Ossai; Senator Ikeje Asogwa; Council Chairman of Uzo Uwani, Barr. Chijioke Ezegwu; Director General of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Enugu, Campaign Council, Chief Charlie Mbah; Nollywood star, Rachael Okonkwo (Nkoli Nwa Nsukka), among others, commended the Governor for the tremendous development recorded in the state under his leadership, promising to support the, APC from top to bottom.

They acknowledged that the development challenges he inherited could be solved in three years and a few months, noting that the important thing was that he was delivering on his campaign promises at great speed.

Other stalwarts present include Senator Chukwuka; Deputy DG of Enugu APC Campaign Council, Dr. Dan Shere; House of Representatives candidate for Igbo Etiti/Uzo Uwani Federal Constituency, Hon. Cornelius Onwubuya; Commissioner for Agriculture and Agro-Industrialisation, Dr. Patrick Ubru; Member representing Uzo Uwani State Constituency, Hon. Chukwuma Ekwueme.

Also, Mbah, who was warmly received by the students of Santa Maria Nursery and Primary School, Adani, pledged to construct a classroom block and set up an innovation hub for the school.

World.title: Awujale: Ogun reveals Fusengbuwa crisis, insists on due process
World.content:
The Ogun State Government has defended its handling of the succession process to the Awujale stool, revealing how it intervened in the internal crisis within the Fusengbuwa Ruling House and insisting that the emergence of the next monarch must strictly follow due process.

The government also warned individuals and groups allegedly sponsoring media attacks and spreading disinformation to pressure it over the succession process to desist or face the full weight of the law.

The State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Mr Oluwasina Ogungbade, stated this in a statement on Wednesday, stressing that the government had acted with fairness, restraint and in accordance with the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration and the Obas and Chiefs Law of Ogun State, 2021.

He explained that following the demise of the late Awujale, Oba Sikiru Adetona, the government had consistently recognised the Fusengbuwa Ruling House’s entitlement to produce the next occupant of the revered traditional stool.

Ogungbade, however, disclosed that the government had to intervene when it discovered that the ruling house was operating under three different family heads, with nomination forms reportedly being sold for as much as ₦10 million.

He recalled that at a meeting with the family on 6 November 2025, the government advised it to resolve its internal leadership disagreements, operate under one recognised family head and discontinue the collection of nomination fees.

According to him, the intervention yielded positive results, as the family subsequently agreed to operate as one united ruling house, abolish candidature fees, refund payments already made by aspirants and expressed appreciation to the government.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He maintained that the government’s intervention was not intended to deprive the Fusengbuwa family of its entitlement but to ensure that the succession process was conducted in an orderly, transparent and legally acceptable manner.

The Attorney-General explained that while the government respected the traditional succession process, it also had statutory responsibilities in the appointment and installation of traditional rulers, including the authority to reject a nominated candidate where the interest of good governance so demands.

He described recent media publications accusing the government of interference and bias as misleading, alleging that some were sponsored to create public hostility and exert undue pressure on the government.

Ogungbade distinguished legitimate criticism and advocacy from what he described as media blackmail and deliberate disinformation, warning that the government would not allow such activities to undermine its lawful responsibilities.

Citing Section 61 of the Criminal Law of Ogun State, he noted that unlawful acts calculated to interfere with the free exercise of a governor’s official duties could attract a three-year jail term.

He consequently cautioned publishers and individuals involved in the dissemination of misleading reports designed to interfere with the succession process, warning that the government would not hesitate to pursue appropriate legal remedies if the alleged activities persisted.

The government reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that the emergence of the next Awujale reflects the provisions of the law, the established traditional institutions of Ijebuland and the principles of fairness and due process.

World.title: ADC accuses Tinubu, APC of obstructing opposition after Kaduna govt sealed Arewa House
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) of using public authority to obstruct opposition activities following the sealing of Arewa House in Kaduna and the release of a controversial court judgement affecting the party’s leadership.

The party said the closure of Arewa House, the proposed venue for a consultation between its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and Northern stakeholders on Wednesday, was part of a pattern of actions to frustrate its political activities.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, Phrank Shaibu, director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, also criticised the timing of the release of the certified copy of the judgement delivered by Peter Lifu, a judge of the Federal High Court in Abuja.

Mr Shaibu said Mr Lifu released the duly authenticated copy on the final day of the seven days prescribed by the Constitution, leaving the party with limited time to study the decision and prepare its legal response.

He said, “Releasing a consequential judgement on the last permitted day leaves the African Democratic Congress with precious little time to study it and prepare its next legal steps.”

Citing Section 294(1) of the 1999 Constitution, Mr Shaibu said courts were required to furnish parties with duly authenticated copies of their decisions within seven days of delivery.

He added that the party would study the judgement and pursue every lawful remedy available to it.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The timing of the release raises serious concern, especially as our party continues to face actions that obstruct its campaign and political consultations,” he said.

Arewa House closure

On the sealing of Arewa House, the ADC said the Kaduna State Government had prevented it from using the historic facility for Atiku’s planned consultation with Northern stakeholders.

Mr Shaibu described Arewa House as part of the shared heritage of the diverse people of Northern Nigeria, saying its closure over a political consultation was an affront to their culture and dignity.

He quoted Atiku as saying, “My campaign team had proposed the Arewa House as the venue for our consultation with stakeholders on Thursday and, today, the APC government decided to seal the building.”

The ADC also recalled an earlier incident during its campaign flag-off in Sokoto, alleging that the APC-led government in the state attempted to frustrate the event.

“This is a troubling pattern. During our campaign flag-off in Sokoto, the APC government also tried to frustrate us. The people stood firm, and their will prevailed,” Mr Shaibu said.

He said the latest development in Kaduna showed that the ruling party was determined to restrict the opposition’s political activities.

“We hold President Bola Tinubu and the APC politically responsible for this pattern of obstruction,” he added.

“An outgoing president and a ruling party should respect democratic competition, not use public authority to impede the opposition, restrict political consultation or weaken Nigerians’ right to choose.”

The ADC said it would not be intimidated and thanked Nigerians for their support, promising to continue its consultations and take its message to voters.

Backstory

The development comes amid a leadership crisis in the ADC following a 5 November judgement by Mr Lifu, which nullified Mr Mark’s emergence as the party’s national chairman and voided actions taken by his leadership, including the nomination of candidates for the 2027 general elections.

The judgement followed a suit filed by Nafiu Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the party, who challenged the emergence of the Mark-led leadership after the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu.

Mr Gombe argued that he was entitled to assume the party’s leadership following Mr Nwosu’s resignation.

The ruling also cast uncertainty over the 2027 presidential ticket produced through the party’s primary organised by the Mark-led leadership, which produced Atiku as its candidate.

The judgement prompted protests by ADC supporters and candidates at the Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday, demanding the release of its certified true copy to enable the party to appeal.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the protesters carried placards and called on the judiciary to release the judgement, while also urging the National Judicial Council to intervene.

The ADC had earlier petitioned the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, alleging that the delay in releasing the judgement was frustrating its constitutional right of appeal.

The party said it applied for the certified copy immediately after the judgement was delivered on 5 November and paid the prescribed fees but had yet to receive it.

The party has maintained that it will challenge the judgement at the Court of Appeal.

World.title: 2027: SDP appoints Peter Obi’s ex-adviser as campaign coordinator
World.content:
Yunusa Tanko, a former special adviser to Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has been appointed National Coordinator of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential campaign team.

Mr Tanko’s appointment was announced on Wednesday during the inauguration of the SDP Presidential Campaign Council at the party’s secretariat in Abuja.

His appointment comes barely two weeks after he resigned as Mr Obi’s political adviser for Northern Nigeria. Before his appointment, Mr Tanko served as the national coordinator of the Obidient Movement, a political movement campaigning for Mr Obi’s presidential bid.

He was welcomed into the SDP campaign team by the party’s National Working Committee (NWC), leaders and supporters.

Tanko speaks

In his acceptance speech, Mr Tanko pledged to work with the party’s presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, to secure victory in the 2027 presidential election.

He described the SDP as a left-wing political party that represents the interests of ordinary Nigerians, particularly the downtrodden. He also thanked the party’s leadership for the confidence reposed in him.

“The SDP is a left-wing political party. For those of you who do not know, we represent the interests of the downtrodden. The SDP represents those people that you neglect on the streets. So, this party is people-oriented.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I express my profound gratitude and sincere appreciation to Almighty Allah for making this historic event possible. I equally thank the leadership of the Social Democratic Party for the confidence and repose in me by appointing me as the National Coordinator of the SDP Presidential Campaign Organisation for the 2027 Presidential Election,” he said.

Mr Tanko said he had informed Mr Obi, his former principal, and Seriake Dickson, the national leader of the NDC, of his decision to join the SDP campaign.
