03 Why it moved

First and heaviest: a hot inflation reading and a stronger dollar. The US dollar index rose 0.60% to 102.84, and the 10-year Treasury yield stayed near 5%.

A higher yield makes gold, which pays no interest, less attractive, and a stronger dollar makes metals dearer for buyers using other currencies. The gold-tracking fund fell 1.13%, and Buenaventura, with its gold and silver exposure, fell more than three times as far.

Second, Nexa’s mild rise on Wednesday looks like buyers returning after the stock’s slide.

The signals conflict in one place: US shares rallied, with the S&P 500 up 1.31% to 7,619 and the VIX fear gauge down 10.12% to 17.49, yet miners did not join in. Oil was flat, up 0.01%. Our best-supported reading, with medium confidence, is that investors rotated into technology and away from metals as yields rose.

04 The trend behind it

Nexa is 28.3% below its 12-month high of US$16.72, set on 2026-05-06, and 113.5% above its low of US$5.61 from 2025-11-11. Over 60 sessions it has fallen 11.2%, so this is a continuation of a cooling trend after a huge rally, not a new collapse.

Buenaventura is the sharper story. It sits 40.2% below its 12-month high of US$43.67 from 2026-02-27, and only 14.6% above its low of US$22.78 from 2025-11-20.

History offers a mild comfort, though not a forecast. Nexa fell 5.3% in 20 sessions, and in 65 earlier cases of a fall that large in our own price records since 2017, it was higher 20 sessions later in 31 cases, or 48%, with a median of -1.0% and a worst case of -37.8%.

Buenaventura fell 14.5% in 20 sessions, and in 59 earlier cases since 2007 it was higher 20 sessions later in 32 cases, or 54%, with a median of +1.1% and a worst case of -36.8%. Past rebounds are common, but so are deeper falls.

05 What it means for Latin America

Peru and Mexico are among the world’s big zinc producers, and Bolivia is another, so zinc prices feed directly into export earnings and mining royalties. Peru is doubly exposed, because gold and silver also matter to its mining sector.

A Lima investor holding Buenaventura saw the pain first-hand. A São Paulo investor following Nexa saw a calmer day, though the stock is still well below its May peak.

A strong dollar also squeezes local currencies. Importers who buy galvanised steel and building materials in dollars feel it twice, through the price of the metal and through the exchange rate.

06 The names to watch

Nexa Resources is the cleaner zinc proxy, with mines in Peru and smelters in Brazil. And Boliden’s agreed purchase of Votorantim’s controlling stake is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

Buenaventura is the better gauge of precious metals sentiment in Peru. Its December-to-November slide shows how exposed it is to gold, which makes it the one to watch if the dollar keeps rising.

07 What would end it

For Buenaventura, the nearest floor is its 12-month low of US$22.78, only 14.6% below the current close. A break below it would open a new phase of weakness, while a recovery would need gold to stop falling.

For Nexa, the ceiling is its 12-month high of US$16.72 and the floor is far below, at US$5.61. A move toward either would need zinc itself to break out.

The one thing that would change the picture is the dollar and the Treasury yield. If the 5% yield eases and the dollar index falls back from 102.84, gold and Buenaventura would likely recover first. The next hard date is the first quarter of 2027, when the Boliden-Nexa deal is due to close.

08 What to watch

Dollar and yields: The dollar index at 102.84 and the 10-year yield at 5% set the tone for every dollar-priced metal.

The dollar index at 102.84 and the 10-year yield at 5% set the tone for every dollar-priced metal. Gold: Buenaventura follows the gold fund, which fell 1.13% on the day, so any rebound there lifts the Peruvian miner.

Buenaventura follows the gold fund, which fell 1.13% on the day, so any rebound there lifts the Peruvian miner. Nexa and Boliden: Regulatory approvals for the sale of Votorantim’s stake, due to close in the first quarter of 2027.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did Buenaventura fall more than Nexa?

Buenaventura earns much of its income from gold and silver, and the gold fund fell 1.13% on a stronger dollar and rising yields. Nexa is mainly a zinc producer and rose +0.25%.

Is zinc itself falling?

We have no settled price for zinc itself, so we read its direction through Nexa, which rose +0.25%. That points to resilience rather than a sell-off.

Who is buying Nexa?

Boliden, the Swedish miner, has agreed to buy Votorantim’s controlling stake in Nexa. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, pending approvals.

Does history say these shares will rebound?

Our records show Nexa was higher 20 sessions later in 48% of comparable cases and Buenaventura in 54%. That is history, not a forecast.

03 Why it moved

First and heaviest, China’s steel demand. The China Iron and Steel Association said end-user demand showed no significant recovery in September, and about 70% of Chinese steel is tied to property and infrastructure, sectors that remain weak. In the first seven months of 2026 China’s crude steel output fell 3.1% to 577.04 million tonnes while iron ore imports rose 5.9% to 736.84 million tonnes, a sign of too much ore chasing too little steel. Confidence: high.

Second, the usual outside drivers pointed both ways. The US dollar index rose 0.60% to 102.84 and the 10-year US Treasury yield stayed near 5%, which normally weighs on metals. Yet the S&P 500 rallied 1.31% to 7,619 and the VIX fear gauge fell 10.12% to 17.49, which supports risk appetite, and the net result was a flat proxy. Gold fell 1.13% in the gold fund, so the pressure was broad across commodities. Confidence: medium.

04 The trend behind it

This is a continuation, not a new phase. The proxy has slid from 17.82 on 20 April to 11.58, and the 3 November low of 10.98 is the lowest close in the past year.

Our own history since 2007 adds context. After 73 earlier falls at least this large in 20 sessions, the proxy was higher 20 sessions later in 36 cases, or 49%, with a median change of -0.5%, a worst case of -40.5% and a best of +37.6%. History is not a forecast, but it says a deep fall is no guarantee of a bounce or of more pain.

05 What it means for Latin America

Brazil is the centre of this story. Vale is its flagship exporter, and iron ore is among its largest sources of export earnings, so weak prices trim trade surpluses, support for the real and corporate tax receipts.

Listed miners feel it directly. CSN Mineração, at R$5.08, is 27.3% below its 10 September high of 6.99 yet 24.5% above its 19 May low of 4.08, a swing that shows how nervous holders are.

Peru, Chile and Mexico are far less exposed to iron ore, as their mining income rests on copper, silver and gold. Importers of steel in the region gain from cheaper inputs, but only if mills pass the savings on.

06 The names to watch

Vale is the bellwether: a further guidance change or cost warning would hit the proxy before the ore price itself moves. Rio Tinto, 12.1% lower over 60 sessions and 6.88% lower over 20, shows the pain is global rather than Brazilian.

CSN Mineração is the highest-risk name.

07 What would end it

The nearest support is the 3 November low of 10.98; a close below it would open the way to fresh yearly lows. The nearest hurdle is the round 12 level, and the far ceiling is the April peak of 17.82.

The catalyst is evidence of Chinese steel demand turning, through monthly steel output, property sales and any new infrastructure stimulus from Beijing, due in the coming weeks. A weaker dollar and lower US yields would help at the margin, but only China can end this downtrend.

08 What to watch

China steel data: Monthly crude steel output and property indicators from Beijing show whether mills are buying more ore.

Monthly crude steel output and property indicators from Beijing show whether mills are buying more ore. The 10.98 floor: A close below the 3 November low would mark a new 12-month low for the Vale-linked proxy.

Why does iron ore matter to Brazil?

Brazil is among the world’s largest iron ore exporters, led by Vale, so the price feeds directly into export earnings, the real and tax receipts.

Is the US$11.58 figure the iron ore price?

No. It is the price of the Vale-linked proxy, which tracks the market but is not the commodity’s own price.

Why is China so important?

Chinese mills make most of the world’s steel, and about 70% of that demand depends on property and infrastructure, which are weak.

Does a big fall mean a rebound is due?

Not necessarily. After 73 earlier falls this large, the proxy was higher 20 sessions later 49% of the time, and history is not a forecast.

03 Why it moved

First and heaviest, a general risk appetite. US shares rallied and the VIX fell 10.12% to 17.49, which tends to lift volatile, heavily sold sectors such as lithium. Confidence: medium.

Second, the usual headwinds did not help. The dollar index rose 0.60% to 102.84 and the US 10-year yield stayed near 5%, which normally hurts mining shares, so the bounce came despite them rather than because of them.

Third, the underlying weakness remains: the fund is 33.3% below its May high and still close to its 12-month low.

04 The trend behind it

The LIT fund has fallen 33.3% from its 11 May high of 91.62, and sits just 2.1% above its 30 October low. Albemarle is 55.5% below its 16 April peak and SQM is 42.6% below the same date’s high.

This is a continuation, not a new phase. Albemarle hit its 12-month low of 90.19 on 3 November, and SQM’s closes then were its weakest in at least six months.

RT base rate: our own history since 2010 shows 52 earlier cases when the LIT fund fell 8.0% or more in 20 sessions. It was higher 20 sessions later in 27 of them (52%), with a median gain of 0.7% and a worst loss of 14.9%; history is not a forecast. For SQM, after falls of 11.2% or more, 42 of 72 cases (58%) were higher, with a median of 1.7% but a worst case of 39.8% lower.

05 What it means for Latin America

Chile feels this most. SQM is its flagship lithium company, and cheaper lithium means thinner company profits and less tax and royalty income flowing back to the state.

Argentina’s brine projects and Bolivia’s long-stalled ambitions face the same arithmetic: at weaker prices, new investment is harder to justify. We found no fresh policy news from the three countries of the Lithium Triangle this month.

For a saver in Santiago or Buenos Aires holding lithium shares, the lesson is that the exposure is volatile and tied to Chinese factory output as much as to electric-car sales.

06 The names to watch

Albemarle sits just 6.4% above its 12-month low of 90.19, so it is the clearest test of whether selling is exhausted. SQM, 5.9% above its own low of 51.70, tells the same story from Chile.

The LIT fund is the broadest gauge; a close below 59.81 would mark a fresh 12-month low and weaken the rebound case.

07 What would end it

The slide ends when supply stops growing faster than demand, and that shows first in Chinese spot prices and in producers’ guidance on output. Until then, bounces like Wednesday’s are rallies inside a downtrend.

Watch 59.81 for the LIT fund as support, and the gap back toward its May high of 91.62 as distant resistance. Our archive does not make a forecast, and we cannot name the date of the next turn.

Support: The LIT fund’s 12-month low of 59.81, set on 30 October.

The LIT fund’s 12-month low of 59.81, set on 30 October. Albemarle: Whether it holds its 3 November low of 90.19.

No. It is a fund of lithium-mining and battery-materials companies, so it moves with shares as well as the metal.

Why did lithium shares rise?

Mainly because US shares rallied and the VIX fell 10.12%, not because lithium demand improved.

Where is Albemarle compared with its peak?

It is 55.5% below its 16 April high, a measure of how deep the downturn has been.

Does the rebound mean the bottom is in?

Second, the supply picture is pushing the other way. Cochilco cut its 2026 forecast for Chilean output to 4.9 million tonnes, 8.4% less than last year, citing lower ore grades at big mines, maintenance and slow project start-ups, and it expects only a 3% recovery in 2027.

Third, the equity rally explains the miners. Oil was flat, so it added little, and the shares simply rode a risk-on day in which investors bought cyclical companies. Confidence: medium, since one good day does not change the 20-session slide.

The pattern is a four-week retreat. Over 20 sessions the copper fund has lost 4.87% and over 60 sessions 3.7%, while the shares have fallen far more because miners amplify every move in the metal.

This looks like a continuation, not a new phase. The fund peaked on 22 September and has not yet found a floor, but it still sits well above its 12-month low of 30.77 set in November 2025.

Our own price history adds perspective. After 67 earlier falls as large as this one, copper was higher 20 sessions later 34 times, or 51%, with a median gain of 0.4% and a worst case of 18.5% lower; history is not a forecast, but it says a coin toss is fair.

05 What it means for Latin America

Chile, the world’s largest producer, feels the shortfall twice. It sells less metal, yet shortages tend to support prices, and Cochilco’s 2027 forecast of 5.08 million tonnes points to only a slow recovery.

Peru and Mexico gain exposure through Southern Copper, whose shares are 49.8% above their 12-month low but 20.6% below their August high. A firmer dollar also pressures Latin American currencies such as the Chilean peso and Peruvian sol, which usually track copper.

For a saver in Santiago or Lima, the practical message is that mining revenue, tax receipts and currencies are tied to a metal that is range-bound, not rising.

06 The names to watch

Freeport-McMoRan, at US$62.12, is the more volatile play and has the largest gap to its high. Its 12-month low of 39.00 was set on 17 November 2025, and the shares are 59.3% above it.

Southern Copper, at US$172.61, offers a purer bet on Peruvian and Mexican output, and its 20-session drop of 13.08% suggests investors have already priced in much bad news. Both remain highly sensitive to the Chinese factory demand that drives roughly half of global consumption.

07 What would end it

The key line for the fund is the 41.43 high from 22 September on the upside and the 30.77 low from last November on the downside. A move through either would define the next phase.

The nearer trigger is the US 10-year yield: a retreat from 5% and a softer dollar index from 102.84 would ease the pressure. A further Cochilco output cut would also lift the metal.

Does it stop? Probably not this week, but supply scarcity makes a deep slide less likely than a drawn-out sideways grind.

08 What to watch

US 10-year yield: A move back below 5% would relieve pressure on copper.

A move back below 5% would relieve pressure on copper. Dollar index: Holding above 102.84 keeps the metal expensive for foreign buyers.

Holding above 102.84 keeps the metal expensive for foreign buyers. Chilean output: Further Cochilco downgrades would confirm the supply squeeze.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, where users bet real money, lists a market on whether US copper cable will be hit with national-security tariffs under Section 232 of US trade law, with US$17,223 traded as of 7:45 p.m. ET, 11 November 2026. It prices a 22.0% chance by 31 December 2026 and a 51.5% chance by 31 December 2027.

These prices are bets, not polls. They show traders see US tariff action on copper products as more likely than not over the next year, but not this year.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did copper stay flat when mining shares jumped?

Copper follows the dollar and interest rates, while mining shares follow the broader stock market, which rose 1.31% on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

Does CPER show the copper price?

No. It tracks copper futures in New York, so it follows the metal closely but is not the spot price.

Why does Chile matter so much?

It is the world’s largest producer, and Cochilco expects 2026 output to fall 8.4% to 4.9 million tonnes.

Is the slide over?

Not yet; the fund is 8.9% below its September high, though history shows a recovery 51% of the time after similar falls.

World.title: Gold Fund Falls 1.1% as Silver Fund Edges Up | Gold & Silver, Nov 11
World.content:
Gold & Silver — the daily wrap.

Key Facts Gold fund slips: the GLD gold fund closed at US$365.17, down 1.13% on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, and sits 2.6% above its 30 October low.

the GLD gold fund closed at US$365.17, down 1.13% on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, and sits 2.6% above its 30 October low. Silver fund edges up: the SLV silver fund rose 0.37% to US$46.65, a small bounce after a 7.11% fall over 20 sessions.

the SLV silver fund rose 0.37% to US$46.65, a small bounce after a 7.11% fall over 20 sessions. Dollar firms, yields stay high: the dollar index gained 0.60% to 102.84 and the US 10-year Treasury yield stayed near 5%.

the dollar index gained 0.60% to 102.84 and the US 10-year Treasury yield stayed near 5%. Fear fades: the S&P 500 rose 1.31% to 7,619, and the VIX fear gauge fell 10.12% to 17.49, which cut demand for havens.

the S&P 500 rose 1.31% to 7,619, and the VIX fear gauge fell 10.12% to 17.49, which cut demand for havens. Prediction markets: Polymarket prices a 53% chance that gold touches US$4,100 in November (US$130,403 traded, 7:40 p.m. ET, 11 November).

Today’s Focus Gold lost ground on Wednesday while silver held steady, as a stronger dollar and a 10-year US yield at 5% made metals that pay no interest less attractive. The pressure follows Tuesday’s hotter-than-forecast US inflation report. We track both metals through their two biggest exchange-traded funds, GLD for gold and SLV for silver, because the spot feeds for the session closed at different hours and do not line up. The funds close with Wall Street and give one clean reading. GLD is 26.4% below its January high of US$495.90, while SLV is 55.8% below its own January peak of US$105.60. Both sit within 5% of their 30 October lows. 01 The session in one read

Think of gold and silver as seesaw partners of the dollar: when the dollar and interest rates rise, they tend to fall. On Wednesday, 11 November 2026, the gold side of the seesaw tilted down while silver held on.

The GLD fund, which holds physical gold, fell 1.13% to US$365.17. The SLV fund, which holds physical silver, rose 0.37% to US$46.65.

Tuesday’s US consumer-price report was hotter than forecast, which fed the idea that the Federal Reserve, the US central bank, will keep rates high or even raise them. That is bad news for metals that pay no interest, because savers can now earn about 5% on a ten-year government bond.

Assessment — Gold under pressure, silver steady MEDIUM The pattern is the classic one: a firmer dollar and higher yields weighed on gold, while silver, the smaller and more volatile market, bounced a little after a sharp fall. One session proves little, and both funds remain close to their 30 October lows. The variable to watch is the 10-year Treasury yield, since a clear move above 5% would keep both metals on the defensive.

03 Why it moved

First and heaviest was the dollar and yields. The dollar index rose 0.60% to 102.84 and the 10-year Treasury yield stayed near 5% (4.98% at Tuesday’s close, after a jump of about 10 basis points), because the US bond market was shut for Veterans Day. That makes gold dearer for foreign buyers and less rewarding to hold.

Second was a retreat from safety. The S&P 500 climbed 1.31% to 7,619 and the VIX fell 10.12% to 17.49, so investors had less reason to hide in metals.

Third is the metals’ different personalities: silver is both a store of value and an industrial input, so it swings harder than gold, in both directions. Oil was flat, with the USO fund up 0.01%, so it played no part. Our confidence in this ranking is medium-high.

04 The trend behind it

GLD closed 26.4% below its 29 January high of US$495.90 and 2.6% above its 30 October low of US$355.78. It has lost 2.88% over 20 sessions and 8.38% over 60 sessions.

SLV is the sharper story. It is 55.8% below its 28 January high of US$105.60 and 4.6% above its 30 October low of US$44.60, and it has lost 18.78% over 60 sessions. This looks like a long unwinding of last winter’s rally, not a fresh phase.

05 What it means for Latin America

Mexico is the world’s top silver producer, at 172.9 million ounces in 2025, roughly a fifth of world supply, according to the Silver Institute (the industry body) and Metals Focus (a London metals consultancy). Its output fell 5% that year, the third annual decline.

Peru produced 130.6 million ounces in 2025, up 7%. Much of its silver is a by-product of lead and zinc mining, and Peru’s zinc output fell 22.2% in July, so lower prices land on top of a supply problem.

For ordinary savers in Mexico City or Lima, the lesson is that a stronger dollar eases the pull of precious metals as a hedge. For governments, mining taxes and royalties shrink when prices slip.

06 The names to watch

In Mexico, watch Fresnillo and Industrias Peñoles, the country’s best-known silver producers. In Peru, Buenaventura and Southern Copper are the listed names most tied to metal prices.

The Silver Institute and Metals Focus forecast a 46.3 million ounce supply deficit in 2026, the sixth in a row, meaning demand exceeds mine supply. That gap is the main argument that the sell-off is overdone.

07 What would end it

For gold, the line is the GLD low of US$355.78 from 30 October. A close below it would open a new leg down, while holding it keeps the rebound case alive.

For silver, the line is the SLV low of US$44.60 from the same day. The catalysts are the next US inflation and jobs reports and the Federal Reserve’s December meeting. Does this stop? Only when yields stop rising, and a 10-year yield back below 5% would be the first sign.

These prices are bets, not polls. They show traders see a wide range for gold and expect the Fed to raise rates next month.

Why did gold fall while silver edged up?

The GLD gold fund fell 1.13% to US$365.17 as the dollar and Treasury yields rose. The SLV silver fund rose 0.37% to US$46.65, a small bounce after a long slide.

Where are gold and silver compared with their highs?

GLD is 26.4% below its January high and SLV is 55.8% below its own. Both funds sit within 5% of their 30 October lows.

Why does Mexico matter?

Mexico produced 172.9 million ounces in 2025, around a fifth of the world’s silver, so its miners and public finances are sensitive to the price.

Gold and silver rarely help with day-to-day currency needs. Watch the dollar, because a stronger dollar weighs on metals and also changes what your local currency buys abroad.

World.title: US Warns Costa Rica Town Halls Off Chinese Cameras, China Pushes Back
World.content:
The United States and Chinese embassies in Costa Rica have traded public statements over Chinese-made security technology used by the country’s municipalities, the latest in a series of disputes between the two powers playing out in San José. The US Embassy published a message on Facebook warning local governments about the risks of contracting low-cost Chinese technology, including security cameras, license plate readers and digital platforms from Chinese companies.

The embassy cited cybersecurity risks, weak data protection, dependence on a single supplier and a lack of transparency in public procurement. The message did not name any municipality or company. The Chinese Embassy answered with its own Facebook post, rejecting the warnings as unfounded and saying they served US interests. It said Chinese products are widely used in China and abroad, that the cameras and tools help protect people and property, and that commercial activity should not be politicized.

Costa Rica’s government has not publicly responded to the exchange. The camera dispute follows months of friction between the two embassies. In January, US Ambassador Melinda Hildebrand listed Chinese economic influence among the challenges facing Costa Rica. That same month, officials in the government of Rodrigo Chaves linked China to a cyberattack detected against the Costa Rican Electricity Institute (ICE).

In March, Chinese Ambassador Wang Xiaoyao asked Costa Rica for evidence supporting the cyberattack accusation. She said China had sought cybersecurity information from Costa Rican authorities since 2024 without a response. In May, Wang criticized Washington for revoking the visas of several Costa Rican public figures, among them former President Óscar Arias.

In late October, the Chinese Embassy rejected a US Embassy statement on Chinese mining companies, also calling it unfounded. Neither embassy said which Costa Rican municipalities use Chinese equipment or how many such systems are in operation.

World.title: Santa Cruz, Home to Tamarindo, Leads Guanacaste in Murders and Car Break-Ins
World.content:
Santa Cruz has recorded 22 homicides so far this year, more than any other county in Guanacaste and about 29% of the province’s 75 killings, according to figures from the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) covering Jan. 1 to Nov. 9. Costa Rica’s count is up from 20 in the same period of 2025, an increase of 10%. Across Guanacaste, homicides rose from 67 to 75, or 11.9%.

Tamarindo has the most homicides of any area in Santa Cruz, with five. Veintisiete de Abril follows with four, while Cuajiniquil and Cabo Velas, the district that includes Flamingo and Brasilito, have three each. OIJ classifies 15 of the county’s 22 homicides as score-settling or revenge killings. That number is unchanged from last year, so the increase comes from other types of cases.

Santa Cruz also leads the area in break-ins of parked vehicles, with 93 of Guanacaste’s 237 reported cases, or about 39%. Liberia follows with 64 and Nicoya with 34. By district, the most break-ins were reported in central Santa Cruz, with 39, followed by Tamarindo with 25 and Veintisiete de Abril with 23. A further 56 vehicles were reported stolen outright in the county over the same period.

The figures come as OIJ agents and the Public Prosecutor’s Office detained 10 people in Santa Cruz yesterday, among them two officers of the Fuerza Pública and a 16-year-old. Investigators suspect the group of involvement in homicide, attempted homicide, drug sales and violent robberies of cars and motorcycles. Authorities link the suspects to at least 13 motorcycle robberies in which victims were seriously injured.

One case under investigation is a homicide on July 6, 2025, in Belén de Carrillo, where a 56-year-old man was shot and his car was then set on fire with him inside. Investigators also connect the group to an attack on Sept. 10, 2025, in which a 77-year-old rancher was beaten while milking and his pickup truck was stolen. Agents seized three assault rifles and ammunition at the home of a woman who was among those detained. Vladimir Muñoz, the OIJ’s interim deputy director, outlined the violent methods investigators attribute to the group.

None of those detained has been charged, and all are presumed innocent. Prosecutors will determine their legal situation in the coming days. The data follow the death of a French woman who was found shot dead inside her home in Cabo Velas earlier this month. OIJ figures are preliminary and can change as cases are reclassified.

World.title: Dengue Up 58% in Costa Rica as Chikungunya Passes 1,000 Cases
World.content:
Dengue cases in Costa Rica are up almost 58% this year, and chikungunya, a mosquito-borne disease that had been absent from the country for nearly a decade, has now passed 1,000 cases. Most of the chikungunya cases are in Guanacaste. The Ministry of Health has counted 6,594 dengue cases so far in 2026, compared with 4,181 at the same point last year. Of those, 105 were classified as dengue with warning signs, the stage that can turn severe.

As of Nov. 2, three patients were hospitalized with dengue, according to the Costa Rican Social Security System (CCSS). The rise follows a September notice in which the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention flagged Costa Rica for higher-than-expected dengue risk. Alajuela province has the most dengue cases at 2,791, followed by Puntarenas with 981 and San José with 880. By county, Grecia leads with 727, then Alajuela with 658, Orotina with 591, San José with 418 and Puntarenas with 416.

Orotina stands out. It has 2,323.8 cases per 100,000 people, about 18 times the national rate. The town sits on Route 27, the main highway from San José to the Central Pacific beaches. Chikungunya reached 1,049 cases through the 42nd epidemiological week of the year, in mid-October. Of those, 916 were confirmed by lab tests and 133 are probable cases still under study, an increase of 126 in two weeks.

The Chorotega health region, which covers Guanacaste, has 602 chikungunya cases, or 57% of the national total. La Cruz, near the Nicaraguan border, has 389, Carrillo has 90 and Santa Cruz has 64. Outside Guanacaste, Alajuela has 136 and San José has 71. Local transmission was first confirmed in July in a Guanacaste beach town and in Alajuela. In September, the virus reached Pavas, on the west side of San José.

Both diseases spread through mosquito bites, so the best protection is not getting bitten. Use repellent, especially during the day, when the mosquito that carries them is most active, and wear long sleeves when you can. Empty anything around your home that holds water, such as plant saucers, buckets, old tires and clogged gutters. That is where these mosquitoes lay their eggs.

If you get a fever, headache or body aches, see a doctor. Don’t take ibuprofen or aspirin until dengue has been ruled out, because these drugs can raise the risk of bleeding if you have dengue. Get care right away if you notice intense abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding from your gums or nose, or extreme weakness. These are signs that dengue is turning severe.

The dry season, which began this month in Guanacaste and the Central Valley, means fewer puddles. Water stored in tanks and buckets during the dry months can still breed mosquitoes, so keep containers covered.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Dollar Slides Back Toward Its Record Low
World.content:
The dollar has fallen back to within two colones of its all-time low in Costa Rica, erasing most of the rebound it had in early October. The average price on Monex, the wholesale market where banks and other authorized institutions trade dollars, closed yesterday at 448.43 colones, according to Central Bank data. That was the lowest close since Sept. 18 and 1.63 colones above the record of 446.80 set on Sept. 17.

For anyone here paid in dollars, the gap with January keeps widening. On Jan. 2, the first trading day of the year, the Monex average was 497.07 colones, and the dollar exchange rate in Costa Rica has trended lower for most of the months since. At Tuesday’s average, $1,000 converts to 448,430 colones. That is 48,640 colones less than on Jan. 2, a drop of about 9.8% in just over 10 months.

The decline resumed after a brief reversal. Following the September low, the rate climbed to 460.45 colones on Oct. 1, eased through the rest of October and has fallen in each of the last five sessions. The Central Bank has been buying dollars to slow the fall. It purchased $9 million on Friday, Nov. 6, its second consecutive day in the market, bringing its stabilization purchases over the two sessions to $24 million.

The Central Bank’s dollar trading on Monex this year total $2.004 billion, of which $1.288 billion were stabilization operations. The bank says those operations are meant to moderate abrupt swings in the price of the dollar, not to set a fixed exchange rate. Carlos Valerin, an exchange-market specialist, said the October rebound was driven mainly by a 25-basis-point rate increase by the US Federal Reserve, while the Central Bank kept its own policy rate unchanged.

Valerin also pointed to the calendar. November brings aguinaldo payments, the year-end bonus required under Costa Rican law, and transnational companies typically pay the second half of December salaries early, he said. Both concentrate dollar conversions into a few weeks.

Central Bank President Róger Madrigal has described a risk running the other way. He said the gap between Costa Rican and US interest rates is likely to widen, which could encourage saving in foreign currency and capital outflows. When interest rates favor a foreign currency, Madrigal said, demand for that currency rises, which in principle should push the exchange rate up. He said the bank is monitoring the situation closely.

The strong colón has squeezed businesses that earn in dollars and pay their costs in colones, from coffee growers to medical tourism providers. It has also cut the purchasing power of residents who live on pensions or other income from abroad. Monex is a wholesale market, so the rates offered at bank windows differ from its daily average. Banks add a margin when they buy and sell dollars, and that margin varies from one institution to another.

The rate now sits closer to its record than at any point since September, and the next few days will show whether the year-end flow of dollars pushes it through.

World.title: Costa Rica Mourns Actor and TV Host Leonardo Perucci, Dead at 87
World.content:
Leonardo Perucci, the Chilean-born actor, director and television host who became one of the most familiar faces on Costa Rican screens and stages, died Tuesday, Nov. 10, at age 87. His daughter, Valeria Perucci, confirmed his death. For a generation of Costa Ricans, Perucci was the host of Fantástico, the Channel 7 variety program that aired from 1985 to 1995. He also appeared on Fabulosos Sábados and later co-hosted the morning show Giros on Repretel.

Perucci had undergone a heart procedure on Monday to treat a blocked coronary artery, according to local reports. His family has not released an official cause of death. Born in Antofagasta, Chile, on Dec. 13, 1938, Perucci began acting professionally in the early 1960s. In 1967 he starred in Los Días Jóvenes, widely regarded as Chile’s first telenovela, and went on to appear in 14 Chilean soap operas.

After the 1973 military coup in Chile, he went into exile in Cuba, where he spent about five years working as an actor, director and playwright. He arrived in Costa Rica in 1979 and never left. Within two weeks of his arrival he was on stage in Fuenteovejuna, directed by Atahualpa del Cioppo. As a member of the National Theater Company, he went on to perform in productions including Pedro y el capitán and La visita de la vieja dama, becoming part of Costa Rica’s long theater tradition.

He also worked extensively behind the scenes, directing plays and training young actors in university classrooms. On screen, he appeared in Costa Rican films including Caribe and Buscando a Marcos Ramírez. In 2004 he returned to Chilean television for a new run of telenovelas, among them Brujas, Descarado and Papi Ricky. The roles introduced him to a new generation of viewers in the country where his career began.

The Universidad Nacional (UNA) honored Perucci with the Universidad Nacional Medal, its highest institutional distinction, which he received alongside his wife, the writer and actress Arabella Salaverry. Culture and Youth Minister Jorge Rodríguez said he had just learned of the death of a leading figure of Costa Rican theater and television. He extended his condolences to Perucci’s family, friends and the country’s arts community.

A wake is scheduled for today from 4 p.m. at the Funeraria del Magisterio, with a memorial Mass planned for Thursday at the San Juan Bosco church, according to arrangements announced by his family. The time of the Mass had not yet been confirmed. Reflecting on his life in Costa Rica in a past interview, Perucci said he would run out of years before he could fully thank Costa Rica for everything it had given him, as an artist and as a person.

World.title: Women in Costa Rica Can Now Choose a Female Uber Driver
World.content:
Women who use Uber in Costa Rica can now ask to be driven by another woman. The company launched the option, called Uber Mujeres, yesterday. It is rolling out gradually across the Greater Metropolitan Area this week and works only with UberX for now. If you don’t see it in your app yet, that’s why.

There is a catch since Uber says availability depends on how many women drivers are connected when you make your request, so a match isn’t guaranteed. You can use the option in three ways. Choose Uber Mujeres when you request a ride right away, if it appears in your app. Book a trip in advance through the app’s reservation feature, or set it as your default so the app prioritizes women drivers on future trips.

To set it as your default, open the app, go to Account and scroll to your ride preferences. In the Spanish-language version of the app, the setting reads “Prefiero viaje con socias colaboradoras,” meaning you prefer trips with women drivers. The size of the pool is the real limit. Women make up more than 10% of Uber’s active drivers in Costa Rica, according to the company, and its press office puts their number at roughly 3,400 to 4,000.

Uber says the number of active women drivers has grown more than 272% over the past five years. Even so, most people driving for the platform in Latin America are men. Laura Santillán, Uber’s general manager for Costa Rica, Panama and the Caribbean, said in an interview that the company aims to raise the share of women drivers to 20% within five years.

The company says the idea grew out of Uber Ellas, a feature launched in 2020 that lets women drivers choose to take trips only with women passengers. Santillán said that experience, along with feedback from riders, led Uber to give women passengers the same choice. Before the launch, Uber surveyed a group of its women users in Costa Rica. According to the company, 90% said a woman-driver option was very or somewhat important, and 95% said offering it showed Uber was listening to women’s needs.

Respondents said they would be most likely to use it for trips at night, when traveling alone and on longer rides. Uber has not published the survey’s sample size or methodology. Costa Rica is the sixth country in Latin America to get Uber Mujeres, the company said. It is the latest addition to an app that already lets you book Costa Rica’s red taxis.

Ride-hailing apps still operate in Costa Rica without a law written specifically for them. A bill to regulate platforms such as Uber and DiDi remains before the Legislative Assembly, years after the apps reshaped the taxi market. Uber has not said when Uber Mujeres will reach areas outside the Greater Metropolitan Area or other ride types beyond UberX.

World.title: Teachers Strike Today as 11 Groups March Through Downtown San José
World.content:
If you plan to drive, ride a bus or walk through downtown San José this morning, expect delays. Teachers’ unions and public universities are holding a one-day strike today with a march from Parque La Merced to the Legislative Assembly. The march is set to leave La Merced at 9 a.m., according to the Ministry of Public Education (MEP) and several of the organizing groups. One union call puts the gathering at 10 a.m., so crowds may build over the whole morning.

The route crosses the city center to the Plaza de la Democracia, in front of Congress. No official road closures had been announced by early Wednesday. Plan for slow traffic on the main avenues through the center and around the Plaza de la Democracia from mid-morning until the crowd disperses. If you can, avoid the area or give yourself extra time, much as you would have during last month’s university march.

Eleven unions and education groups have backed the strike, including the main teachers’ unions ANDE, APSE and SEC, university staff unions and the teachers’ professional association, Colypro. The University of Costa Rica and the National University (UNA) have authorized staff and students to take part. The National Technical University (UTN) has called on its students and staff to join.

Organizers say the 2027 budget falls far short of the constitutional target of 8% of GDP for education. APSE puts next year’s education spending at 4.9% of GDP. Unions are also demanding unpaid salary adjustments and payment of what the state owes the teachers’ pension fund, Jupema.

APSE says that pension debt still tops 44,000 million colones (about $97.6 million), even after a 30,000 million colón payment (about $66.5 million) announced by the MEP. The union also says about 50,000 million colones ($110.9 million) is missing from the 2027 budget to cover pension obligations.

Universities have their own grievance. Lawmakers approved a cut of 8,048 million colones (about $17.8 million) to the Special Fund for Higher Education (FEES) for 2027, part of the dispute that drove thousands into the streets in October. The National Rectors’ Council (CONARE) and the public universities say that money is part of 62,590 million colones (about $138.8 million) postponed in 2020 and 2021 that the government agreed to repay in installments, and that the first installment has not been paid.

University budgets also pay for public services outside the classroom, such as round-the-clock tsunami monitoring. Education Minister Leonardo Sánchez has rejected the unions’ arguments, saying their motives are more political than technical. He said that if classes are suspended, the ministry will ask the Attorney General’s Office (PGR) within 24 hours to seek a court ruling on whether the strike is legal.

If you have children in public school, the MEP has ordered all schools to stay open today. Schools must keep cleaning and security staff on duty and continue serving meals and special-education services, the ministry said. Whether your child’s teacher works depends on the school, so check with the school directly.

The strike comes as the government looks for savings across the board, with a revenue shortfall of $882 million squeezing courts, police and schools. Public schools have also lost 180,000 students in five years. The fight now moves to the final vote on the 2027 budget, which the Constitutional Chamber has barred lawmakers from approving in second debate before Nov. 29. Whatever happens on the streets today, that vote will decide how much money schools, universities and courts have to work with next year.

World.title: A Quiet Island Escape in Costa Rica’s Gulf of Nicoya
World.content:
A three-hour journey and a short boat ride from my home in Costa Rica took me somewhere that felt much farther away. Isla Jesusita sits in the Gulf of Nicoya near Paquera, surrounded by forested hills, calm water and small islands crowded with birds. I went there for two nights at Isla Chiquita Glamping Hotel, expecting a comfortable little escape.

What I found was one of those places where the surroundings quickly became more important than the accommodation.My arrival was gray, misty and cooler than I expected. I had pictured bright tropical sunshine, but the hills were wrapped in clouds and the Gulf had an almost rainforest feel. I immediately wished I had packed a light jacket.

A few hours later, the rain stopped and the sky produced one of the most beautiful sunsets I have seen in Costa Rica. By the next morning, the water was calm and the sun was shining. I liked the changeability of it. Nothing felt staged. The island seemed to shift with the weather.

The setting reminded me of Tsowa Safari Island, a tented camp where I stayed on the Zambezi River near Victoria Falls. Obviously, the Gulf of Nicoya is very different from the Zambezi, but the feeling was remarkably similar. In both places, I felt as though I was staying inside the landscape rather than looking at it from a conventional hotel.

My air-conditioned canvas tent was comfortable without separating me from what was happening outside. I could hear the sounds of the island, walk down to the water within minutes and spend much of the day outdoors. The property is small enough that it never felt crowded during my stay, which became one of the things I appreciated most.

The beach itself is not the kind of broad white-sand beach people often picture when they think about Costa Rica. It is smaller and quieter, and I found myself paying attention to things I might normally have walked past. At low tide, for example, the wet sand was covered with elaborate flower- and fern-like patterns created by tiny crabs feeding beneath the surface. At first, I wasn’t quite sure what I was looking at. Once I realized what was making them, I kept stopping to examine the patterns.

There is also a forest trail through the island. I had intended to explore it, but after the rain, I took one look at the mud, exposed roots and steeper sections and reconsidered. I had brought water shoes rather than proper walking shoes, so the beach won. It was a good reminder that glamping does not necessarily mean every part of the experience is manicured.

One of my favorite parts of the stay was actually how little I felt I needed to do. I slept incredibly well. One morning, I woke around five to the sound of howler monkeys somewhere in the distance and stayed in bed listening to them for a while. Eventually, I wandered down for breakfast and spent much of the morning simply enjoying the water and the quiet.

That pace worked particularly well for me as a solo traveler. There was enough privacy that I could disappear with a book or walk by myself, but I never felt isolated. The excursions provided natural opportunities to meet other people without requiring me to organize my trip around a group.

I met a couple from Austin on a sunset cruise through the Gulf. As we traveled among the small islands and rocky shoreline, we watched frigatebirds circling overhead, large groups of birds filling the trees and bright red crabs clinging to the rocks. Then the sky began to change. Orange, pink and lavender spread across the water while the islands became dark silhouettes. Every few minutes, the colors shifted again. I have lived in Costa Rica long enough to know that the country does spectacular sunsets very well, but this one was exceptional.

Later that evening, we went back onto the water for a bioluminescence excursion. We were given nets to move through the water, triggering flashes of light from the tiny organisms below the surface. The glowing water was fascinating, but what surprised me just as much was the sky. Away from the brighter lights, the stars were spectacular. For a few minutes, there was light above me and light below me.

That was probably my favorite moment of the trip. The Gulf of Nicoya does not always get the attention given to Costa Rica’s more famous beach destinations. That may be part of its appeal. From the water, the landscape feels less like a beach resort corridor and more like a collection of islands, forest, fishing communities and stretches of undeveloped coastline.

It also felt refreshingly uncrowded. There were no lines, no packed beaches and none of the sense that everyone was competing for the same photograph. The experience was quieter and more intimate than that. For travelers interested in making a similar trip, Isla Chiquita is located on Isla Jesusita near Paquera. Guests arriving from the Guanacaste side travel by road to a mainland meeting point at Punta Cuchillos, where a small hotel boat provides the final transfer to the island. The boat ride is short, but it creates a definite psychological break between the mainland and the stay.

My two-night air-conditioned tent stay, including breakfast, cost $460. My share of the sunset cruise and bioluminescence excursion brought my accommodation-and-activity total to a little over $556 before additional meals, drinks and incidentals. Those were the prices during my November 2026 visit and should be checked directly before planning a trip.

I would also pack differently next time. Comfortable walking shoes would make the forest trail much more practical, particularly during the rainy season, and I would bring a light sweater or jacket. Costa Rica may be tropical, but an evening on the water after rain can feel surprisingly cool.

I would return, but not because Isla Jesusita offers a checklist of things to do. In fact, almost the opposite was true. What I enjoyed was waking to monkeys, watching the tide expose tiny signs of life on the beach, seeing islands filled with birds and sitting on the water as the sky changed color. It gave me the scenery and solitude I wanted, but enough interaction with other travelers that being there alone never felt lonely.

Sometimes a short trip does not need to be packed with activities to feel like an adventure. Sometimes it is enough to go somewhere quiet and pay attention.

About the Author

Jennifer Pietrzak-Wahl is a retired technology executive and solo traveler living in Costa Rica. She writes about independent travel, immersive experiences and the practical realities of exploring the world later in life. Her travels have taken her from safari camps in Africa to the Scottish Highlands and islands throughout the Caribbean, with a particular interest in experiences that combine culture, nature and a strong sense of place.

World.title: PM Briceño unable to say how much controversial Ambergris Caye road project will cost, says Town Council spearheading development
World.content:
PM Briceño unable to say how much controversial Ambergris Caye road project will cost, says Town Council spearheading development

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Prime Minister John Briceño says the controversial road development project in northern Ambergris Caye is intended to provide access to thousands of previously distributed land parcels, but acknowledged that he does not know the project’s exact cost.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Briceño was questioned about the construction of the road, including its estimated cost and the contractors involved.

The Prime Minister explained that the project forms part of a broader development plan for Ambergris Caye, which includes improving access to land in the northern portion of the island.

According to Briceño, approximately 1,000 lots have already been distributed in the north, where the terrain is more suitable for development than other areas that are largely swampy.

He said a road is necessary to allow landowners to access their properties.

Briceño explained that the San Pedro Town Council had taken the initiative to begin implementing the plan, arguing that development projects cannot advance unless work gets underway.

However, when pressed to disclose the cost of the road, the Prime Minister acknowledged that he did not have the exact figure available.

He also faced questions about the identity of the contractor and whether the project was linked to a particular individual, but the supplied exchange ended before any substantive answer to those questions was recorded.

The project has attracted scrutiny over its cost, environmental implications and the lack of publicly available information about contractors and funding.

According to reporting on the wider Ambergris Caye development proposals, questions have also been raised about the origins of construction materials and the extent of public consultation.

The road forms part of a broader discussion about development in northern Ambergris Caye, including a proposed new airport and other major infrastructure projects.

While Briceño defended the need to provide access to landowners, his latest comments leave unanswered questions about the road’s total price tag, construction arrangements and financial oversight.

World.title: PM Briceño warns San Pedro airstrip has been outgrown, says schoolchildren fear planes could crash into their school
World.content:
PM Briceño warns San Pedro airstrip has been outgrown, says schoolchildren fear planes could crash into their school

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Prime Minister John Briceño says San Pedro’s tourism industry has outgrown the existing municipal airstrip, warning that increasing aircraft traffic, congestion and safety concerns make long-term planning for a new airport necessary.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Briceño defended his administration’s exploration of a new airport on Ambergris Caye, amid opposition from tourism stakeholders and residents concerned about the future of the existing facility.

The Prime Minister clarified that his previous reference to increasing aircraft activity was not a claim that the island’s visitor arrivals had surpassed pre-pandemic levels.

Instead, he said that during peak tourism periods, the existing airport experiences exceptionally heavy aircraft movements, with as many as 55 landings per hour at certain times.

Briceño warned that such concentrations of aircraft could present safety challenges, particularly as tourism continues expanding.

He explained that one possible solution would be to accommodate larger aircraft capable of transporting more passengers per flight, but the existing municipal airstrip is physically constrained and cannot accommodate the required expansion.

The Prime Minister also highlighted concerns about nearby schools, saying that during a survey, students expressed fears that an aircraft could one day crash into their school.

He said government must consider not only the future of tourism but also congestion, aircraft noise, the impact on schoolchildren and the safety of passengers.

Briceño stressed that the proposed airport remains in the planning stage and that government is working with airlines to assess possible solutions.

He also confirmed that the plans would be made public once completed.

The proposal has generated considerable opposition on Ambergris Caye.

As BBN previously reported, tourism stakeholders have opposed the proposed construction of a new airport near Secret Beach and urged government to prioritize existing infrastructure, traffic congestion, waste management and other pressing island needs.

The San Pedro Town Council has also formally voted against closing the current John Greif II Airstrip.

Briceño previously confirmed that the government has not made a final decision on constructing the new facility, with technical studies being undertaken with assistance from the Inter-American Development Bank.

Breaking Belize News+2

World.title: PM Briceño says controversial extra gate at Corozal Free Zone has been closed, denies U.S. demanded closure of Free Zone
World.content:
PM Briceño says controversial extra gate at Corozal Free Zone has been closed, denies U.S. demanded closure of Free Zone

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Prime Minister John Briceño says an additional gate at the Corozal Commercial Free Zone has been closed as authorities continue efforts to address concerns surrounding cigarette trafficking and the possible involvement of Mexican drug cartels.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Briceño was questioned about the situation at the Free Zone following recent major cigarette seizures in Mexico and concerns about pressure from the United States.

The Prime Minister said that, as far as he was aware, the additional gate previously operating at the facility had been closed.

He also confirmed that American officials had visited the Free Zone and were shown the measures and operations being implemented.

Briceño maintained that Belize was doing its best to address the concerns.

Asked whether American authorities had been pressuring Belize over activities at the Free Zone, the Prime Minister said U.S. officials had never approached him to demand that the facility be closed.

However, he acknowledged that concerns had been raised about the potential infiltration of Belize by Mexican drug cartels, reiterating his longstanding position that everything possible must be done to keep those criminal organizations out of the country.

Briceño also suggested that the movement of cigarettes exported from the Free Zone into Mexico was a matter for Mexican authorities to address.

The discussion comes as Mexican authorities intensify their crackdown on illicit cigarette trafficking.

On November 6, Mexico’s Secretariat of the Navy announced that authorities had seized approximately 481 million illicit cigarettes, equivalent to 678 tonnes, between 2024 and 2026.

Mexican authorities estimated the seizures had disrupted criminal operations by approximately 2.375 billion Mexican pesos, identifying organized crime networks, particularly the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, among those affected.

The Mexican report did not establish that those seizures originated from Belize’s Corozal Free Zone.

The Prime Minister’s comments nevertheless underscore the continuing scrutiny surrounding the Free Zone and efforts to prevent cross-border criminal activity.

World.title: PM Briceño praises José Mai as one of Belize’s best Agriculture Ministers, says he would consider bringing him back to Cabinet
World.content:
PM Briceño praises José Mai as one of Belize’s best Agriculture Ministers, says he would consider bringing him back to Cabinet

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Prime Minister John Briceño has described former Agriculture Minister José Abelardo Mai as one of the best persons to have held the portfolio since before Belize’s independence, while confirming that he would consider bringing the Orange Walk South Area Representative back into Cabinet.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Briceño was asked whether he was considering reappointing Mai, who has expressed his readiness to return to ministerial duties.

Briceño praised Mai’s performance in agriculture, describing him as one of the country’s best Agriculture Ministers in decades.

However, the Prime Minister explained that Cabinet appointments require balancing responsibilities among ministers, and he has already established his current Cabinet.

He indicated that if he decides to make changes at an appropriate time, Mai would certainly be among those considered.

Briceño also acknowledged his responsibility to the entire Cabinet, explaining that ministerial appointments involve maintaining the proper balance within government.

Mai stepped down from Cabinet in November 2025 amid health concerns and subsequently underwent two surgical procedures on his right knee.

As BBN reported on November 9, Mai recently returned from Mérida, Mexico, where he underwent a second procedure and continued physical therapy.

Rodwell Ferguson currently holds the Agriculture portfolio.

Mai has indicated that he expects to be sufficiently recovered to resume full duties within the coming months, although he acknowledges that any return to Cabinet remains entirely at the Prime Minister’s discretion.

World.title: PM Briceño sees no reason for Godfrey Smith’s U.S. visa revocation, refuses to speculate on possible China connection
World.content:
PM Briceño sees no reason for Godfrey Smith’s U.S. visa revocation, refuses to speculate on possible China connection

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Prime Minister John Briceño says he sees no reason why the United States revoked the visa of former Foreign Minister and Attorney General Godfrey Smith, but acknowledges that Washington has the right to determine who is permitted to enter their country.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, November 11, Briceño said that while he considers Smith an outstanding Belizean, decisions concerning U.S. visas rest entirely with the American government.

The Prime Minister explained that anyone applying for a visa is essentially requesting permission to enter another country as a guest, and that country has the authority to accept or reject the request.

Asked whether the revocation could be interpreted as a warning to Belize against strengthening relations with China, Briceño declined to speculate, saying he could not comment on something he did not know.

Smith’s visa was revoked by the U.S. Department of State on November 7, with the decision communicated to him through the U.S. Embassy in Belmopan. No specific reason was publicly disclosed.

Smith has suggested that the decision could be connected to his advocacy for Belize to establish diplomatic relations with mainland China instead of Taiwan. He has also facilitated exchanges involving Belizeans travelling to China.

Smith has maintained that he has done nothing wrong and says he will neither appeal the decision nor apply for another U.S. visa.

As BBN previously reported, Smith also offered to resign as Chairman of a Commission of Inquiry in Guyana following the visa revocation, but President Irfaan Ali rejected his offer.

World.title: Man accused of grabbing woman’s butt, pulling knife on her then threatening to kill her and her man remanded to prison
World.content:
Man accused of grabbing woman’s butt, pulling knife on her then threatening to kill her and her man remanded to prison

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 47-year-old Belize City man accused of sexually assaulting a woman, threatening to kill her and her partner, and confronting her with a pocketknife has been remanded to the Belize Central Prison after prosecutors successfully objected to bail.

Jason Meighan, a maintenance worker of Sittee Street, appeared unrepresented before Senior Magistrate Dennison Mannon on Wednesday, November 11, where he was charged with one count of sexual assault, two counts of threat of death and one count of aggravated assault.

According to allegations, on November 8, Meighan sexually assaulted the woman by touching her right buttock without her consent. He is also accused of pulling a pocketknife on her after inappropriately touching her and telling her: “Gial, I nuh give ah f**k about yuh pickney pah, I wah kill you and he.”

Prosecutors further alleged that on November 9, Meighan again threatened the woman, telling her, “F**k you and yuh man. I wah kill you and your man.”

Meighan pleaded not guilty to all four charges.

The prosecution strongly objected to bail, arguing that the alleged incidents occurred on two consecutive days and that Meighan posed a risk of reoffending or interfering with the complainant if released. The prosecutor also cited the prevalence of sexual assault and threats of death in Belize.

When given an opportunity to explain why he should be granted bail, Meighan maintained his innocence, telling the court, “Honestly, I never do it.”

He also claimed to have evidence supporting his denial of the allegations.

However, the magistrate was not persuaded to grant bail, and Meighan was remanded to the Belize Central Prison.

His next court appearance is scheduled for December 15, 2026.

World.title: 20-year-old Jahdey Castillo caught with loaded gun following Belize City Post Office burglary; remanded to prison – wanted for questioning in other crimes
World.content:
20-year-old Jahdey Castillo caught with loaded gun following Belize City Post Office burglary; remanded to prison – wanted for questioning in other crimes

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 20-year-old man caught carrying a loaded firearm near the Belize City Post Office during an early-morning burglary has been remanded to prison and is now being sought for questioning in connection with other criminal investigations in Belize City and northern Belize.

Jahdey Castillo, a bodywork technician originally from Hopkins Village and currently residing on Neal Penn Road in Belize City, appeared before Senior Magistrate Dennison Mannon on Wednesday, November 11, charged with keeping a firearm and ammunition without a gun licence.

Castillo pleaded not guilty to both charges but was denied bail and remanded to the Belize Central Prison until January 22, 2027.

The charges stem from a burglary reported around 2:50 a.m. on Tuesday at the Belize City Post Office, located at the corner of North Front Street and Pickstock Street.

A police officer and two Belize Defence Force soldiers responded to the area, where they encountered Castillo running from the direction of Rhaburn Alley wearing black clothing and a face mask while carrying what appeared to be a firearm.

The officer ordered Castillo to drop the weapon, and he complied before being detained.

Police subsequently recovered a SIG Sauer P320 pistol loaded with 15 live rounds of 9mm ammunition, including seven Luger-brand rounds and eight Smith & Wesson rounds.

The incident occurred as police investigated a daring burglary at the Post Office, where several suspects reportedly disabled electricity meters, forced open shutters, shattered a glass window and removed safes from the building. Authorities reported that approximately $200 was stolen.

However, Castillo’s legal troubles may not be over. Immediately following his arraignment, Criminal Investigation Branch officers escorted him back to the Queen Street Police Station for further questioning.

Police reportedly want to question Castillo in connection with several other allegations under investigation in Belize City, Orange Walk and Corozal. Additional charges are expected, although none had been confirmed in those matters at the time of his arraignment.

Castillo has not been formally charged with the Post Office burglary itself.

The investigation continues.

World.title: Ministry of Education and U.B. launch Gwendolyn Lizarraga Scholarship
World.content:
Ministry of Education and U.B. launch Gwendolyn Lizarraga Scholarship

By Zoila Palma: Today, Francis Fonseca, Minister of Education, attended the launch of the Gwendolyn Lizarraga Scholarship, established in honour of Belize’s newly designated National Hero, Gwendolyn Lizarraga.

Through a collaborative effort between the Ministry of Education, Culture, Science and Technology, the University of Belize and the National Institute of Culture and History, 5 scholarships will be awarded to new students pursuing a degree in History at the University of Belize.

“This initiative seeks to carry forward the legacy of Lizarraga by encouraging a deeper understanding of Belize’s history and supporting young Belizeans in pursuing higher education,” NICH noted.

NICH says that by investing in the next generation of historians, we are also investing in the preservation of our national story.

World.title: Gov’t cautions Jamaicans against employment offers linked to Russia-Ukraine war
World.content:
In this file photo Ukrainian soldiers drive in a military truck along a road in the Kharkiv region on July 30, 2026, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Photo by Roman PILIPEY / AFP)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — The Government of Jamaica has become the latest Caribbean nation to warn its citizens to avoid recruitment offers to participate in foreign wars or conflicts.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade issued the warning in a press release on Wednesday amid a wider caution regarding overseas employment opportunities advertised through social media, messaging platforms and other online channels.

The Government mentioned in particular those offering unusually high salaries, travel assistance or expedited immigration arrangements.

“It has come to the Government’s attention that there are international reports of foreign nationals being recruited to participate in Russia’s war against Ukraine including through s on social media,” it said.

Noting that the Government could not verify the legitimacy or authenticity of the reported overseas employment offers, it said it is however aware of international media reports of persons recruited from various countries to participate in that war, including accusations of ill-treatment of Africans and persons of African descent as well as misrepresentation of duties, difficulties in receiving payments and difficulties in returning to their home countries or onward travel.

“Jamaicans are therefore strongly encouraged to avoid such recruitment offers. The ministry further reminds that participation in foreign armed conflicts carries serious risks to personal safety including ultimately to life, and may also expose individuals to legal, immigration and consular complications,” it said.

“ The Government of Jamaica also wishes to advise that neither it, nor international humanitarian organisations can guarantee consular or humanitarian assistance or safe repatriation from active conflict zones,” the Government added.

The warning follows similar bulletins issued by the Dominican Republic.

READ: Lured to war: Caribbean men recruited by Russia with promises of work

The ministry is urging Jamaicans more widely to exercise due diligence in verifying the legitimacy of overseas employment offers, recruitment agencies and prospective employers before making travel arrangements or providing personal documents.

“Particular caution should be exercised where recruiters request passport information, advance payments or the signing of contracts that have not been independently verified or fully understood,” the ministry added.

Jamaicans at home who receive suspicious recruitment offers are encouraged to report the matter to the Ministry of Labour and Social Security. Those already overseas who believe they have been misled or coerced into military service should seek assistance from the nearest Jamaican diplomatic or consular mission, where it is safe to do so.

Persons may consult the Ministry of Labour and Social Security’s list of licensed employment agencies at www.mlss.gov.jm or contact its Employment Agencies Unit to seek verification of overseas employment opportunities.

World.title: ‘You said it’: Cardi B calls out Ryan Burke, apologises to Jamaican gov’t
World.content:
Cardi B (Photo: billboard.com)

American rapper Cardi B has apologised to the Jamaican Government after making claims that it had offered to cover the outstanding balance of her performance fee for BZR WKND, which was scheduled to take place from October 16 to 18.

During an Instagram live on Tuesday, the Grammy-winning artiste claimed that event organiser Ryan Burke had sent an email indicating that the Jamaican Government had invested in the festival.

“I want to apologise to the Government of Jamaica… Motherf***s was putting y’all name in the finesse. I got text messages…And in two hours from now, I challenge a motherf**** to call my bluff. Call my bluff. Cause I’m gonna post this email and I’m gonna post this text message where you, Ryan…I got an email from you telling my people, you said it, that the Government invested in the festival, you said it. Now, I dont know if that’s true or not cause like I said, everything was a finesse,” the rapper said.

“It was a finesse from the beginning because you presented the show as a festival and then you presented it as a Cardi B concert cause you was expecting me to pay for the production for the whole festival. You sent an email saying that the Government, you sent it. You did!” she continued.

Cardi B added, “I give you two hours to call my bluff, cause now y’all p*ssing me off.”

Her apology follows a statement from the Ministry of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport denying any financial involvement in the proposed concert.

The ministry clarified that it had made no commitment or payment towards Cardi B’s appearance fee or any other expenses associated with the event. It further emphasised that BZR WKND was a private commercial engagement in which the Government had no involvement.

The development comes amid an escalating dispute between the Bodak Yellow rapper and the festival’s organisers following her withdrawal from the event.

On Monday, Cardi B threatened legal action against the organisers after reports emerged that they intended to sue her over her cancellation.

BZR WKND Chief Executive Officer Ryan Burke disclosed the organisers’ intention to pursue legal action during an interview this week with CVM News.

The controversy has since intensified, with both parties publicly disputing the circumstances surrounding the rapper’s cancelled performance.
