World.title: Polish government ministers suggest tighter gun controls after deadly terrorist shooting
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. In the wake of Saturday’s deadly terrorist shooting in Kraków, a deputy defence minister has called for debate on limiting the number and types of weapons people can own. Meanwhile, a deputy interior minister says the tragedy provides an “incentive” to revisit proposals to better register certain guns. Poland has among the lowest levels of gun ownership in Europe, though the number of firearms licences being issued has risen in recent years and some politicians have called for expanded access to guns. Saturday’s attack was carried out by a man who legally owned firearms. On Saturday, 24-year-old Michał Oksiński drove through the historic city centre of Kraków, which was packed with tourists and locals, firing at random from his car. He killed six people and injured over a dozen more. Later in the day, the bodies of the perpetrator’s parents and sister were found in his home, where they had been shot dead. Oksiński’s rampage was brought to an end in a shootout with two police officers, which left all three with serious injuries. On Monday morning, the police announced that Oksiński had died in hospital. One of the police officers remains in what is described as “serious but stable” condition. The man who carried out Saturday’s deadly terrorist attack in the Polish city of Kraków has died in hospital from the injuries he sustained during a shootout with police. One of the two officers who stopped him remains in serious but stable condition https://t.co/rT1YBXhkp7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 9, 2026 The incident has caused shock in Poland, a country that has never previously experienced this type of mass public shooting. Speaking to Polsat News on Sunday, deputy defence minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka said that the tragedy “is the best illustration that it makes no sense to talk about expanding access to firearms”. She added that “it’s already relatively easy” to obtain a gun licence, which can be granted to anyone aged 21 or over who has passed the relevant tests and declared that the firearm is for sporting purposes. Both Oksiński and his father had such licences and legally owned 11 firearms. “I would like to start a discussion about whether access to such a large number of weapons should actually be so easy,” said Sobkowiak-Czarnecka. “This is also a question of whether someone who uses weapons for sporting purposes should have so many different types of weapons stored at home.” Also speaking to Polsat on Sunday, Czesław Mroczek, a deputy interior minister, said that “weapons are certainly a challenge for us”. He noted that “in Poland we have had many cases of killings using black powder weapons, for which there is not even a register, let alone a permit procedure”. Such weapons use traditional black powder rather than modern smokeless powder and include firearms manufactured before 1885 and their modern replicas. According to a recent study by researchers from the Jagiellonian University in Kraków, they make up a considerable proportion of firearm-related fatalities in the country. While noting that the issue is not directly related to the Kraków attacks, Mroczek said that plans to include these weapons in a register had already been drawn up and “this event [in Kraków] is an incentive for us to reexamine the matter”. 🇵🇱 Poland's interior ministry says black-powder guns, currently exempt from registration, will be entered into the register. The Krakow attack is described as an impulse to review the whole permit system.https://t.co/Nh7dr46MJ7 — Олег Рощин (@oleg_roshchin) November 9, 2026 On Monday morning, the spokesman for the National Prosecutor’s Office, Przemysław Nowak, held a press conference at which he provided further details on their findings so far. He revealed that Oksiński had been found with two AR-15 rifles and two handguns on his person and in his car, as well as around 500 rounds of ammunition. He had earlier fired “several dozen, possibly several hundred, shots”. A further seven guns had been found at Oksiński’s home. The total of 11 firearms matched the number of weapons there were permits for, noted Nowak, quoted by news website Wirtualna Polska. “The entire matter related to the weapons and the firearms permits will be reviewed,” added the spokesman. “We know that, since March of this year, he [Oksiński] has held firearms permits for one rifle and one pistol.” Prosecutors have launched a terror investigation into Saturday’s shooting in Kraków, which left six dead. Three more bodies were later found in the suspect's home. Further details have also emerged about the heroic actions of police and medical personnel https://t.co/icBJWLRK7c — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 8, 2026 Although gun ownership in Poland is relatively low, it has been rising steadily in recent years, particularly since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, with the total number of registered firearms owned by Poles surpassing 1 million, up from around 380,000 in 2014. Last year, a record 50,709 new gun licences were issued in the country in 2025, up 10.6% compared to a year earlier. Under Polish law, civilians can apply for licences for sporting, hunting, collecting and personal protection purposes. To obtain one, applicants must undergo medical examinations, pass a test, and join a relevant association, such as the Polish Sports Shooting Association, the Polish Hunting Association, or a collectors’ group. Licences for sports and collection purposes are the most popular types of permits, together making up 76% of last year’s permits. But the number of licences issued for “personal protection” has grown from just 81 in 2021 to 7,254 last year. A record 50,709 gun licences were issued in Poland last year and the total number of registered firearms has now surpassed 1 million. Gun ownership in Poland has risen particularly rapidly since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 https://t.co/axt2YS044Z — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 11, 2026 Access to firearms widened in 2023 under the former government, when parliament passed a law removing “unnecessary administrative and legal barriers.” That allowed members of uniformed services to apply for personal protection permits, a change lawmakers said was intended to “strengthen Poland’s defence potential”. However, some politicians, especially on the right, have pushed for ownership rules to be further loosened. In September, speaking at the opening of a shooting range, President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, called for “public discussion about responsible access to weapons”. “Even in the European Union, Poland remains at the bottom of the list in terms of access to firearms,” he said, quoted by Polsat. “Only about 1% of Polish citizens have access to weapons and are skilled at using them. Fortunately, I’m in that 1%.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Fugitive Polish opposition politician Zbigniew Ziobro, who fled to the United States rather than face criminal charges in his homeland, has been pictured attending a gala at Donald Trump’s luxury Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida. The US president himself spoke at the event. The Polish justice minister has responded by saying that he hopes the US will show “true friendship” by cooperating with Poland’s request to extradite Ziobro, just as Poland would do if an American fugitive was on its territory. Ziobro na przyjęciu w rezydencji Trumpa. Wiadomo, co podano na eleganckiej kolacji w Mar-a-Lago [ZDJĘCIA] https://t.co/geANxBTn0J — Andrzej Holinka 🇵🇱 #Nawrocki2030 🇵🇱 ✌️ (@HolinkaPis) November 7, 2026 On Saturday, Blask Online, a news website linked to conservative broadcaster TV Republika, published images of Ziobro at Mar-a-Lago alongside senior Republika figures. The cheapest tickets to attend the gala cost $2,500, ranging up to $7,500 for VIP access. Blask Online’s photos show Ziobro eating dinner at the event and speaking to former British Prime Minister Liz Truss. Trump himself addressed the guests, saying that he “wants to congratulate everybody here”. Nikodem Rachoń, an advisor to Polish President Karol Nawrocki – who is aligned with the opposition and is a close Trump ally – also attended the CPAC event, where he was listed as a speaker. Ziobro is a deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s main opposition party, which is aligned with Trump and his Republican Party. From 2015 to 2023, Ziobro served as justice minister in a PiS-led government, overseeing judicial reforms that are widely seen as having undermined the rule of law. After a new, more liberal ruling coalition led by the current prime minister, Donald Tusk, took power in December 2023, it launched a number of investigations into the actions of senior PiS officials. That led, last year, to prosecutors announcing that they want to charge Ziobro with 26 crimes, including leading a criminal group and approving the unlawful purchase of Pegasus spyware, which was used to surveil some of PiS’s political opponents. However, although parliament approved the lifting of Ziobro’s immunity from prosecution, he had by then already travelled to Hungary, which was at the time ruled by conservative PiS ally Viktor Orbán. In December 2025, the Hungarian government granted Ziobro political asylum. At this year’s Hungarian parliamentary elections in April, Orbán’s Fidesz party was removed from power and his successor, Péter Magyar, pledged to extradite Ziobro to Poland. But, just as Magyar was being sworn in in May, Ziobro left Hungary and flew to the United States, reportedly with the help of a senior US State Department official. World.title: Prague to Mark 37 Years Since Velvet Revolution With 160 Events
World.content:
Prague will mark the 37th anniversary of the Velvet Revolution on November 17 with more than 160 events taking place along Národní Street as part of this year’s Korzo Národní celebrations.

Organised by the association Díky, že můžem, the annual event will bring together concerts, theatre performances, public discussions, exhibitions and activities exploring democracy and freedom.



This year’s programme carries the motto “Let’s Not Stand on the Sidelines. Democracy Relies on Each of Us.” The organisers say the message reflects growing concerns about declining trust in society and the challenges facing democratic institutions.

One of the central moments of the celebrations will take place at 17:11, when the traditional song Modlitba pro Martu (A Prayer for Marta) will be performed from the balcony of the Metro Palace.

This year, the performance will form the finale of a theatrical production titled DŮM VŠECH (House for All), which begins at 17:00. Visitors unable to gather directly beneath the balcony will be able to watch the performance on large screens along Národní Street or through a live broadcast.

The day’s programme will begin earlier, with the popular Velvet Brunch, a charity event held directly on the street between 10:00 and 13:00. At 13:00, members of the Czech Radio Children’s Choir will perform the national anthem.

Other events include live podcasts, musical performances and discussions on social issues. Among the scheduled speakers and performers are Markéta Foukalová, Martin Brunner, Václav Kopta and Vietnamese community representative Quang Luong.

Havel, the Vietnamese community and Věra Čáslavská

Several parts of this year’s celebrations will focus on important anniversaries.

The programme will commemorate the 90th anniversary of the birth of Václav Havel, the playwright and former Czech president.

His legacy will be explored through the traditional Václav Havel’s Living Room, titled “For Vašek”, at Platýz Palace. Actors including Vojtěch Vondráček and Taťjana Medvecká will read texts dedicated to Havel.

Another anniversary concerns the Vietnamese community, which marks 70 years in the Czech Republic. The programme will include Lost in Translation, a discussion bringing together three generations of Vietnamese residents to examine questions of identity, belonging and life between cultures.

The celebrations will also remember gymnast Věra Čáslavská, ten years after her death. Her life and the relationship between sport and politics will be examined through a special lecture aboard the Educational Tram and a live recording of the Outsider podcast.

World.title: FlixBus Launches Direct Route Between Prague Florenc and Airport
World.content:
FlixBus will introduce a direct bus connection between Prague’s Florenc Central Bus Station and Václav Havel Airport on November 12.

The new service will operate 13 times a day in each direction, with the journey taking approximately 30 minutes.

The first bus will leave Florenc at 3:40 a.m., while the last departure is scheduled for 10:40 p.m. From the airport, services will run between 4:15 a.m. and 11:15 p.m.



Ticket prices will depend on demand and departure times. According to the FlixBus website, the usual fare is around CZK 128, including the booking fee. The cheapest tickets start at CZK 108, while some departures cost up to CZK 278.

The company expects the route to attract business travellers in particular. Passengers will have access to Wi-Fi and power outlets on board.

BusAir joins the competition

FlixBus is not the only company expanding its airport connections. A separate private service, operating under the name BusAir, began running between Prague’s city centre and the airport in late October.

Operated by UBUS, the service offers eight departures a day in each direction, with buses running every two hours. A ticket costs CZK 125 and remains valid for 24 hours.

Due to renovation work on the ceiling at Prague Main Railway Station and traffic restrictions on the city’s main arterial road, BusAir currently departs from Opletalova Street, close to the station. On the way to the airport, it also stops at Hradčanská metro station on Line A.

Both new services are entering a market where the main competitor is the Airport Express, operated by Prague Public Transit Company (DPP).

The Airport Express runs more frequently than the private alternatives, with departures every 20 to 30 minutes during the day and hourly services overnight. It is also currently the only direct bus connection between the city centre and airport operating throughout the night.

Standard Prague public transport tickets are not valid on the service. A single adult ticket costs CZK 200, although passengers can get a lower fare when purchasing it together with a train ticket.

World.title: Říčany Named Czech Republic’s Best Place to Live for Ninth Year
World.content:
Říčany has been named the best municipality in the Czech Republic for quality of life for the ninth consecutive year, retaining its position at the top of a nationwide ranking ahead of Prague.

The Central Bohemian town, located southeast of the capital, again led the Quality of Life Index compiled by the Obce v datech project. The ranking assesses 206 Czech municipalities with extended administrative powers.

At the other end of the table, Orlová in the Karviná District ranked last, while nearby Karviná finished second from bottom.



The geographical divide remains clear: the 14 highest-ranked municipalities are all located within 50 kilometres of Prague or Brno, while many of those at the bottom are found in former industrial and border regions, particularly in the Moravian-Silesian and Ústí nad Labem regions.

There have nevertheless been signs of improvement in parts of the Moravian-Silesian Region. Over the past eight years, Odry, Kopřivnice and Hlučín have each climbed by around 40 places in the ranking.

The picture is less positive in the Ústí nad Labem Region, where only six of the region’s 16 assessed municipalities have improved their position since 2018. Roudnice nad Labem was the only municipality in the region to record a substantial rise.

Pohořelice Makes the Biggest Leap

Pohořelice, in the Brno-Country District, has recorded one of the most striking improvements since the index was introduced in 2018. The town has climbed from 117th place to fifth this year.

Nepomuk, in the Plzeň Region, has made an equally large jump of 112 places and now ranks 24th. Kuřim has moved up 65 positions to 15th, while Mnichovo Hradiště has risen 46 places to 18th.

According to Jan Havránek of AQE Advisors, which developed the project, municipalities do not need to perform at the top in every category to improve their overall ranking.

For around half of the 30 municipalities that have improved the most, the stronger results were linked to a younger population, population growth and, in many cases, longer life expectancy.

The Quality of Life Index evaluates municipalities across several broad areas, including health and the environment, material security and education, and relationships and public services.

World.title: ROCK THE OPERA Returns to Prague for 25th Anniversary Concert
World.content:
Twenty-five years after conductor Friedemann Riehle helped pioneer the symphonic rock concert format in Prague, he is returning to the Czech capital for a special anniversary performance.

ROCK THE OPERA will take place on Sunday, 13 December 2026, at Smetana Hall in Prague’s Municipal House.

The concert will bring together the Prague Philharmonic Orchestra, rock musicians and vocalists for an evening dedicated to some of the biggest songs in rock history.



The anniversary also marks a full-circle moment for Riehle. On 29 October 2001, he promoted and conducted one of the first symphonic rock shows in Prague, combining a symphony orchestra with rock drummers and vocalists to give legendary songs a new sound.

What began as an experiment has developed into a long-running international project. Over the past 25 years, Riehle has conducted more than 100 symphonic rock concerts across Europe, performing everywhere from Iceland to Istanbul and appearing at venues including the Vienna State Opera, Berlin Philharmonie and Athens’ Odeon of Herodes Atticus.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by RONNIE GRACE | ROCK SINGER ⚡️ (@ronniegrace)

For the Prague anniversary concert, Riehle will be joined by Ronnie Romero, one of the best-known voices in contemporary rock. Romero has performed with several internationally recognised rock musicians and bands and will bring his distinctive vocals to the symphonic arrangements.

The programme will feature music associated with some of rock’s biggest names, including Pink Floyd, Queen, AC/DC, Led Zeppelin and U2.

Alongside Romero, the concert will feature vocalists Lucie Koutniková and Sabina Olijve, guitarist Jiří Rambousek and drummer František Hönig. The Prague Philharmonic Orchestra will perform under the direction of Friedemann Riehle.

Tickets are available via Ticketportal.

World.title: St. Martin’s Day 2026 in Prague: Where to Enjoy Traditional Goose
World.content:
St. Martin’s Day, which Czechs celebrate on November 11, is a holiday of good food and drink. Autumn slowly alternates with winter, and it begins to snow.

In the past, the economic year was ending at this time, and the landowners were preparing a feast for their people as a form of thanks, when they were also paid out their wages.

St. Martin’s Day in restaurants

You can be sure that almost every restaurant around mid-November will be offering its visitors a special St. Martin’s Day menu. What does it feature?

According to a tradition that has lasted for several centuries, geese were always roasted in the autumn, fresh cabbage was processed, and wine or beer was drunk. And today’s restaurants and pubs remain faithful to these basic ingredients.

Typically, you will be served liver pâté as an appetizer, followed by a strong broth with liver dumplings and noodles, which the chefs usually leave to simmer overnight, with the main course being roast goose with red or white cabbage and dumplings.

Where to taste St. Martin’s menu?

Restaurant Salabka (November 6 – 14): Choose from 3 to 5 courses featuring seasonal autumn ingredients and contemporary gastronomy. Available from November 6, alongside the regular autumn tasting menu.

More info here.

Pilsner Urquell Experience: until November 15, here you can find a St. Martin’s Menu for 1,095 Kč including goose liver pâté with cranberries, roast goose leg with red cabbage and Carlsbad dumplings, followed by traditional Czech potato cones with poppy seeds.

More info here.

GARE Restaurants: Celebrate St. Martin’s Day at three GARE Restaurants: La Gare, Les Moules and Pivovar U Supa, each offering its own take on the Czech goose-feast tradition. Highlights include goose pâté, traditional goose kaldoun and confit goose leg with poppy-seed potato dumplings, plums and fermented cabbage.

La Gare serves its festive menu during lunch from November 9–13. Les Moules offers its specialties from November 7 while stocks last, while Pivovar U Supa continues its goose feast until November 15.

La Gare | Les Moules | Pivovar U Supa

Alternatively, guests can enjoy homemade potato lokše filled with pulled goose meat, onion cabbage and apples (359 CZK). To finish on a sweet note, the menu offers apple strudel with vanilla sauce, walnuts, honey and cinnamon crumble (149 CZK).

Available for lunch and dinner until November 15, the menu costs 1,480 CZK per person, with individual dishes also available. Guests can enjoy their meal with views of the Vltava River and Prague Castle.

World.title: All Aboard the Pajama Express: Prague Metro Supports Hospitalised Kids
World.content:
The Prague Metro will host a special pajama-themed journey on Friday, November 13, as part of the Czech Republic’s annual Pajama Day, an initiative supporting families of children undergoing long-term hospital treatment.

For the first time, a dedicated carriage will be reserved for passengers travelling in their pajamas. The special train, known as the Pajama Express, will operate on Metro Line A, with participants invited to board its first carriage at any station along the route.



The journey will begin at Depo Hostivař at 9:13 a.m. and end at Nemocnice Motol, the metro station serving Motol University Hospital. Hospital representatives will welcome participants upon arrival.

The initiative aims to highlight the difficulties faced by children who spend extended periods in hospital, often separated from their usual surroundings, and the importance of having family members close by during treatment.

Several public figures and bloggers are expected to join the journey. Among them will be actress Veronika Arichteva, patron of the project.

Now in its third year, Pajama Day has attracted around 400 registered participants. Schools, businesses, public institutions, theatres, hospitals and individuals across the country have signed up for this year’s edition.

The event is organised by the Ronald McDonald House in the Czech Republic (Dům Ronalda McDonalda Česko), which provides free accommodation for families of seriously ill children at Motol Hospital.

The facility allows parents to stay close to their children throughout lengthy hospital stays, reducing the burden of travelling between the hospital and home.

Passengers wishing to take part in the Prague event do not need to register separately. They simply need to wear their pajamas and board the first carriage of the special train at any station along Line A.

World.title: Three Days of Chocolate and Sweet Treats Await in Prague
World.content:
Chocolate lovers in Prague will have a sweet reason to head to Novo Plaza this weekend as ČokoFest arrives at the shopping centre for the first time.

The three-day chocolate festival will take place from Friday, November 13, to Sunday, November 15, offering visitors free entry and a programme filled with tastings, handmade sweets and activities for children.



Visitors can expect a selection of handmade chocolates, pralines, cakes and other sweet specialties, with plenty of opportunities to sample different products throughout the weekend.

Families with children will also find a range of activities, including chocolate workshops designed for young visitors. Meanwhile, Thermomix will host live demonstrations and chocolate tastings during the event.

ČokoFest will also offer the chance to win several prizes. One of the main giveaways is a weekend drive in a Chery Tiggo 7, provided by Mach Motors. Visitors can also enter to win a ČokoBox and other sweet prizes.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by ČokoFest / Čokoládový Festival (@cokofestcz)

With Christmas just around the corner, the festival could also be a good place to find original gifts for chocolate lovers.

ČokoFest takes place at Novo Plaza Shopping Centre in Prague 4, and admission is free throughout all three days.

World.title: Micro Praha Festival Returns With 93 Watch Brands From 27 Countries
World.content:
The fourth edition of the international watch festival will take place at Fantova budova on November 28–29. Admission is free with online registration.

The Micro Praha Festival will return to Prague on November 28–29, bringing together 93 independent watch brands from 27 countries.



The fourth edition of the event will take place at Fantův sál inside the historic Fantova budova, near Prague’s Main Railway Station. Visitors will be able to discover new collections, try on watches and meet the people behind the brands.

Organisers say this year’s edition will be the largest so far, with microbrands and established independent watchmakers exhibiting alongside each other for the first time.

Brands from countries including Switzerland, Germany, the United States, Canada, France, the Netherlands, Japan, Taiwan and the Czech Republic will take part. Several exhibitors will be appearing in Prague and Central Europe for the first time.

Among the newcomers are New York-based Brew, known for watches inspired by coffee culture; MING, which focuses on experimental designs and engineering; Atelier Wen, specialising in watches with hand-crafted guilloché dials; and Lorier, a brand recognised for its vintage-inspired designs.

Chrono24 Joins as Main Festival Sponsor

The 2026 edition will also see Chrono24, the international online marketplace for luxury watches, join the festival as its primary sponsor and partner.

Representatives from the company will be present throughout the weekend to discuss the watch market, industry trends and the platform’s latest features. KB Bank is also listed among this year’s primary sponsors.

The festival was founded in 2023 by Bhanu Chopra and Ondrej Vislocký, two watch enthusiasts who wanted to create a platform for smaller independent brands in Central Europe.

Chopra is a watch journalist who previously served as editor-in-chief of Revolution USA, while Vislocký is a Prague-based photographer whose work has appeared in international watch publications and brand catalogues.

The two also co-own INFINTY Watches, a specialist retailer of microbrand and independent watches in central Prague.

World.title: One of the most beautiful waterfalls in Hungary ranks among the world’s top 20 – photos
World.content:
One of Miskolc’s best-known attractions, the Szinva Waterfall in Lillafüred, has received further international recognition, featuring as the world’s 17th most beautiful waterfall in Worldworthy’s 2026 ranking. This recognition further strengthens the international reputation of Miskolc-Lillafüred as a tourist destination. Alongside the natural treasures of the Bükk Mountains, the city’s historic city centre, the spas of Miskolctapolca, the Avas Wine District and the ever-expanding range of culinary delights all contribute to making Miskolc a rewarding destination for a stay of several days.

The Szinva Waterfall in Lillafüred has been included in this year’s edition of The Worldworthy 100, which showcases the world’s best-rated waterfalls. According to the organisation, the ranking is compiled using independent criteria such as online reviews, press coverage and travelogues; it is not possible to apply for inclusion on the list or to pay to be included.

The Iguaçu Falls in Brazil topped Worldworthy’s 2026 ranking, with Mexico’s Cascada El Chiflón taking second place and the world-famous Victoria Falls in Zimbabwe coming third. The Szinva Falls in Lillafüred came 17th in this prestigious international ranking, representing Hungary as the only Hungarian site on the TOP 100 list, which features 42 countries.

The Miskolc attraction even outperformed such world-famous waterfalls as the Kuang Si Falls in Laos (18th place), the Rhine Falls in Switzerland (38th place), Yosemite Falls in the United States (40th place) and Seljalandsfoss in Iceland (50th place).

The unique spectacle of the Lillafüred waterfall is complemented by the forest setting of the Bükk Mountains. Hungary’s highest waterfall is situated next to the hanging gardens of the Palotaszálló, just a few steps from Lake Hámori. Thanks to the area’s romantic atmosphere, the historic hotel, the forest narrow-gauge railway and the walking trails, as well as the caves with their spectacular chambers, Lillafüred offers enough to keep visitors occupied for several days in its own right.

Visitors can also combine their nature walks with a visit to the thermal baths in Miskolctapolca, another popular holiday resort in the Miskolc area. The Cave Baths, built within natural cave passages, and the Ellipsum Adventure Baths offer a variety of bathing experiences all year round, making the town an attractive destination not only for excursions and active pursuits but also for those seeking relaxation; it can be an appealing destination for school holidays or even a week-long summer break.

If you missed it – Dining Guide Top100: Hungary’s best pizzeria has been named – and it’s not in Budapest

Miskolc took centre stage on the international stage in 2026

In 2026, Miskolc’s Edible Forest – Forest Gastro Express programme won the award for the world’s best sustainable tourism initiative at the Green Destinations international competition. This unique experience combines the natural treasures of the Bükk Mountains with local gastronomy. Under expert guidance, participants can learn about the forest’s edible plants and then sample dishes made from local ingredients. The programme was also included in the 2026 Green List, an international selection by the British travel magazine Wanderlust.

In Time Out magazine’s 2026 international selection, Lillafüred was ranked as the 19th most beautiful place in the world. The Palotaszálló, Lake Hámori, the waterfall and the Bükk forest complex form a natural and built environment that stands out even by international standards.

Similarly, according to Time Out’s 2026 guide, Miskolc is Europe’s 4th best value-for-money destination worth discovering. This ranking draws attention to the town’s affordable yet rich range of tourist attractions. Visitors can enjoy a wide variety of activities and experiences, whilst the city is becoming an attractive alternative for an increasing number of international travellers.

The success of the Miskolc Advent Tram has also extended far beyond the country’s borders. This special festive tram was voted Europe’s most beautiful Advent tram for the ninth time running in 2026 in an international public poll. The tram is one of Miskolc’s best-known attractions during the Advent season, drawing many visitors to the city every year.

Miskolc has become one of the key regional centres for gastronomic tourism in Hungary, and its range of restaurants has elevated it to the status of one of the country’s most significant gastronomic destinations. Many of the city’s restaurants feature in the recommendations of the international Michelin Guide and the Hungarian Street Kitchen guide, meaning that Miskolc now offers travellers a remarkable gastronomic experience on a par with the capital and Lake Balaton.

The character of the local dining scene is defined by creative chefs, seasonal and locally sourced ingredients, and dishes drawing on the flavours of the Bükk Mountains. The unique atmosphere of the Avasi Wine Quarter adds further experiences to the city’s gastronomic offering.

The Szinva Waterfall’s inclusion on the world list presents a further opportunity to further strengthen Miskolc’s position on the international tourism map. International recognition is showcasing Miskolc’s attractions to an ever-wider audience.

World.title: Fidesz: Magyar’s talks in Berlin ‘failure for Hungary’
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s talks in Berlin were a failure for Hungary, the spokesperson for the former prime minister’s office said on Wednesday.

Bertalan Havasi said in a statement that Germany had made it clear at the talks that Hungary must purchase LNG from Germany instead of Russian gas, at a price that is not yet known.

Given the energy policies of Western European countries, this does not bode well for Hungarian households and businesses, as energy prices there are significantly higher, he said, adding that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz also made it clear that Hungary cannot be exempted from providing financial support to Ukraine.

Havasi said that whereas the Czech and Slovak prime ministers had rejected the German chancellor’s “blackmail”, Magyar had avoided giving a direct answer.

The Tisza government should follow the position of its predecessor because that served Hungary’s interests, and the Hungarian government must recover the one billion euros in EU fines imposed on it for protecting its borders, Havasi added.

The Tisza government should not settle for anything less than the European Union reimbursing Hungary the full amount spent on protecting the EU’s external borders—more than 2.5 billion euros, he said. Hungary must also recover more than 2 billion euros in cohesion funds, he added.

World.title: EU customs duty triggers shift in online orders from Asian webshops
World.content:
One-third of Hungarian consumers have scaled back the frequency of their purchases from Asian webshops since the introduction of a European Union customs duty on low-value parcels on July 1, a survey commissioned by delivery company DODO shows.

The representative survey, conducted by Ipsos, shows 29pc of Hungarian consumers have stopped using Asian webshops since the rollout of the EUR 3 customs duty levied on each product category for items valued up to EUR 150 from sources outside of the EU.

Around 5pc of survey respondents still buy as frequently from Asian webshops, but take care to limit their product categories per package.

About 29pc now buy products from Hungarian webshops that they earlier ordered from Asia, while a further 21pc now choose webshops based in other EU member states.

From November 1, the EU has slapped an additional EUR 2 handling fee per item on non-EU packages on top of the EUR 3 customs duty.

If you missed it: Shein and Temu shoppers hit by new EU fee as cheap orders now cost more

How do the new EU customs charges affect Asian webshops?

The new rules apply to low-value goods shipped directly to EU consumers from countries outside the bloc, including purchases from popular Asian online marketplaces such as Temu and Shein. Crucially, the EUR 3 customs duty is calculated according to product categories rather than the total number of products in a parcel.

For example, a package containing several identical T-shirts attracts a EUR 3 duty, while an order containing T-shirts, shoes and electronic accessories could incur EUR 9 in customs charges if the goods fall under three different tariff classifications. The additional EUR 2 handling fee, introduced on 1 November, further increases the costs associated with importing low-value goods.

Why is the EU tightening rules on low-cost imports?

The European Union introduced the measures to address the rapid growth of low-value e-commerce imports and create fairer competition between European retailers and sellers based outside the bloc.

According to the European Commission, the previous customs exemption gave non-EU businesses a competitive advantage and made it more difficult to tackle undervalued shipments and products that fail to meet EU safety standards.

The changes are part of a broader reform of the EU customs system, aimed at improving oversight of cross-border online shopping. For Hungarian consumers, the DODO survey suggests that the new charges are already influencing purchasing decisions, with domestic and EU-based webshops gaining attention as alternatives to Asian platforms.

World.title: Budapest housing prices stall as Hungary’s property market loses momentum
World.content:
Hungary property prices are rising at their slowest annual pace in more than two years, while Budapest’s residential market has remained virtually unchanged for three months. New figures also reveal substantial price differences between the capital’s districts, following a brief surge in buyer interest at the end of October.

Hungary’s residential property market appears to be entering a quieter period after years of rising prices. According to the latest figures published by property listings platform ingatlan.com on Wednesday, 11 November, annual house price growth slowed to 6.9% in October, down from 8.2% in September.

The slowdown was particularly pronounced in Budapest, where prices increased by just 1.8% compared with October 2025 – the weakest annual growth recorded in the capital since December 2023.

On a monthly basis, Hungary property prices rose by only 0.2%, while Budapest recorded virtually no change.

The latest figures suggest that the previous wave of rapid price increases has lost momentum, although a nationwide decline in property values has yet to emerge.

Budapest property prices have barely moved for three months

The stagnation in Budapest is especially noteworthy because the Hungarian capital remains by far one of the country’s most expensive housing markets.

According to the latest ingatlan.com figures reported by MTI, the median asking price for existing residential properties in Budapest stood at HUF 1.4 million (€3,862) per square metre in early November.

That was practically identical to the figure recorded a year earlier.

For buyers considering a typical 60-square-metre property, this translates into an indicative asking price of HUF 84 million (approximately €232,000).

However, the capital’s overall median conceals significant differences between neighbourhoods.

The price gap between Budapest’s districts remains enormous

Budapest’s central 5th district remains the most expensive area for existing properties, with median asking prices approaching HUF 2 million (€5,517) per square metre.

At the other end of the market, the 20th and 21st districts have median asking prices of approximately HUF 1.03 million (€2,841) per square metre.

This means that, based on district-level median prices, a 60-square-metre property would have an indicative asking price of almost HUF 120 million (€331,000) in the 5th district, compared with approximately HUF 61.8 million (€170,000) in the more affordable outer districts.

The difference approaches HUF 58 million (€160,000), illustrating why location remains one of the most important factors influencing property affordability in Budapest.

Newly built properties command an additional premium.

The median asking price for new homes in the capital reached HUF 1.72 million (€4,744) per square metre in early November, representing an annual increase of 4.5%.

The 2nd district recorded the highest median new-build price, at HUF 3.1 million (€8,551) per square metre.

These figures also demonstrate that the slowdown is not uniform across property categories. While the broader capital market has stagnated, newly built homes continue to show higher annual asking prices.

A final rush before Hungary’s mortgage programme changed

Another important development occurred at the end of October, when Hungary’s government-backed Otthon Start mortgage programme was being phased out and replaced by Wekerle Plusz.

If you missed it: What is Wekerle Plusz? Here’s the new housing programme the government offers instead of Orbán’s Home Start

According to ingatlan.com’s October demand analysis, the final days of the previous scheme triggered a temporary surge in buyer interest.

Between 26 and 30 October, telephone enquiries about properties advertised on the platform were 38% higher than on an average September day.

The increase was even more pronounced for Budapest properties meeting the former programme’s eligibility criteria, where enquiries were estimated to be 55% above the level expected without the policy change.

However, the surge proved short-lived. By 31 October, buyer interest had already fallen below the level normally recorded on a Saturday.

Across October as a whole, approximately 250,000 telephone enquiries were registered for properties for sale. Despite the temporary increase compared with September, average daily demand remained 15% below its level a year earlier.

The figures indicate that the late-October rush was closely linked to the mortgage deadline rather than necessarily signalling a broader recovery in demand.

What does the slowdown mean for buyers in Hungary?

The latest figures offer a mixed picture for prospective homebuyers.

On one hand, Budapest prices are no longer increasing at the pace seen during earlier periods of rapid growth. The capital’s three-month stagnation may also reduce some of the pressure on buyers to make immediate decisions.

On the other hand, relatively stable prices do not automatically mean affordable housing.

Even in Budapest’s less expensive districts, the purchase of a typical flat requires substantial savings or mortgage financing.

The government’s new Wekerle Plusz programme introduces different borrowing conditions for newly built and existing homes, potentially influencing which properties attract buyers.

Whether this leads to sustained changes in housing demand and prices remains uncertain.

For now, the evidence points towards a market that is cooling rather than collapsing.

Is Hungary’s housing market entering a new phase?

The latest property figures raise a broader question about the future of Hungary’s residential market.

Want to explore Hungary’s property market beyond Budapest?

The extended analysis on Substack compares housing costs in Hungary’s largest cities, examines the growing supply of properties for sale and explores how the new mortgage scheme could affect buyers.

Read our full Hungary property market analysis on Substack.

The slowdown in Budapest is occurring alongside significant differences in housing costs across the country, changes in mortgage support and shifting patterns of buyer demand.

These developments could become increasingly important for Hungarian households, foreign residents considering a property purchase and investors assessing the market.

While prices remain high, October’s figures suggest that the period of rapid and widespread increases may be giving way to more stable market conditions.

The coming months will show whether Budapest’s stagnation becomes a lasting trend – and whether the rest of Hungary’s housing market follows the same path.

World.title: Indonesia’s super priority tourism destinantions spotlighted in Budapest to boost Hungarian travel ties
World.content:
The Europe Committee of the Association of the Indonesian Tours and Travel Agencies (ASITA), supported by the Embassy of the Republic of Indonesia in Budapest, successfully hosted an official Tourism Promotion and Business Networking Event at the Kimpton BEM Budapest on 9 November 2026.

For the event, a specialized 6-member Indonesian tourism delegation—led by Mr. Rocky W Praputranto—traveled to Hungary to connect directly with Hungarian tour operators, travel agencies (represented in part by Ms. Zsuzsa Tukacs from MUISZ Hungary), tourism industry professionals, and travel influencers.

The event officially opened with key remarks from H.E. Ms. Penny Dewi Herasati, Ambassador of the Republic of Indonesia to Hungary, highlighting tourism as a crucial vehicle for cultural connection between the two nations.

“Tourism is the ultimate catalyst for people-to-people connection,” stated Ambassador Herasati during her opening address. “When a Hungarian traveller visits Indonesia, they do not just see a beautiful landscape—they connect with our local communities, experience our rich cultural heritage, and share in our universal values of hospitality. These personal, human connections are the bedrock of the deep, long-standing relationship between Hungary and Indonesia.”

Ambassador Herasati also emphasized Indonesia’s strategic shift beyond traditional travel hubs, championing the country’s Super Priority Tourism Destinations:

Lake Toba (North Sumatra): The world’s largest volcanic lake, offering breathtaking highland landscapes, a cool climate, and the rich cultural heritage of the Batak people;

Likupang (North Sulawesi): An emerging premier marine paradise dedicated to sustainable ecotourism, pristine white-sand beaches, and luxury coastal resorts;

Borobudur (Central Java): The world’s largest Buddhist temple and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, serving as the crown jewel of Indonesia’s spiritual and cultural tourism;

Mandalika (West Nusa Tenggara): A world-class integrated resort zone on Lombok Island, established as a premier global sports tourism hub hosting the MotoGP world championship; and

Labuan Bajo (East Nusa Tenggara): The exclusive gateway to the UNESCO-listed Komodo National Park, world-renowned for luxury Phinisi cruise adventures and rich marine biodiversity.

Following the Ambassador’s address, the ASITA delegation delivered a comprehensive presentation detailing these destinations and their latest travel packages, highlighting experiences ranging from ancient heritage and unique wildlife to luxury wellness and marine ecotourism.

The core of the event featured intensive one-on-one B2B matchmaking sessions, allowing Hungarian travel buyers to negotiate directly with Indonesian suppliers and destination management representatives. The Budapest event serves as the first leg of a three-nation European tourism promotion for the ASITA delegation, concluding today with a networking lunch to formalize new commercial partnerships.

Beyond fostering travel ties, the Embassy views this initiative as a stepping stone toward a more comprehensive cultural exchange. The Embassy plans to amplify this collaboration by integrating future tourism campaigns with gastro-diplomacy and cultural showcases across Hungary. To ensure continuous engagement, the Embassy will also serve as a dedicated information hub to assist Hungarian travel influencers, journalists, and content creators looking to feature Indonesia’s Super Priority Destinations in the local media.

If you missed it: What Indonesia and Hungary can learn from their young people

World.title: PM Magyar: V4 to cooperate in EU budget talks
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar emphasised the Visegrad Group’s cooperation in connection with the talks on the European Union’s next seven-year budget, in a telephone interview with commercial news channel ATV on Tuesday evening after his visit to Berlin.

Magyar said Hungary, Czechia, Poland and Slovakia were presenting a united front on the EU budget, as were several other countries with an interest in upholding the importance of the Common Agricultural Policy.

Hungary, he said, was coordinating almost every position with the other V4 countries, adding that apart from a few exceptions, they shared similar views on nearly every issue.

Magyar said that just a few months after the strengthening and revival of Visegrad cooperation, it was already clear that this gave them substantive bargaining power in Brussels as well, since it involved more than 60 million people, and companies of defining weight. He said it was far easier to negotiate, whether with the president of the European Council or with other member states, in this manner than separately.

If you missed it: Hungary expands energy cooperation with Poland and Czechia in new regional agreement

The prime minister also touched on the Dublin summit to be held in the second half of the week, noting that the leaders of every European country will be present there. An informal EU summit follows on Friday, also in Dublin under the Irish presidency, where the EU budget and artificial intelligence will both be on the agenda, and many one-on-one meetings will be held with leaders of various countries, he added.

Magyar also touched on the political changes in Serbia. “We are proud that Hungary plays a stabilising role in the Western Balkans. I have already held talks with the leaders of all the countries concerned, and as soon as the new Serbian government is in place, I am ready to negotiate with its leader as well, either in Belgrade or in Budapest. Closer cooperation with the Western Balkan countries is as much in the EU’s interest as it is in theirs. We know from history how important it is that there be peace and prosperity in the Balkans too, and if the EU does not go there, other forces will, and those will certainly not be European,” he said.

As regards Hungary’s energy supply, the prime minister said the energy mix must be constructed so it is as cheap and as secure as possible. Hungary has interconnectors and cross-border capacities and can source gas from many directions, he added.

He stressed that the size of the transit fee is the most decisive element in choosing resources. “What comes from Russia is very cheap, but everywhere there is the exchange price, and Russian gas is also priced off the gas exchange, or the fee payable for the gas delivered to Hungary follows from that,” he said.

He also said he would negotiate with the Romanian prime minister about the Black Sea gas field, on which an agreement is already at hand.

“In Dublin, at the EU summit, we will also hold discussions with other international players. Transit fees are crucial factors everywhere, along with the volumes and the security of the supplies. It is in our interest that gas can come reliably from as many directions as possible. If that is the case, we can coordinate, and indeed bargain, over the transit fees,”

Magyar said. He noted that Hungary can purchase liquefied natural gas through northern as well as southern routes, and American, Norwegian and Azerbaijani gas can come via Turkiye, Romania and Russia.

World.title: Áron Orbán, brother of former Hungarian PM Viktor Orbán, faces arrest in people-smuggling investigation
World.content:
Hungarian prosecutors have requested the pre-trial detention of Áron Orbán, the younger brother of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, following a series of police raids linked to an alleged people-smuggling operation. Four suspects are accused of helping more than 100 Vietnamese nationals enter Hungary and travel onwards to Western Europe.

Hungarian authorities have stepped up their investigation into Áron Orbán and his business associates, with prosecutors formally requesting the pre-trial detention of all four suspects on Tuesday, 10 November.

According to 24.hu, the Budapest Chief Prosecutor’s Office has asked a court to order their detention, citing concerns that the suspects could obstruct the investigation or interfere with evidence if released.

The development follows coordinated police operations on Monday in Budapest, Fót and Dunakeszi, two towns in Pest County near the Hungarian capital.

The case, which was also reported by Turkish news agency Anadolu, involves allegations of organised people smuggling and influence peddling connected to the former prime minister’s younger brother.

Áron Orbán and three others suspected of people smuggling

Hungary’s National Bureau of Investigation (NNI) has questioned four suspects, including Áron Orbán, over allegations of facilitating illegal migration for financial gain as part of a criminal conspiracy.

According to investigators, the group allegedly helped Vietnamese nationals obtain Hungarian visas during several months in 2024.

The individuals officially applied to enter Hungary to participate in short training programmes. However, investigators suspect that many never attended the courses, while others remained beyond the validity of their visas.

Authorities believe their actual destination was Western Europe, where they hoped to find better employment opportunities and living conditions.

The suspects allegedly arranged visa-related procedures through Hungarian diplomatic missions in Vietnam and charged recruitment fees for their services.

Investigators estimate that more than 100 Vietnamese nationals may have been assisted through the alleged scheme.

The four suspects have been questioned and taken into custody. Prosecutors have requested their pre-trial detention, but the final decision rests with a court.

IF you missed it: Áron Orbán arrested in case involving more than 100 Vietnamese nationals smuggled through Hungary – VIDEOS

Counter-terrorism officers involved in police raids

The investigation led to coordinated searches at four locations on Monday, 9 November.

Officers from the NNI and the National Office for Asset Recovery and Protection (NVVH) searched properties in Budapest, Fót and Dunakeszi.

Hungary’s Counter Terrorism Centre (TEK) also participated in the operations. According to police, specialist officers were deployed at two locations because investigators anticipated the possible presence of firearms.

Documents, electronic records and other potential evidence were seized during searches lasting several hours.

Anadolu reported that counter-terrorism officers had searched a property in Fótliget linked to a company associated with Áron Orbán.

Anna Unger, head of the NVVH, initially declined to confirm or deny the details of the operation but acknowledged that her office had carried out further investigative measures in a case involving Orbán.

Alongside the people-smuggling allegations, investigators are examining possible influence peddling.

One suspect is accused of seeking an unlawful benefit from the head of a labour recruitment company by referring to political connections.

Investigation began after leaked recording in 2025

The allegations surrounding Áron Orbán first attracted significant attention in May 2025, when Hungarian investigative news outlet Telex published details about his business associates and their visa-related activities.

The reporting followed the emergence of an audio recording in which Orbán reportedly discussed visa applications with Dávid Héjj, an official associated with the Prime Minister’s Cabinet Office during Viktor Orbán’s administration.

The conversation reportedly suggested that some visa applications connected to the business network had been blocked by the authorities.

The investigation subsequently expanded into allegations involving the organisation of travel for Vietnamese nationals and possible misuse of political influence.

What happens next in the Áron Orbán case?

According to 24.hu, prosecutors consider pre-trial detention necessary to ensure that the four suspects remain available during criminal proceedings and do not interfere with the collection of evidence.

A court is expected to consider the detention requests on Wednesday, 11 November.

Áron Orbán’s lawyer has disputed the justification for taking his client into custody.

The case has attracted national attention because of the suspect’s family connection to Viktor Orbán, who led Hungary for 16 consecutive years before losing power following the April 2026 parliamentary election.

However, the allegations remain under investigation, and no criminal conviction has been established.

The next significant development will be the court’s decision on pre-trial detention, as investigators continue examining the alleged visa scheme, the movement of Vietnamese nationals and the possible involvement of political connections.

World.title: Péter Magyar and Friedrich Merz seek closer ties but clash over Ukraine funding – VIDEO
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz agreed to strengthen Hungarian–German relations during talks in Berlin on Tuesday, 10 November. However, the two leaders expressed differing views on linking the European Union’s next seven-year budget to financial support for Ukraine. While Merz insisted that continued assistance to Kyiv was essential for European security, Magyar warned against making the EU budget dependent on a separate political issue.

Péter Magyar and Friedrich Merz agree to strengthen Hungarian–German relations

Speaking at a joint press conference in Berlin, Péter Magyar said the foundations were in place for closer political and economic cooperation between Hungary and Germany.

According to Hungary’s state news agency MTI, Magyar highlighted the strong relationship between the two countries, noting that bilateral trade exceeds €65 billion and that German companies have made substantial investments in Hungary.

The Hungarian prime minister said both governments saw further opportunities for cooperation, ranging from major industrial projects to smaller investments.

Magyar also welcomed the revival of regular high-level bilateral meetings, pointing out that the two countries’ leaders had previously gone years without holding such talks.

He announced that Friedrich Merz was expected to visit Budapest in spring 2027. The two governments also plan to organise a joint Hungarian–German cultural season in 2028.

Merz insists EU budget must secure Ukraine funding

Despite the positive atmosphere surrounding bilateral relations, significant differences emerged over the European Union’s proposed 2028–2034 budget.

According to Anadolu Agency, Merz stressed that the next long-term EU budget must guarantee continued financial assistance for Ukraine.

The German chancellor argued that supporting Kyiv was a matter of collective European security and therefore a responsibility shared by all member states.

He also called for substantial revisions to the current budget proposals, warning that negotiations could not be concluded quickly without significant changes.

The disagreement comes amid growing concerns over Ukraine’s financial needs. Kyiv faces an estimated €70 billion funding shortfall in 2027, while the European Commission is examining options for providing approximately €45 billion in additional European assistance.

Germany has reportedly made its support for the next EU budget conditional on all member states agreeing to contribute fairly towards Ukraine’s financing needs.

If you missed it: Germany and Hungary revive defence ties – Leopard tanks, joint exercises and Ukraine on agenda

Magyar rejects linking EU budget negotiations to Ukraine

Péter Magyar took a different position, arguing that the EU’s seven-year budget should primarily serve the interests of European citizens, farmers, businesses and national economies.

He said Hungary would participate constructively in negotiations but would not compromise on its national interests.

The Hungarian prime minister stressed that agricultural and cohesion funding must not be significantly reduced. These funds are particularly important for Hungary, which has historically benefited from EU programmes designed to reduce economic disparities between member states.

Magyar also criticised the proposed financial arrangements, arguing that they could make Hungary one of the EU’s largest net contributors.

He further stated that Hungary could not accept being required to take out loans worth €1 billion or more, or provide guarantees for financing commitments of that magnitude.

However, Magyar did not reject European security cooperation. Instead, he argued that financial discussions should also recognise Hungary’s spending on protecting the EU’s external borders and its involvement in NATO and Western Balkan security missions.

The prime minister also referred to Hungary’s continuing negotiations with the European Commission over financial penalties related to its border and asylum policies, expressing hope that the dispute could be resolved before the end of 2026.

Germany offers energy cooperation to Hungary

Energy security was another important topic during the meeting between Péter Magyar and Friedrich Merz.

The Hungarian prime minister warned that high energy prices were undermining European competitiveness and placing increasing pressure on households and businesses.

Magyar welcomed Germany’s offer of cooperation in liquefied natural gas (LNG), emphasising Hungary’s interest in diversifying its energy supplies and securing oil and natural gas at competitive prices.

Germany also signalled its willingness to share expertise in LNG infrastructure and renewable energy as Hungary works to reduce its dependence on Russian energy supplies.

The leaders also discussed EU enlargement, particularly the accession prospects of Western Balkan countries.

Magyar reiterated Hungary’s support for Serbia and Montenegro joining the European Union, while stressing that Ukraine and Moldova should progress towards membership through a transparent, merit-based process.

Regarding Ukraine, he welcomed initial steps towards restoring the rights of the Hungarian minority living in the country, although he said further measures were necessary.

EU budget dispute could test Hungarian–German cooperation

The Berlin meeting demonstrated both the potential for closer Hungarian–German relations and the political challenges facing the two governments.

Economic cooperation, energy diversification and cultural ties offer opportunities for progress. However, their contrasting positions on financing Ukraine could become a significant obstacle during negotiations over the EU’s next long-term budget.

EU leaders are expected to discuss the funding disagreements at an informal summit in Dublin on Friday, 13 November.

For Hungary and Germany, the coming negotiations will test whether closer bilateral cooperation can coexist with fundamentally different approaches to sharing the financial burden of European security.
