World.title: Saudi university launches Red Sea coral restoration facility amid worsening global reef bleaching crisis
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) has launched a large-scale coral restoration facility on the Red Sea coast, aiming to produce up to 360,000 corals annually and restore 100 hectares of reef by 2030.

The opening of what KAUST describes as the world’s largest coral restoration facility was announced at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkiye, according to a university statement published late Wednesday.

The KAUST Coral Restoration Initiative (KCRI) operates a land-based nursery and research campus. It aims to plant more than 2 million corals across 100 hectares of reef at Shushah Island by 2030 and establish a resilient reef ecosystem by 2040.

The project comes as coral reefs face mounting threats from rising ocean temperatures and marine heat waves.

Corals growing in a nursery at the KAUST Coral Restoration Initiative. (SPA photo)

Global coral bleaching crisis

The fourth global coral bleaching event, which occurred between 2023 and 2025, affected more than 84 percent of the world’s reef area, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, or NOAA. It was the most severe such event on record.

Scientists also warn that a powerful El Niño weather pattern, forecast to intensify through early 2027, could expose vulnerable reefs to renewed severe heat stress.

KAUST said the Red Sea offers valuable opportunities for research because its corals survive in some of the world’s warmest and saltiest waters. Their natural resilience could provide lessons for protecting reefs elsewhere.

The initiative combines the region’s distinctive coral species with KAUST’s marine science expertise to develop methods for growing corals at scale and conditioning them to withstand warmer waters before they are returned to reefs.

It also draws on the expertise of the Coral Research and Development Accelerator Platform (CORDAP), an international initiative working to advance scientific and technological solutions for coral conservation and restoration.

Tanks at KAUST Coral Restoration Initiative. (KAUST photo)

Research, artificial intelligence and restoration

KCRI brings together four main components: a large-scale land-based coral nursery, sea-based nurseries, more than 50 research programs and an artificial intelligence-driven monitoring system.

The research programs cover areas including coral probiotics, heat-resistant corals, robotics and AI-based modeling.

The initiative also uses eCoral, an AI-driven digital twin of the reef system. The technology helps determine where corals should be planted and guides their subsequent monitoring.

“For the first time, we don’t just have the technology to predict the future of our oceans. We have the power to change it,” said Prof. Carlos Duarte, a KAUST distinguished professor and CORDAP executive director.

He described KCRI as a beacon of hope for the Red Sea and a potential model for coral restoration efforts worldwide.

Corals growing in a nursery at the KAUST Coral Restoration Initiative. (SPA photo)

Building Saudi scientific expertise

Saudi scientists, divers and aquarists are playing an important role in the initiative, developing specialized skills in coral cultivation, marine science and reef restoration.

KAUST said the project represents a long-term investment in the Kingdom’s marine science capabilities, beyond its immediate environmental goals.

“When we set out to develop KCRI, the ambition was to tackle a challenge that had never been addressed at this scale,” said Ian Campbell, senior vice president of KAUST’s National Transformation Institute.

“Opening the facility is not the finish line,” he said, adding that its success would be measured by the results achieved in the Red Sea, the expertise developed in Saudi Arabia and the contribution the research could make to reef restoration elsewhere.

Amr Atiah, KAUST’s vice president of campus and community and a former KCRI director of special projects, highlighted the opportunities the initiative offers young Saudis.

He said he was particularly encouraged by seeing young people develop an interest in marine science and build careers around protecting the Red Sea.

Atiah expressed hope that the opportunities created by the initiative would encourage more young Saudis to pursue careers in the field.

Coral reefs support about a quarter of all marine species, protect coastlines from storms and sustain the livelihoods of more than 500 million people, according to KAUST. (SPA photo)

Protecting marine ecosystems

Coral reefs support about a quarter of all marine species, protect coastlines from storms and sustain the livelihoods of more than 500 million people, according to KAUST.

The university said KCRI aims not only to restore the Red Sea’s reef ecosystem but also to develop a framework that other coral restoration programs around the world could adopt.

KAUST is also working with international partners to find ways to safeguard coral diversity for future generations.

World.title: Israeli strike kills six at southern Gaza hospital: civil defense
World.content:
GAZA CITY, Palestinian Territories: An Israeli strike killed six people and wounded around 20 at Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, a civil defense official told AFP on Thursday.

The Gaza Strip’s civil defense, a rescue agency operating under Hamas authority, said the bodies of those killed and “more than” 20 people wounded in the strike had been recovered from a building at the medical complex.

“The death toll from the Israeli strike inside Nasser Medical Complex, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, has risen to six,” civil defense spokesperson Mahmoud Bassal told AFP.

Nasser Hospital confirmed the six deaths in a statement.

A spokesperson for Israel’s military said they were checking for information on the incident when asked for comment by AFP.

Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, after two years of war triggered by an attack of unprecedented scale carried out by the Palestinian Islamist movement against Israel on October 7, 2023.

On Tuesday, Israeli forces killed seven people, including a 13-year-old boy, in the Gaza Strip, according to local emergency services, while the Israeli military said it had targeted “military operatives.”

More than 1,590 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to the Gaza Ministry of Health, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

During the same period, the Israeli military has reported the loss of seven soldiers, as well as one civilian contractor.

World.title: Andreeva reaches WTA Finals semis, Svitolina fights back to beat Muchova
World.content:
INDIAN WELLS, California: World ‌number three Mirra Andreeva booked her place in the semifinals of the WTA Finals with a 6-4 ​6-0 win over Aryna Sabalenka on Wednesday, while Elina Svitolina battled back to beat Karolina Muchova and keep her hopes alive.

Andreeva, the 19-year-old French Open champion, won her second straight Group 2 match and advanced as group winner after Svitolina earlier defeated Muchova ‌3-6 6-2 ‌6-2.

The result eliminated Muchova from ​semifinal ‌contention, ⁠while ​Svitolina will ⁠face Sabalenka in Friday’s final group match with the remaining place in the last four at stake.

Sabalenka, the world number two and US Open runner-up, made the stronger start and broke Andreeva in the fourth game of ⁠a closely fought opening set to ‌move 3-1 ahead.

Andreeva responded ‌immediately, however, winning three consecutive ​games to draw ‌level at 4-4 before breaking Sabalenka again and ‌serving out the set.

The Russian maintained the momentum in the second set, capitalizing on Sabalenka’s errors to break early and race into a 3-0 lead.

Andreeva ‌did not allow Sabalenka another game, sealing a dominant victory on her ⁠WTA ⁠Finals debut.

Earlier, Svitolina recovered from a set down to overcome Muchova in their third consecutive meeting to go the distance.

Both players had lost their opening matches in straight sets, but Muchova edged a competitive first set before Svitolina raised her level.

The Ukrainian broke twice in the second set and served it out to force a decider, before carrying ​that momentum into ​the final set with another two breaks of serve.

World.title: Syrian demining worker killed, another injured as explosive remnants claim 14 lives since Oct. 14
World.content:
ALEPPO, Syria: A member of Syria's Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management was killed and another injured on Wednesday while clearing explosive remnants of war in eastern Aleppo countryside, bringing the death toll from landmines and other unexploded ordnance across the country to at least 14 since October 14.

The ministry identified the deceased as Farouk Abadan, a member of its war remnants clearance and demining teams, who was killed while carrying out a clearance operation in the village of Al-Seen.

His colleague, Mustafa Al-Taha, was injured in the same operation, the ministry said in a statement mourning Abadan's death and wishing the injured worker a speedy recovery.

Minister of Emergency and Disaster Management Raed Al-Saleh said in a post on X that teams tasked with clearing landmines and explosive remnants of war faced significant challenges because of their widespread presence across Syria and the complexity of safely handling and disposing of them.

Landmine explosion victims include civilians, military personnel and children, highlighting the continuing danger posed by explosive devices left behind by the ousted regime, as well as the risks faced by teams working to remove them. (SANA photo)

The latest casualties add to a growing toll from explosive remnants of the country's civil war. At least 14 people have been killed and 17 injured in reported landmine and unexploded ordnance incidents between October 14 and November 11, according to figures from recent reports carried by SANA.

The victims include civilians, military personnel and children, highlighting the continuing danger posed by explosive devices left behind by the ousted regime, as well as the risks faced by teams working to remove them.

Civilians and children among the victims

A SANA roundup published on November 1 documented seven deaths and 11 injuries in six explosions involving landmines and unexploded ordnance across Hasakah, Hama, Daraa and Quneitra provinces between October 24 and 30.

Three children were among those killed, while several other children were wounded.

The incidents included a cluster munition explosion in Latamneh, northern Hama, that killed a six-year-old child and injured three others who were playing in a house garden. In western Hasakah, a landmine explosion near grain silos in Umm Al-Keif village killed one child and seriously injured two others.

Three young men were also killed and two people injured in a landmine explosion in Umm Zar village near Al-Shaddadi in Hasakah on October 27.

Other incidents involved a four-year-old boy killed while his family was harvesting olives in Halfaya, northern Hama, on October 26, and a young man killed by an unexploded cluster munition while grazing sheep in northern Quneitra on October 24.

Two children were also injured in a separate landmine explosion in Daraa's Khirbet Ghazaleh area.

Military personnel and clearance teams also targeted

The danger has extended to Syrian military personnel involved in dismantling explosive devices.

On November 4, two Syrian Arab Army soldiers were killed when a landmine left behind by the ousted regime exploded in Daraa countryside.

Three days later, another soldier was killed and a second injured in a landmine blast while they were working to dismantle remnants of the former regime in the Al-Mayadin area of eastern Deir Ezzor countryside.

Earlier, on October 17, a member of the Military Engineering Administration was killed and another injured while clearing landmines and other remnants of war in the Al-Tanf area of eastern Homs countryside.

On October 14, a young man was seriously injured when a landmine exploded near an excavator he was operating on farmland between Otman and Dael in Daraa province.

The civilian toll also rose on November 3, when a landmine explosion in Al-Bukamal, eastern Deir Ezzor, killed two people and injured two others. The injured included a girl whose condition was being assessed after she was transferred to Deir Ezzor National Hospital.

Landmine explosion victims include civilians, military personnel and children, highlighting the continuing danger posed by explosive devices left behind by the ousted regime, as well as the risks faced by teams working to remove them. (SANA photo)

A persistent threat to Syria's recovery

Landmines, unexploded cluster munitions and other explosive remnants continue to threaten communities across Syria, particularly in agricultural areas where residents risk encountering buried or unexploded devices while cultivating their land, harvesting crops or grazing livestock.

The contamination also complicates efforts to restore normal life and facilitate the return of displaced families to their homes, as many communities remain exposed to hazards even after fighting has subsided.

Syrian authorities have continued clearance operations through engineering units and specialized teams from the Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management and the Ministry of Defense.

According to figures previously reported by SANA, Syrian Arab Army engineering units dismantled and destroyed more than 110,000 explosive objects across the country between the beginning of 2026 and April. The devices included landmines, improvised explosive devices and unexploded ammunition.

The latest death of a demining worker underscores the dangers facing personnel tasked with making contaminated areas safe, as Syria continues efforts to remove explosive remnants and restore access to homes, farmland and public spaces.

World.title: Russian ambassador to US dies, foreign ministry says
World.content:
MOSCOW: Russia’s ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, has died aged ‌66, ‌the ​Russian Foreign ‌Ministry ⁠said ​on Wednesday.

Ministry ⁠spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said later on Telegram that Darchiev had died ⁠in Moscow from ‌a ‌chronic ​illness.

Putin ‌appointed Darchiev, a ‌veteran diplomat known in the past for his public ‌denunciations of the West, as ⁠ambassador ⁠to Washington in March 2025 to lead a rapprochement with the Trump administration that has rattled Ukraine and ​European ​countries.

World.title: Motor racing-Hamilton urges Israel to let Gaza aid in after Rafah visit
World.content:
Formula One driver Lewis ‌Hamilton said on Wednesday that Israel must allow aid trucks into Gaza, a day after he visited ​the Rafah border crossing in Egypt.

Hamilton, a seven-times world champion, arrived in El Arish on Tuesday, where he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it is sent into Gaza, as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent’s ‌aid warehouses.

“The past ‌three years of Israel’s ​genocide ‌in ⁠Gaza ​is appalling. ⁠It’s an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less,” the Ferrari driver wrote on Instagram.

Israel strongly denies accusations of genocide ⁠and says its military campaign in ‌Gaza targets Hamas militants.

Hamilton ‌described seeing food trucks lined ​up and ready to ‌go at the border that were regularly ‌held up or faced major delays.

He said that at a nearby logistics center, items had been rejected for “crazy reasons,” including sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, ‌wheelchairs, and footballs for children.

“Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ⁠ceasefire ⁠and let the aid trucks in. No excuse,” he said. “I don’t want us to get used to their suffering. I don’t want us to look away.”

Hamilton, 41, is an advocate for humanitarian causes. In 2021 he founded Mission 44, a charity that supports young people and works to improve their access to education and employment.

He is fourth in the drivers’ ​championship. Mercedes’ Kimi ​Antonelli has won the title with three races remaining.

World.title: Debris falls on Makkah region after Houthi missiles destroyed by Coalition
World.content:
RIYADH: Fragments of two ballistic missiles that were destroyed over Makkah fell in the village of Sabouha, the Saudi Civil Defense said early on Thursday.

Earlier, two drones launched by the Houthi militia were intercepted and destroyed in the Makkah and southern regions, the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen said on Wednesday.

The spokesperson for the coalition Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki said separately that three cruise missiles launched by the Houthi militia toward the Riyadh region had been destroyed.

Later on in the evening, the coalition announced that air defenses intercepted and destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles in Saudi Arabia's western region.

This is not the first time that the Iran-backed Houthi militia have targeted the Makkah region, home to the holiest site in Islam.

Last month, the Kingdom condemned the group for launching a drone toward the holy city.

In 2017, Saudi air defense forces intercepted a ballistic missile launched toward Makkah. The coalition said the missile was shot down over Al-Wasliya area in Taif province, some 69 kilometers away from Makkah.

The Houthis have been firing missiles and drones at the Kingdom as part of the wider war in the region between the US and Israel on one side and Iran, a key funder of the Yemeni group, on the other.

World.title: Trump defends Iran war in Veterans Day address
World.content:
WASHINGTON, United States: President Donald Trump defended the war against Iran Wednesday at a US Veterans Day commemoration that saw his defense secretary publicly admonished for a lack of decorum.

“The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible,” Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington.

“When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better place, more peaceful place, and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer.”

The war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes against Iran, has so far cost the lives of 23 US service members and wounded several hundred more, according to the latest Pentagon figures.

Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which “has been waging war on America since 1979.” He stressed that US forces were acting in order to halt Iran’s capacity to build a nuclear weapon.

Trump, 80, attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery’s Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a sacred symbol for America’s lost service members.

During his speech before troops, veterans and top officials in his administration, Trump namechecked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who was in attendance, saying he had “done a fantastic job.”

Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort — launched by an outgoing Republican lawmaker — to impeach Hegseth for allegedly waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.

Hegseth stirred even more controversy at the ceremony: an army sentinel watching over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reprimanded a small group of people that included Hegseth, his wife and several aides, when some of them laughed after posing for a picture in front of the sacred site.

“All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times,” the sentinel called out, halting his patrol to face the group as they walked up some stairs to leave. Hegseth turned around to look at the guard.

During his remarks, Trump brought up the issue of the 250-foot-tall (76-meter-tall) triumphal arch he hopes to build just outside the cemetery, saying it would be dedicated “soon.”

On Tuesday, the family of John F. Kennedy asked a court to prevent its construction, arguing the massive structure would block views and cast shadows over the gravesites of the slain president and other Kennedy relatives buried at Arlington National Cemetery.

The project also faces lawsuits from a group of veterans, the city of Washington and the state of Virginia.

World.title: Iraq Museum in Baghdad to reopen on December 1 following two-year closure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities announced the official reopening of the Iraq Museum in Baghdad, scheduled for December 1 (1-12-2026), following an extensive closure that lasted for more than two years.

According to an official document published by the Ministry’s General Directorate of Public Relations and Media, Minister of Tourism and Antiquities Dr. Ali Al-Dakhili confirmed the decision to reopen the landmark cultural institution to domestic visitors, international tourists, and researchers from around the world.

The reopening follows extensive renovation and curatorial preparations across the museum’s historic exhibition halls, which house tens of thousands of Mesopotamian, Sumerian, Babylonian, and Assyrian antiquities.

The document highlighted several key artifacts and curated wings prepared for public display:

Assyrian Statues and Reliefs: Featuring monumental winged bulls (lamassu) and stone carvings depicting legendary Assyrian monarchs.

Cuneiform Collections: Ancient clay tablets and historical prisms recording legal codes, administrative decrees, and foundational texts of ancient Mesopotamia.

Abbasid and Islamic Galleries: Intricately carved wooden mihrabs, monumental calligraphic friezes, and fine decorative architectural panels.

Mosaics and Stone Relics: Classical stone carvings, glasswork, and multi-era mosaics recovered and restored across diverse historical periods.

The ministry characterized the December 1 reopening as a pivotal milestone for Iraq’s cultural recovery and heritage tourism, framing the reactivation of the country’s flagship museum as a national celebration and an enduring bridge linking modern Iraqis and the global community to the roots of world civilization.

World.title: Spain’s De la Fuente hopeful teen star Yamal can face England
World.content:
Prague – Spain coach Luis de la Fuente said Wednesday he is optimistic Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal will be fit to face England in the Nations League at the weekend.

The 19-year-old winger will miss the world champions’ visit to face the Czech Republic in Prague on Thursday with a knee problem and is set to join up with Spain after that game.

Yamal played for Barcelona in the 2-1 La Liga win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday and on Monday Spain said he would not travel to face the Czechs.

“He got hurt in the last match, he had some discomfort in one knee, he went for the usual treatment, a scan in Barcelona, and they saw he had inflammation and fluid in the knee — that meant he needed rest,” De la Fuente told reporters.

“Our medical staff and his medical staff have a fantastic relationship, and I decided that his trip here should be avoided without knowing whether he’d be in any condition to play.”

The coach said he had spoken to the winger and his recovery was looking positive ahead of England’s visit to Madrid on Sunday.

“He’s doing a series of exercises with his physio and with the club that indicate the recovery is going well,” continued De la Fuente.

“We believe, I’m optimistic, that on Friday he’ll be with us.”

De la Fuente dismissed the idea that Yamal, who came third in the Ballon d’Or voting in October, has any special privileges compared to his La Roja team-mates.

“He has no privileges, and his team-mates are relaxed about it, because we treat everyone the same,” added the coach.

“In similar situations we would have done exactly the same for any other player, and the players know that.”

– Unstoppable run –

Spain have won all four games so far in Group A3 and sealed qualification to the quarter-finals.

De la Fuente’s side are unbeaten in their last 43 competitive outings, and the coach said it provided his team with extra motivation.

“We want to keep setting new milestones, and this is another one,” explained De la Fuente.

“None of us would probably ever have thought we’d even reach 35, because we already felt those were astronomical numbers, but having reached 43, you think, my goodness, we want to get to 44, of course we do.”

Spain won their previous outing away in Croatia with a brace from Arsenal’s Mikel Merino.

The midfielder is frequently used as a substitute by De la Fuente to great effect, with Merino netting vital goals against Portugal and Belgium in the World Cup off the bench this summer.

Merino said he would like to be a starter for Spain but he would not kick up a fuss.

“Of course, what player wouldn’t like to get (more) minutes?” Merino told reporters.

“You’ll never hear me complain about the coach’s decision, I will respect it… but all players want to be important, have minutes and enjoy themselves on the pitch.”

World.title: Iraq can serve as diplomatic bridge between US and Iran: US envoy
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US Special Envoy for Iraq and Syria Tom Barrack stated that Iraq can serve as a diplomatic bridge between the United States and Iran.

Speaking at the Chatham House Iraq Initiative event in London, Barrack pointed out that Iraq may serve as a “magic key that unlocks the door” for a new sort of dialogue that Washington is unable to conduct directly.

Barrack emphasized that Iraq and Iran have “hand and glove” policies due to their shared 1,500-kilometer border, close religious connections, and extensive historical engagement.

Barrack also called for foreign investments, especially from American, French, Italian, and Middle Eastern corporations, to construct new pipeline infrastructure alongside current lines to help Iraq reach its goal of producing 10 million barrels of oil per day.

The US official underlined that Iraq’s largest obstacle to drawing in the international investment necessary for long-term prosperity and stability is still establishing the rule of law and clear regulations.

World.title: Al-Zaidi orders foundation stones laid for 1M land plots by 2027
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi directed local and federal authorities on Wednesday to lay the foundation stones for the ambitious “One Million Residential Plots” initiative (the Watan Initiative) across all governorates before the close of 2026.

Chaired by Al-Zaidi, the Seventh Regular Session of the High Commission for Coordination Between Governorates focused on reviewing intergovernmental mechanisms to accelerate infrastructure delivery and streamline stalled development portfolios.

According to a press statement released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office and carried by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the General Coordinator for Provincial Affairs presented a comprehensive operational report confirming that groundbreaking has already taken place across four governorates: Karbala, Najaf, Nineveh, and Anbar.

Preparations are finalized for immediate foundation laying in Basra and Maysan, while Saladin, Diyala, and Dhi Qar have completed all statutory and administrative clearances. To expedite delivery, provincial investment commissions were formally empowered to handle technical contracting workflows for the housing rollout. Al-Zaidi also issued directives to accelerate the counterpart initiative allocating one million agricultural plots nationwide.

Addressing inter-provincial connectivity and road safety, the Prime Minister ordered the formation of a ministerial steering committee led by the Deputy Prime Minister for Service Affairs, with the Minister of Construction, Housing, Municipalities, and Public Works and the General Coordinator for Provincial Affairs serving as members.

The committee is tasked with conducting an immediate operational audit of arterial highways connecting Iraqi governorates to prioritize widening, resurfacing, congestion relief, and commercial freight optimization.

The High Commission adopted a comprehensive package of executive decisions to regulate urban expansion, municipal revenues, and public services:

World.title: ‘Dictator’ Infantino needs psychiatric help, says former FIFA chief Blatter
World.content:
Berlin – Former FIFA boss Sepp Blatter has slammed current chief Gianni Infantino, calling his successor a “dictator” and suggesting he needs psychiatric help, in an interview with Der Spiegel published Wednesday.

Blatter, 90, criticised Infantino’s decision to create the FIFA Peace Prize award for US President Donald Trump in the lead-up to this year’s World Cup, hosted in the US, Canada and Mexico.

He was also critical of Infantino’s post-World Cup plans to sell off part of the commercial rights of the competition in the future, which was scrapped after a fierce backlash.

“FIFA is suffering. It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded,” Blatter told the German magazine.

The Peace Prize, he said, was “embarrassing”.

“Why would he do something like that?,” Blatter asked. “Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards? That’s madness.”

Blatter said it was easy for Infantino to secure support for his own re-election from national football bodies.

“‘If you vote for me,’ he tells the national associations, ‘you will get much more money than before.’

“He is a dictator. People in FIFA tell me that no one is allowed to ride in the elevator with him. He is ‘untouchable’.”

Speaking of Infantino’s World Cup sale plans, Blatter said: “Infantino no longer knows any borders. He doesn’t understand any of this.

“I mean, maybe Infantino should be sent to a psychiatric ward one day.”

President of FIFA from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations, including accusations he had sought to buy votes for his presidency.

Charges were brought against him but Blatter was eventually cleared in two trials but was banned from football by FIFA’s ethics committee.

Blatter told the magazine he had “no regrets” from his time in charge of the organisation.

The Swiss was also critical of FIFA’s decision to suspend a red card awarded to USA striker Folarin Balogun after Trump intervened ahead of a crucial match at this summer’s World Cup.

“The red card. That’s the worst. Statutes can be interpreted. But rules of the game must apply to everyone, you can’t interpret them.”

Japanese official Kozo Tashima has announced plans to run against Infantino in his re-election bid, but Blatter named World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as his pick to take over FIFA.

“It is not important who is running. What is important is that the incumbent president is no longer elected.

“Coe was also chairman of the FIFA Ethics Committee. He is a strong personality. A president from the motherland of football, England, would be good.”

Blatter said he had not spoken with Infantino since early 2016.

AFP has contacted FIFA for a response.

World.title: Iraq, Bahrain review regional developments
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and the King of Bahrain, Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, discussed on Wednesday bilateral relations between the two countries and approaches to enhance joint cooperation in different sectors.

During their phone conversation, the two leaders addressed regional developments, ongoing efforts to de-escalate tensions and promote stability, and the importance of coordination on issues of mutual interest, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi renewed his invitation to the King of Bahrain to visit Iraq. He also commended Bahrain’s stance and its positive role in the region, emphasizing the importance of promoting relations between the two countries and expanding the horizons of cooperation.

The king of Bahrain praised Iraq’s contribution to regional peace and stability, expressed his great admiration for the Iraqi people, and reaffirmed his country’s support for the Iraqi government’s initiatives.

The two leaders’ discussion comes a few days after Bahrain formally decided to send its ambassador back to Iraq, signaling a major diplomatic step forward.

Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani made the announcement on Saturday following a phone conversation.

The major development took place after Iraqi al-Zaidi made a formal visit to Manama.

Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, the crown prince of Bahrain, described al-Zaidi’s trip as historic, pointing out that it was the first time an Iraqi prime minister has visited Bahrain since 2003.

Zayani emphasized that reinstating the ambassador demonstrates Bahrain’s commitment to enhancing joint cooperation and reinforcing communication channels to support regional stability, according to the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

In the past few years, relations between Iraq and Bahrain have occasionally been strained. In June 2019, Bahrain recalled its ambassador after demonstrators broke into the embassy’s headquarters in Baghdad.

In April 2026, Manama summoned Iraq’s chargé d’affaires due to regional security concerns, despite the appointment of Khalid al-Mansour as a new ambassador in 2024 to improve relations.

World.title: Iraq plans to build gas pipeline linking south to north
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry has ordered a feasibility study to build a national liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) pipeline running from the southern part of the country to the northern provinces of Nineveh and Kirkuk.

The project aims to resolve domestic distribution bottlenecks, bridge a growing supply deficit, and create export capacity for surplus fuel.

Deputy Oil Minister for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber announced the plan on Tuesday following meetings with ministry officials and oil company representatives.

The pipeline would deliver LPG straight to northern distribution networks in Kirkuk and Nineveh from southern production hubs.

In addition to stabilizing domestic supplies, the project is intended to allow Iraq to export surplus LPG to foreign markets.

The Iraqi government has not yet disclosed the precise route, estimated cost, pipeline capacity, construction schedule, or collaborating companies.

Iraq produces around 4,500 tons of LPG per day compared to a domestic demand of 4,700 tons, resulting in a daily shortage of roughly 200 tons.

With more motorists switching from gasoline to gas, domestic consumption has significantly increased. The number of vehicles using gas rose to 95,000 in July 2026, up from just 70,000 in March.

To replace slow tanker-truck transport with direct pipeline delivery, the new line complements larger network upgrades, such as a 3,000-cubic-meter LPG depot in Najaf that started trial operations in August 2026.

World.title: Former Iraqi MP found dead in Lebanon
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Lebanese and Iraqi authorities have launched an investigation after the body of former Iraqi lawmaker Ahmed al-Alwani was discovered in an apartment in the Lebanese capital, Beirut.

While initial reports from Lebanese media emerged on Tuesday, judicial sources indicate the body was found on Monday evening in the Tariq al-Jadideh neighborhood.

Authorities found the body after al-Alwani’s family reported losing contact with him four days earlier.

Although authorities have not yet issued a complete forensic report, media outlets mentioned that al-Alwani was strangled with a curtain cord after being lured to the residence.

Three suspects who allegedly leased the property were identified by investigators: two Syrian nationals and one Lebanese citizen.

The two Syrian suspects are said to have left the country, while security personnel apprehended the Lebanese suspect for interrogation.

According to surveillance footage, al-Alwani and two guys entered the premises freely.

The corpse was sent to Zahle Government Hospital once it was discovered.

Judge Ahmad Rami al-Hajj, Lebanon’s chief prosecutor, requested DNA testing in addition to a family examination to confirm the identity because the remains had started to decay.

Mohammed al-Husseini, Iraq’s ambassador to Lebanon, affirmed that the embassy is working with Lebanese security services in anticipation of the official results.

Between 2005 and 2014, al-Alwani chaired the parliament’s economic committee and represented the western Anbar province of Iraq.

A well-known supporter of the Sunni demonstrations against the administration of former Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki in 2012 and 2013, al-Alwani was arrested in a raid on his home in December 2013.

The former Iraqi lawmaker was released under a nationwide amnesty in April 2025 after spending more than 11 years on terrorism-related accusations.

World.title: Centre looks to open up car-rental market, cuts proposed minimum fleet to five
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a move that could make it easier for more players to enter and expand in the self-drive and chauffeur-driven car rental business, the road transport ministry has proposed reducing the minimum fleet requirement to just five vehicles from the existing 50.

The draft scheme also explicitly extends its coverage to rental vehicles offered with or without drivers.

The road transport ministry has proposed sweeping changes in the draft Rent-a-Cab Scheme, 2026, which would be the first comprehensive replacement of the 1989 framework in 37 years. A limited amendment was carried out in 2021 by extending its coverage to battery-operated cabs and those running on methanol and ethanol that are exempt from permit requirements.



The reduction in the minimum fleet requirement to just five vehicles -- a minimum of two vehicles stationed at each place of operation -- is likely to encourage smaller entrepreneurs, local car-rental companies and start-ups to enter the business. It may also help existing operators expand into more locations without having to maintain a large fleet.

The proposed scheme, which ministry targets to roll out from next year also introduces stricter safety, insurance and operational requirements for companies renting out cars and at the same time it proposes to introduce online licencing, time-bound approvals and a formal grievance redressal mechanism.





It proposes to fix the licencing fee at Rs 25,000, irrespective of the size of the fleet or the number of operating locations.

The proposed framework also introduces a nine-year age limit for vehicles; valid registration, fitness and pollution certificates, paid motor vehicle tax and comprehensive insurance covering the renter, driver and other occupants up to the vehicleâs passenger capacity. Vehicles must also be free of specified pending challans and unpaid toll fees, and must not figure in the National Crime Records Bureauâs police crime database.

Another major departure in the proposed scheme is it explicitly covers renting vehicles with or without drivers. The 1989 framework was primarily designed for self-drive rentals. Operators will now be required to provide drivers with valid licences, police-verified character and antecedents, no unpaid challans and welfare coverage under the Code on Social Security, 2020.

The draft also introduces passenger-safety requirements, including vehicle location tracking devices, child restraint systems, first-aid kits and round-the-clock customer care.

It proposes that operators must resolve website-based grievances within 24 hours and complete an inquiry into complaints against drivers within seven days.

As per the draft, licencing will also become digital. Applications and renewals will be submitted electronically, with authorities required to process them within 60 days. The licence will remain valid for five years. Applications for adding or removing operating locations or vehicles will be deemed approved if authorities do not decide within 30 days.

World.title: Collegium wants transfer of HC judges streamlined, random ways discarded
World.content:
Collegium wants transfer of HC judges streamlined, random ways discarded

Judge âclose toâ CJI runs transfer risk once mentor leaves office

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court collegium is trying to break away from the unwritten norms for transfer of judges from one high court to another, done so far on the basis of a judge's integrity, conduct, requirement of expertise in another HC and, very often, because of his/her closeness to an ex-CJI or ex-collegium member.The five-member SC collegium led by CJI Surya Kant and comprising Justices Vikram Nath, B V Nagarathna, M M Sundresh and P S Narasimha had an informal discussion last week on evolving a well-defined policy framework to streamline the process for transfer of judges from their parent HC to another. They felt that random or pick-and-choose methods of transfer for reasons that are not objective must be discarded. A proposal for transfer of a judge from his/her parent HC to another could be moved for various reasons.For instance, an HC judge, high in seniority, could be transferred to prepare him/her for taking over as CJ of that HC. There have also been occasions when a senior judge was sent to another HC to create a buffer between the CJ and senior judges there because they were not getting along.There have been cases where transfer proposals were initiated when in-house inquiries corroborated complaints regarding the integrity of a judge or that his/her behaviour was unbecoming of the constitutional post in the courtroom or in public.On the constructive side, a judge having expertise in certain fields of litigation could be transferred to another HC where his/her services could be more productive.There is another reason as well, one that has never made it to the records but has always been whispered aloud, a secret that is hardly so â a judge perceived to be close to a CJI or a member of the SC collegium who is transferred as soon as the mentor has demitted office. Very often, it is meant to settle scores against the CJI who refused to accommodate requests for appointment or transfer of judges from colleagues. All these grounds for transfers till 2018 were couched in the specious âin the interest of better administration of justiceâ officialese.The phraseology was discarded by 2020 and collegium resolutions plainly stated the transfer of a particular judge.In 2022, the collegium had recommended transfers of 18 HC judges, 34 in 2023, 11 in 2024, 44 in 2025 and 12 in 2026. The deliberations among members of the SC collegium would factor in the complexities and may also include a provision for reconsideration of a recommendation for transfer which has not been honoured by the executive.There have been some examples where recommendations for transfers remained pending for years with govt. In some cases, the collegium had acted expeditiously in accepting representations of HC judges seeking transfers while in others, it had maintained a posture of benign indifference.Even though SC has frowned upon transfers being used as a punitive measure, the majority of transfers in the past five years were seen as dislodging judges from their parent HCs because of one or the other complaint.A view has gained ground that in such situations, the judge concerned should be asked by the CJ concerned to mend his/her ways within a specified period before the collegium resorts to shifting him/her out.

World.title: SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Taking advantage of liberal laws abroad to obtain a divorce for a wedding solemnised in India will not automatically lead to dissolution of the marriage under Indian law,

has ruled.

Viewing negatively the use in a foreign court of grounds for divorce which are not recognised in India, SC said a person who contracts a second marriage on that basis may face prosecution for bigamy as the first marriage continues to subsist under Indian law, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.

With many men approaching a foreign court to get a divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage - despite the wife opposing the plea - and thereafter remarrying, SC said the person has to face proceedings even in a case where he had become a citizen of a foreign country.



The top court said legal consequences stemm-ing from the subsisting marriage cannot be overridden by a subsequent change in a spouse's nationality.

Irretrievable breakdown of marriage no divorce ground in Indian law: SC

The bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar allowed criminal proceedings for bigamy against a man who remarried after getting a divorce order from a foreign court on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage in proceedings opposed by the wife.





The court said that irretrievable breakdown of marriage is not a ground for divorce in Indian law and, therefore, the divorce granted by the foreign court is not valid.

âIn our view, the foreign divorce decree was passed in contravention of the existing matrimonial law in India and on a ground that is not even recognised statutorily. This violates the legal threshold of Section 13 of the CPC, which every foreign decree has to pass through,â the SC bench said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The bench also said that if the foreign decree does not satisfy the requirements of Section 13 of the Civil Procedure Code, then the husband, relying on such a decree, cannot be permitted to contend that his first marriage stood dissolved in the eyes of matrimonial laws of India and, thus, escape the rigours of Section 494 of IPC (marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife).

âNow, coming to the argument of the husband that since he was a British citizen when the second marriage with second wife was solemnised and since the second marriage took place outside India, keeping in view the mandate of Section 4 of the IPC, he cannot be held liable. We cannot accept this submission in the manner canvassed as the husband was married to first wife in India under Hindu rites, rituals and customs; thus, even if the second marriage took place outside India, the allegations under Section 494 of the IPC cannot be said to be diluted since enquiry for the offence of bigamy cannot be confined to the place of second marriage but must necessarily take into account the subsisting matrimonial relationship.

..â the bench said.

The court, however, quashed criminal proceedings against the parents and second wife of the man.

World.title: Complete data could've raised average Diwali pollution level 49%
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Missing PM2.5 data from monitoring stations could have raised the city's average pollution level by 49% on Diwali, according to an analysis by Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).

Had the missing readings been recorded at 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre (g/mÂ³), the city's average PM2.5 level would have increased from 269 to 400(g/mÂ³), it revealed. The daily national ambient air quality standard for PM2.5 is 60 g/mÂ³ and WHO's safe guideline is 15 g/mÂ³.

The analysis was done a day after Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) said its stations' analysers were calibrated to measure particulate matter concentrations only up to 1,000g/mÂ³ and could not display readings beyond it on Diwali night for several hours.



Nor were these readings considered for calculating the average AQI, it said.

CREA said if 400g/mÂ³ had been considered, city's AQI on Monday would have risen from 344 (very poor) to near severe. AQI is calculated based on 8 pollutants, including PM2.5.

TOI reported Tuesday that CPCB had stopped giving data on particulate matter at the peak of Diwali night pollution for several hours after particulate matter levels at air quality monitoring stations surpassed 1,000g/mÂ³.





However, Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), which operates 43 of the total 60 stations, gave readings on Diwali night that crossed 1,000g/mÂ³. At least at 11 locations, the hourly PM2.5 concentration was above 2,000g/mÂ³. In four, it was above 3,000.

CPCB compiles data from all 60 stations and releases the AQI. One station has been defunct for the past few months.

The latest analysis examined hourly PM2.5 data from 59 monitoring stations between 4pm on Nov 8 and 4pm on Nov 9, corresponding to the 24-hour averaging period used for CPCB's 4pm AQI bulletin on Nov 9.

It analysed 1,416 hours (24 hours x 59 stations).

It found that 255 of the 1,416 expected station-hour observations or 18% were missing. CREA conducted a sensitivity analysis by assigning them a value of 1,000g/mÂ³, the upper measurement limit cited by CPCB for particulate matter. Under this scenario, the pooled average PM2.5 concentration across the expected observations increased from 269g/mÂ³ to 400g/mÂ³, a rise of 49%.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The peak PM2.5 levels of Delhi was 584 g/mÂ³ at 1am on Nov 9 when there was missing data. However, after replacing the missing data with 1,000 g/mÂ³, the peak PM2.5 concentration was 825 g/mÂ³ at 2am and 824 g/mÂ³ at 3am," said CREA.

It clarified that the sensitivity analysis does not establish that all 255 missing observations were caused by PM2.5 concentrations exceeding 1,000g/mÂ³. Assigning the upper measurement limit to these observations was only an illustrative exercise to understand how the reported average could change under such a scenario.

TOI reported Tuesday that hourly PM2.5 levels at Mundka touched 3,744g/mÂ³ at 2am Monday, according to DPCC's data. However, CPCB did not share Mundka's PM2.5 readings from 12 midnight to 4 am.

World.title: Yuge Yugeen museum set to open doors to public next year; cabinet approves Rs 3,230 cr
World.content:
NEW DELHI: North Block, which once housed the home and finance ministries, will reopen in less than a year from now, showcasing the first gallery of one of the largest museums in the world.

Announced three years ago, Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum (YYBM) will be opened to public next year, govt said Wednesday after the cabinet committee on economic affairs (CCEA) cleared a Rs 3,230 crore development plan for the museum that will include the North and South Blocks and will be spread over nearly 1.8 lakh square metre, equal to 25 football fields. Once complete in 2031, the museumâs display area will be 1 lakh square metre, compared with 73,000 square metre of display area in Louvre and 70,000 square metre at the British Museum.



On X, PM Narendra Modi said, âImagine New Delhi becoming home to the worldâs largest museum display area? Think scale. Think culture. That is the vision behind Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum...From ancient knowledge systems, mathematics and astronomy to architecture, art, languages and spirituality, the museum will bring thousands of years of our heritage to life through immersive experiences and world-class galleries.





â

The project scheduled to be complete by March 2031 will cost nearly two-and-half times that of the new Parliament building.

I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters that the museum aims at presenting the complete âcivilisational journeyâ of India using modern technology while maintaining architectural integrity of the two buildings on Raisina Hill that were until recently the seat of power.

Culture ministry, which is working on the project, was looking at opening the inaugural gallery by 2026-end.

The ministry will soon start work on laying out the gallery, which will be on the theme of âadornmentâ in the North Block, officials said. This gallery is expected to present the aesthetics that have defined Indiaâs civilisational journey through the ages depicting it through the jewellery and decorations.

A modular approach is being formulated to add more galleries. The content and collection analysis is being done and around 1.8 million objects have been identified from National Museum and other culture ministry museums, 52 Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) site museums and various state museums and private collections to be displayed in the YYBM.

Although the museum will open next year, the metro station that will come up next to Rakabganj Gurdwara is likely to be operational by June 2029 and will act as a crucial link given that nearly 70% of visitors are expected to come from the entry gate behind the North Block. The earlier plan to explore connecting the North and South Blocks through an underground tunnel has been dropped and will now have a surface level connection, officials said.

The museum is also expected to generate recurring revenue through ticket sales, food and beverage facilities, events and venue rentals, digital experiences, guided tours, retail outlets and other visitor services.

TOI has learnt that the CCEA has approved the culture ministryâs proposal of annual revenue generation of around Rs 163 crore from letting out five auditoriums and venues for events and programmes, seven food courts and sale of tickets.

The ministry, in its proposal, has proposed Rs 100 as ticket for Indians and Rs 1,000 for foreigners.

Considering the scale of the museum, there will be a separate director general and four additional director generals for the project. People aware of the project said around 262 posts would be created, including curators and support staff.

World.title: NTA plans exam centres in every district
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a move that could spare lakhs of students long journeys for entrance examinations, the education ministry has initiated an exercise to create a nationwide pool of standardised examination centres, with the aim of having at least one in every district.

The plan also envisages backup centres nearby to deal with last-minute disruptions. In a parallel move, the National Testing Agency (

) is creating a permanent pool of independent observers, including retired armed forces and paramilitary personnel, as part of a wider overhaul of the examination system following repeated security breaches and disruptions.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The twin initiatives are aimed at addressing two persistent problems - inadequate examination infrastructure and the shortage of trained personnel to supervise high-stakes tests.



NTA, which conducts examinations in more than 500 cities, has invited applications from educational institutions and testing service providers across the country to expand its network for both computer-based tests (CBT) and pen-and-paper examinations.

Govt is considering shifting NEET-UG from pen-and-paper mode to CBT.

Under the Nov-7 notification, a standard CBT centre must have at least 285 functional computer workstations per shift, including buffer capacity, while a pen-and-paper centre must be able to accommodate at least 250 candidates. Smaller CBT centres can be considered in locations where testing facilities are limited.

World.title: Confident of trade pact ahead of PM Modi's trip: Canada envoy
World.content:
As India and Canada hold the 6th round of trade negotiations this week, Canada's high commissioner to India Christopher Cooter has said Ottawa is confident of finalising the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) ahead of PM Narendra Modi's visit to Canada next month.

While the agreement will still have to be ratified, the announcement about successful conclusion of the negotiations during Modi's Dec 11-12 visit will mark a milestone in the relationship, capping the dramatic turnaround in India-Canada ties under Canadian PM Mark Carney and Modi in the past 18 months.

"The actual ratification would take some time because we have provincial governments that are involved as well.



But I think we can be pretty confident that the final text will be there," said Cooter in an interaction with TOI editors.

"We're hopeful about our ratification process. The 6th round of talks is coming up. I'm pretty confident that we're getting close, so we'll keep our fingers crossed. We're also looking at some subsidiary agreements that would facilitate business travel," added Cooter. He also said many other big-ticket announcements were expected from the visit including in space.





Cooter also addressed public anxiety over international student policies of Canada, home to roughly 300,000 Indian students.

He clarified that official caps were targeted at fraudulent institutions rather than legitimate Indian applicants.

"People said, 'Oh my God, Canada's not open'. This was a misperception. In fact, the caps are nowhere near being met. This is probably the best time ever, if you're a prospective Indian student.

Of course there were some abuses. There were these fly-by-night colleges. They weren't about education as much as getting PR. So, we've got to clean that up," said Cooter.

Cooter also said the progress witnessed in the ties since Carney assumed office had moved "far beyond a reset". He said the recovery was initially fragile, but gained unprecedented momentum following bilateral engagements between the leaders.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"It's not a reset. It is far beyond a reset. When I arrived here in Sept last year, it was a tentative approach. None of us knew what was going to happen next. Is this going to be a slow march? Are we going to take a step back? Very fragile at the beginning. But it didn't happen that way. When foreign minister Anita Anand was here last month, we called on your PM and he described it as the fastest acceleration in the relationship," said Cooter.

World.title: ‘Madurai Reads’ campaign marks prelude to book festival
World.content:
As a prelude to the upcoming Madurai Book Festival-2026, a reading awareness campaign titled ‘Madurai Reads” was held here on Wednesday..

The event, conducted on the historic Ezhuthanikkara Street on South Masi Street, was presided over by Madurai MP Su. Venkatesan in the presence of Collector Nishanth Krishna and Deputy Mayor T. Nagarajan.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Venkatesan said that Madurai held the unique distinction of transforming the book fair into a massive people’s movement. The main book fair would be held at Tamukkam Grounds from November 13 to November 23, 2026.

Pointing to the cultural significance of launching the preliminary events on Ezhuthanikkara Street, he said: “Just as Sannithi Street is special to spiritual devotees, Ezhuthanikkara Street holds a unique significance for literary enthusiasts.”

He elaborated on the street’s rich history, saying that centuries before the advent of the printing press, literary works were painstakingly hand-copied onto palm-leaf manuscripts by scribes — known as ezhuthanikkarargal —who once inhabited the neighbourhood. Hence, initiating the book fair proceedings from a location with such a distinctive heritage was a matter of immense pride for the nation.

Calling upon the public to ensure that this year’s edition surpassed previous milestones, Mr. Venkatesan urged every family to encourage students and youth to visit the fair. Bringing students to such events was not merely about purchase of books, but about exposing them to a vast literary landscape to cultivate a lifelong reading habit and positive outlook toward literature.

He also acknowledged the vital role of the media in supporting the event, which would feature over 200 publishing houses, and asserted that the district administration had finalised all preparatory arrangements.

World.title: Mississippi elects Democrat Scott Colom as state's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction
World.content:
Democratic nominee Scott Colom has defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's closely contested U.S. Senate race after a prolonged ballot-counting process, giving the state its first Black U.S. senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction.

Mr. Colom's narrow victory is a seismic shift in Mississippi, which has been controlled mostly by white conservatives for generations, and it yielded immediate echoes around the country. The outcome adds to a decisive midterm rebuke of President Donald Trump, whose party suffered defeats in several Republican-controlled states, and it will bolster some Democrats' argument that their future runs through the American South.

The Associated Press called the contest Wednesday (November 11, 2026) in Mr. Colom's favour after local election officials spent several days processing absentee and provisional ballots, called affidavit ballots in Mississippi.

“While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters,” Ms. Hyde-Smith said in a two-minute concession speech posted online. “I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state.”

A spokesman for the Senator said she called Mr. Colom to congratulate him and concede before the video was shared publicly.

The last time Mississippi chose a new Democratic Senator was 1947, and the winner then was a staunch segregationist. Mr. Colom, a 43-year-old local prosecutor, capitalised on the state's large Black population, discontent with the economy and Ms. Hyde-Smith's missteps as she sought a second full term.

“They actually deserve a Senator that will listen to them, that actually cares about what they think, actually cares about what they're going through,” Mr. Colom said in the campaign's closing stretch.

Mr. Colom said during the campaign that he could represent all of Mississippi, a state where racial divisions have long defined its politics and society.

“It's got to be about having a party that represents rural America again, suburban America, urban America — a party that makes sure we actually deliver for voters in ways that make their lives better,” he said.

National Democrats celebrate along with Colom

Party leaders hailed the senator-elect's triumph, with nods to the South's emerging battleground status after other upset victories from North Carolina to Texas.

“Scott Colom is the only person who could've gotten this done,” Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer of New York posted online. “Along with his staff and volunteers, Scott ran the campaign of a lifetime and re-imagined what's possible for Democrats in the South.”

Former President Bill Clinton, a native Arkansan who campaigned with Mr. Colom days before the election, addressed Mr. Colom on social media, saying he won “because you believe in the promise of your state's people. And they believed in you right back. I'm honoured to have stood alongside you.”

A race Washington once viewed as a long shot

Despite Mr. Schumer's support, the contest was a latecomer to the national spotlight, drawing attention from Democrats who belatedly infused cash into Colom's candidacy well after Black senators, including Georgia's Raphael Warnock and Maryland's Angela Alsobrooks, urged donors and party leaders to see the contest as winnable.

The son of a one-time Republican who worked for President Ronald Reagan, Mr. Colom garnered attention for his aggressive campaign as Democrats widened the Senate battleground map and Ms. Hyde-Smith's vulnerabilities crystallised.

Mr. Colom attracted particular notice for some of the year's most widely circulated ads. After Ms. Hyde-Smith, 67, seemed to brush off high beef prices by saying consumers could choose other proteins, Mr. Colom cut a 30-second spot depicting incredulous voters saying they'd “pick another senator instead.”

When Mr. Trump came to Corinth, Mississippi, in late October for a rally with Ms. Hyde-Smith, Mr. Colom walked the line of Mr. Trump supporters as they waited outside the gates. He introduced himself, asked about their concerns and explained his priorities.

Later that evening, when Mr. Trump called Ms. Hyde-Smith to the stage, she said nine words in six seconds: “Is this not the best President in our lifetime?”

Then she stepped away.

“I love that,” Mr. Trump replied when he continued his 80-plus minutes at the microphone. “Sometimes they get up and they talk for 10 minutes.”

The appearance tracked Mr. Colom's tactic of criticising Mr. Trump's policies — especially the Iran war and tariffs that he said were especially hard on Mississippi farmers — without taking personal jabs at the President or people who voted for him. Instead, he consistently put the onus on Ms. Hyde-Smith, framing her as a nonentity in Washington — a critique that resonated in a state that has been accustomed to long-serving senators like Thad Cochran, Trent Lott and John Stennis, who all rose to powerful posts and routed federal money back to Mississippi.

There is some irony in Ms. Hyde-Smith finding herself flat-footed against Mr. Colom. In 2022, then-President Joe Biden nominated Colom to be a U.S. District Court judge in the Northern District of Mississippi. Mississippi's senior Republican Senator Roger Wicker and former Gov. Haley Barbour, who is also a former national Republican chairman, backed the nomination.

Ms. Hyde-Smith, however, blocked Mr. Colom's confirmation under the Senate tradition that members can spike a president's choices for federal judicial positions in their home state.

Mr. Colom said his Senate bid was never about getting even with Ms. Hyde-Smith.

Mr. Colom called on Mississippi's history. The Senator-elect concluded his campaign with an ad that featured him at the Jackson home of Medgar Evers, the civil rights leader who, in 1963, was gunned down in his driveway by a white supremacist and died in front of his family.

“In Mississippi, no one is above the law, and no one should be outside its protection,” Mr. Colom said, telling the story of Evers' military service at Normandy in World War II, his voter registration efforts in Mississippi, his assassination and the three decades it took to win a conviction.

“He was killed for helping Mississippians vote,” Mr. Colom said. “On Tuesday, use your vote and honour everyone who died for that right.”

Black Democrats, including Maryland Sen. Angela Alsobrooks and Georgia Sen. Raphael Warnock, highlighted Colom's bid early. Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer helped Colom raise money, and he drew financial support from other outside players, including Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, a billionaire and potential presidential candidate.

Former President Bill Clinton and former Vice-President Kamala Harris campaigned on Mr. Colom's behalf in the campaign's closing weeks.

Despite Republicans' domination, the path was always there. With the largest share of Black voters of any state, Mississippi's general elections have been closer for years than those of its immediate Southern neighbours. Trump won by double digits in each of his three presidential contests, but in 2023, Republican Governor Tate Reeves managed to win reelection by a margin of just 3 percentage points.

Mr. Colom and other Black party leaders and strategists insisted throughout 2026 that he could narrow the gap with strong Black turnout, Republican voter discontent and an uptick in Democrats' usual share of the white vote in Mississippi.

Results showed strong turnout in the Mississippi Delta and its concentration of majority-Black counties. But nearly all of the state moved leftward from the 2024 election, when Trump carried Mississippi by nearly 23 points.

Then-Governor Phil Bryant first appointed Ms. Hyde-Smith, who was the state agriculture commissioner, to the Senate in 2018 when Cochran resigned. She won a special election runoff in 2018 and a full term in 2020. Both times she defeated Democrat Mike Espy, a former US agriculture secretary who'd also been Mississippi's first Black congressman since Reconstruction.

During the extended vote count, Mr. Colom acknowledged the historic nature of doing what Mr. Espy could not. But he said he sees his place more in terms of other Mississippians, especially the state's youngest residents, than in his individual story.

“My job is to do well enough as the next United States senator that the next time some young black boy or girl has the work ethic, the vision, and the values,” he said, “and they want to be United States Senator, that nobody says because of anything I've done that they shouldn't get a chance.”

World.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
World.content:
Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, are facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Who is Jensen Huang?

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News. He graduated in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and later obtained a master’s degree from Stanford University, according to his Linkedin profile.

Jensen Huang timeline (according to Graphics News)

February 17, 1963: Jensen Huang is born in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher.

1968: His family moves to Thailand before relocating to the United States during the Vietnam War.

1970s: He spends part of his childhood at a boarding school in Kentucky before moving to Oregon, where he develops an interest in computing.

1984: Graduates with a degree in electrical engineering from Oregon State University.

1984-1992: Completes a master’s degree at Stanford University.

1993: Co-founds Nvidia with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. He becomes chief executive officer as the company enters the computer gaming market with an initial capital of $40,000.

1999: Nvidia goes public. The launch of the GeForce 256, promoted as the world’s first GPU, establishes the company as a major force in the technology industry.

2006: Under Mr. Huang’s leadership, Nvidia introduces CUDA technology, enabling graphics processors to handle complex computing tasks beyond gaming and helping lay the groundwork for the AI revolution.

2022: The launch of ChatGPT triggers a sharp rise in demand for advanced AI processors.

2024: The boom in generative AI drives Nvidia’s rapid expansion, with Mr. Huang’s net worth surpassing $100 billion.

Spy scandal timeline

2024-2025: Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are reportedly seen together at several industry events in Taipei.

2026: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio sends a memo warning Trump administration officials about the Nvidia chief executive’s relationship with Alice Huang.

October 29, 2026: The New York Times reports that U.S. authorities investigated Alice Huang over suspicions that she passed intelligence to Beijing and helped circumvent U.S. restrictions on advanced AI chips.

November 5, 2026: Senior U.S. lawmakers seek a closed-door briefing from Jensen Huang over potential national security concerns.

November 8, 2026: Mr. Huang admits he was “unfaithful” to his wife. Nvidia announces an independent investigation into the espionage allegations.

November 9, 2026: Nvidia shares fall by more than 4%. U.S. President Donald Trump says the FBI is investigating the controversy involving Mr. Huang and Alice Huang.

The Jensen-Alice saga

Mr. Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang. The Nvidia chief executive said he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he said in a statement posted on Nvidia’s website.

The New York Times reported that Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen allegedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Mr. Huang.

Mr. Huang also sent a message to Nvidia employees on November 8, 2026, acknowledging the affair and apologising to both his family and company staff. While expressing regret for his actions, he did not address allegations that Alice Huang was a suspected spy.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and alleged that she was providing information directly to Beijing.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on November 8, 2026. Independent directors have engaged external legal counsel to examine the circumstances surrounding the relationship. Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised, and that Mr. Huang would remain in charge while cooperating with the investigation.

World.title: First phase of Musi rejuvenation to begin shortly, says Telangana CM Revath
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Wednesday said the first phase of the Musi rejuvenation project would begin shortly, asserting that the river had to be cleaned up and restored rather than merely beautified. He said the government would ensure that no one suffers losses in the process and called for the cooperation of all political parties.

Speaking at the inauguration of the revived Thammidikunta Lake, he said Musi river pollution was causing hardships to people in Nalgonda district, who were paying the price for the neglect of successive governments. The lives of Hyderabad residents were closely linked to the river, he said.

Recalling the construction of Osmansagar and Himayatsagar reservoirs by the Nizam to protect Hyderabad from floods, he said the Musi riverfront had been developed nearly a century ago, but the water body had now become polluted.

Describing Hyderabad as a city of rocks and lakes, Mr. Revanth Reddy said it had 1,372 lakes, but nearly 50% had disappeared due to various reasons. Encroachments had resulted in waterlogging on roads and flooding of residential colonies during rains. He stressed the need to free lakes from encroachments as part of efforts to protect nature and establish Hyderabad as a global city.

He said Thammidikunta Lake had been expanded from 14 to 30 acres, keeping the future of coming generations in mind, even if some people suffered losses in the process. Actor Akkineni Nagarjuna had voluntarily handed over two acres of land to the government, he said, describing him as a hero in real life as well as in films.

The Chief Minister said the lake would become a new destination alongside Shilparamam and called for developing a lake economy around it. He directed police officials to ensure adequate security and suggested planting a Jammi tree on the lake premises so that lakes could become venues for Dasara celebrations and help preserve cultural traditions.

World.title: Morning Digest: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Huang, say reports; Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng says she has been stopped from visiting India, and more
World.content:
Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: U.S. media

Nvidia's board is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, U.S. media reported Wednesday (November 11, 2026), as the chip giant's chief faces new accusations of infidelity, after revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. The New York Times reported on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) that Mr. Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with a subordinate, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia's vice-president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Nvidia shares have plummeted in recent days since Mr. Huang admitted to the affair.

Trump defends Iran war in Veterans Day address

U.S. President Donald Trump defended the war against Iran on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) at a U.S. Veterans Day commemoration that saw his Defence Secretary publicly admonished for a lack of decorum. “The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible,” Mr. Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington.“When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better place, more peaceful place, and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer.”

Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng says she has been stopped from coming to Hyderabad for Bharat Summit

Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng, who works for the Oslo-based daily newspaper Dagsavisen, has said that she has been stopped from coming to India despite having a valid visa. “I got a visa to India and was supposed to leave this morning to attend the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad. I had been invited as a panellist and speaker on the future of media and press freedom. But «orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa,” she said in a post on X, on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

India simplifies visa norms; categories cut, forms to be 70% leaner

The government has simplified its visa regime by reducing the categories from 13 to nine and making the application forms leaner by up to 70%, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said in a statement on Wednesday (November 11, 2026). The “Tourist Visa” has been renamed “Visitor Visa”, reflecting a broader range of permitted purposes beyond conventional tourism, the Ministry said.

Delhi air pollution: Police stop students’ protest march against worsening air quality near Turkman Gate

Dozens of students and young people took out a protest march against worsening air quality in central Delhi on Wednesday (November 11) evening, but were stopped by the police after covering around 300 to 400 metres from Turkman Gate towards Jantar Mantar.
